home_pitcher_note: The reigning AL Cy Young Award winner will be making his fifth career Opening Day start. He is 14-3 with a 3.48 ERA in 23 career starts against the White Sox, including a 2-0 record and 2.57 ERA in three starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: After having his streak of five straight Opening Day starts snapped last season, Buehrle makes his sixth Game 1 start in the past seven years. He holds a 5-4 record at the newly dubbed Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona shocked the baseball world last year with a 19-8 season in which he had a 3.06 ERA in 32 starts. The only reason he was in the Tribe's rotation the first two months of the year was because Cliff Lee and Jake Westbrook suffered abdominal strains. Now, he's the club's bona fide No. 2 starter and a potential ace in the making.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez signed a three-year, $34.5 million extension prior to last season and then went out and pitched like a staff ace. Vazquez led all White Sox starters in wins, strikeouts and innings pitched (216 2/3). Vazquez's 213 strikeouts ranked as the sixth-best single-season total in franchise history and placed him fourth in the American League.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook turned his 2007 season around in the second half, particularly by going 4-1 with a 1.90 ERA in August. In 25 career starts against the Sox, Westbrook is 8-10 with a 5.06 ERA. He went 1-3 with a 5.70 ERA against them last year.
away_pitcher_note: It was a tale of two halves for the White Sox rookie in 2007. Before the All-Star break, Danks posted a 5-6 record with a manageable 4.62 ERA. Following the Midsummer Classic, Danks finished 1-7 with a 7.11 ERA and allowed 63 hits in 49 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer, who made three starts for the A's late in the 2003 season but was used exclusively in relief during the following four seasons, has transitioned back to the starting role he prefers this spring after recovering from hip surgery that ended his 2007 season in May. Prior to his big league debut in 2003, Duchscherer made 23 starts at Triple-A Sacramento and went 14-2 with a 3.25 ERA to claim Pacific Coast League Pitcher of the Year honors. An All-Star setup man for the A's in 2005, Duchscherer threw mostly cutters out of the bullpen, but he'll be using his full arsenal (two-seamer, four-seamer, curveball, changeup) as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Unfortunately, Byrd's 2007 season will best be remembered for his admitted use of human growth hormone, which he said he used under doctor's supervision to treat a medical condition. MLB hasn't said whether Byrd will face a suspension for that HGH use, so he'll take the ball for the opener of a three-game set at McAfee Coliseum, where he is 1-2 with a 5.26 ERA in five career starts. The veteran Byrd was a 15-game winner in '07, but he'd still like to improve his performance against left-handed hitters. He certainly doesn't have to improve his control after leading the AL with 1.31 walks issued per nine innings pitched last year.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland, 24, was part of the six-player package that Oakland received from the Diamondbacks in the deal that sent ace Dan Haren to Arizona. He entered Spring Training with only 41 games of experience at the big league level.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians will keep Sabathia pitching on his fifth day after his uneven outing on Opening Day start against the White Sox, pushing fifth starter Cliff Lee back a day. Sabathia, though, will get an extra day of rest twice in the month of April because of the off-days built into the Tribe�s schedule. That should ease the burden on his arm after he logged 256 1/3 innings last year. Sabathia always seems to struggle in hometown Oakland. He is 1-3 with a 7.17 ERA in seven starts in McAfee Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton faced the Red Sox in his first two starts of the season and pitched well enough to win in both of them. After tossing five shutout innings in Oakland's opener, he got a couple of tough breaks before being chased with two out during Boston's three-run sixth and didn't factor in the decision. A week later, he held the Red Sox to two runs on seven hits over six innings but got only one run of support on the way to the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Look who?s back. Lee has reclaimed his old spot in the rotation after a truly disastrous 2007 in which he strained his abdominal muscle, struggled upon his return and was demoted to Triple-A Buffalo at the end of July. He came into spring camp in good shape and hungry to win his job back, and he did just that.

home_pitcher_note: In the best of his 34 career starts, Joe Saunders dominated the Twins for eight innings at the Metrodome his last time out, yielding four hits and a walk while striking out four. Putting all four of his pitches where he wanted in any count, he needed only 80 deliveries, 52 for strikes, to get through eight innings. He wanted to finish what would have been his first complete game and first shutout, but Francisco Rodriguez closed for the save. Saunders has won both his career starts against the Indians with a 1.32 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona might have a target on his back after his breakout, 19-win season. But he also still has a devastating sinkerball -- and the latter quality reigned supreme in a victory over the White Sox on a bitterly cold Wednesday night at Progressive Field. With the temperatures in the low 30s, Carmona did his part to chill the Sox bats for seven innings in which he gave up just a run on four hits with four walks and four strikeouts. He induced three double plays and 16 ground-ball outs.

home_pitcher_note: Santana sailed through five innings at the Metrodome, giving up one hit with his 96 mph heater, before running into trouble -- and a high pitch count -- in the sixth. He gave up two runs on three hits in the inning, and that was the end of his day after 102 deliveries. He walked two and struck out three in a highly encouraging debut, given all of his struggles last season on the road. He looked like the Santana who won 16 games in '06, working at a fast tempo and throwing strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook was just about perfect in Spring Training play, not issuing a single run in 18 innings of work. The Indians asked him to be just as perfect in his '08 debut Thursday against the White Sox, and he couldn't deliver. Westbrook turned in a solid outing, but he gave up a pair of solo home runs over 7 1/3 innings, and that was enough for him to get tagged with a loss. Westbrook is 2-5 with a 3.12 ERA in eight career starts against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Moseley, filling in for injured starters John Lackey and Kelvim Escobar, struggled in his start against the Texas Rangers, yielding five earned runs in five innings while taking the loss. The righty will get a chance to redeem himself in Wednesday's matinee series finale against Cleveland, a team against whom he owns twice as many wins (two) as he does against any other club.

Sabathia's struggles in his hometown of Oakland continued Saturday. He lasted just 5 1/3 innings against the A's, surrendering four runs on six hits with four walks and two strikeouts. It was an uphill battle for Sabathia all afternoon, as he struggled to get ahead in the count. He hopes to have better luck in his other "home" at Progressive Field, as the reigning Cy Young Award winner has been slow to get into the flow of the regular season.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton dominated for six innings against the Indians on Sunday at McAfee Coliseum, but once again, he came away with a loss. Blanton, who went 6 2/3 innings, allowing just two runs on seven hits while striking out two, issued four walks in the game, including one with the bases loaded in the seventh. The righty used a heavy fastball and solid breaking pitch to keep the Indians' hitters at bay. In seven career starts against the Jays, Blanton is 4-2 with a 3.12 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona had some rare control problems in his start in Anaheim on Monday, yet he still came out virtually unscathed. In six innings of work, all he allowed was an unearned run on four hits. But he also walked five batters, including three with two outs in the fifth. Carmona is 2-1 with a 5.73 ERA in five career appearances against the A?s, including a 2-1 record and 7.71 ERA in three starts against them last season.
away_pitcher_note: This start originally belonged to right-hander Rich Harden, but he was scratched after being placed on the 15-day disabled list with a mild subscapularis strain in his right shoulder. The leading candidate to take Harden`s place is long reliever Lenny Dinardo. The 28-year-old left-hander made 20 starts for the A`s last season, going 7-8 with a 4.93 ERA. Dinardo has surrendered two runs on four hits while walking one in one third of an inning so far this season.

home_pitcher_note: In his return to the Tribe rotation on April 6 in Oakland, Lee looked much more like the 18-game winner he was in '05 than the demoted disaster he was in '07. Lee was solid for 6 2/3 innings, allowing just an unearned run on four hits with a walk and four strikeouts. He got ahead with his fastball and began working his changeup into the mix more often as the game wore on. If Lee can keep up that type of performance this season, the Indians' rotation looks even more potent and dangerous than previously thought.
away_pitcher_note: Gaudin made his season debut in his last outing against the Blue Jays. The 25-year-old righty started the season in the Minor Leagues rehabbing from offseason hip surgery. The results were mixed in his start against Toronto. Gaudin allowed six runs -- five earned -- on eight hits while striking out three over four innings of work. Not the best of pitching lines but all of the earned-run damage came on home runs to Toronto center fielder Vernon Wells and second baseman Aaron Hill. Without those two mistake pitches that were left up in the zone, Gaudin's night would have gone a lot smoother. Gaudin is 2-1 with a 5.47 ERA in nine career outings against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: After a scoreless Spring Training season, Westbrook has taken his stellar command and efficiency into the regular season. He only has one win to show for it because of a tough-luck, 2-1 loss to the White Sox in his season debut. In his last start against the Angels on Tuesday, he went the distance, giving up three runs on seven hits with no walks and four strikeouts. He needed just 94 pitches to notch the complete-game victory. This will mark Westbrook's first appearance against the Red Sox since Game 7 of the American League Championship Series.
away_pitcher_note: Lester was inconsistent in his last start, giving up five hits and four runs over 5 1/3 innings in a loss to the Tigers. The lefty also walked four and struck out none in that outing. Jacobs Field, the site of this outing, will always mark a special place in Lester's heart. That is where he made his comeback from cancer last July 23 and pitched the Red Sox to victory. Lester has 10 walks and seven strikeouts in 16 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd has really struggled in the early going of ?08. His pitches have not been sharp, and the results speak for themselves. In two starts against the A?s and Angels, Byrd has given up 11 runs (nine earned) on 13 hits with four walks in just 7 1/3 innings. He lasted only three innings against the Angels on Wednesday, giving up three home runs, including a grand slam. Byrd won 15 games last season, in large part because of his propensity to work ahead, but he?s often been behind in the count this year.
away_pitcher_note: Wakefield battled through his last start against the Tigers, despite not having his usual command. In fact, the knuckleballer wound up pitching well enough to win, giving up three hits and one earned run over five innings while throwing 108 pitches. He walked five and struck out five. Wakefield is 9-8 with a 4.50 ERA in 23 career appearances against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: In a big contract season, the 2007 Cy Young Award winner has endured one of his career's toughest stretches to open the season. Struggling greatly with his command, Sabathia has yet to win, pitching poorly in each of his three starts. Whether the pressure is getting to Sabathia cannot be said so early, but his 3 2/3 innings Friday against the A's was his shortest stint in nearly two years. Lifetime against the Tigers, Sabathia is 13-8 with a 4.30 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga will be recalled from Triple-A Toledo to make his second Major League start. He'll take the place of Dontrelle Willis, who went on the 15-day disabled list with a hyperextended right knee. The 26-year-old Venezuelan, won each of his first two starts this season at Triple-A Toledo, allowing three runs on seven hits over 12 innings with 11 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona followed up a pair of outstanding starts with a startlingly wild loss against Oakland Saturday night. Blaming faulty mechanics, Carmona walked a career-high eight hitters while allowing three runs over just 3 1/3 innings. No Cleveland starter in 15 years had walked as many hitters in a game. Carmona says his arm was getting away from his body, which led to an inconsistent delivery. The team hopes the 24-year-old right-hander will be able to correct his delivery during his bullpen session between starts. In eight career outings against Detroit, Carmona is 3-2 with a 3.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This was not where Verlander expected his stats to be three starts into this season, but to some extent, he has pitched better than his record. He allowed a run on two hits over his first seven innings last Saturday at the White Sox before he lost his command in the eighth inning. He ended up being charged with six runs over 7 2/3 innings as his winless streak stretched to three starts, the second-longest of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano'’s return to the Major Leagues following a 19-month layoff due to Tommy John surgery wasn'’t quite as impressive as the Twins had hoped. In bitter cold conditions in Kansas City, Liriano gave up four runs on six hits over 4 2/3 innings. Walks were the big trouble point for the left-hander as he issued five while struggling to find his command. His next start will be in the warm conditions of the Metrodome, where he faces the Indians. Liriano is 1-1 with a 3.29 ERA in four career starts against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Lee tossed his second straight outstanding start in a victory over the A's Sunday in Cleveland. Continuing to stash aside a disappointing 2007, Lee was as good as he's been in perhaps two years. Lee found himself ahead of almost every hitter, relying virtually solely on a precisely commanded fastball before mixing in a few more off-speed pitches to keep the A's guessing late. In all, Lee allowed only one run on two hits while striking out eight over eight innings. Save for a back-to-back hits in the fourth inning, Lee was perfect. He retired all 23 other hitters he faced. Lee attributes the strong start to a healthy Spring Training, which he missed last year and says contributed to his disastrous 2007 season.

home_pitcher_note: After shutting down two potent offenses in the Angels and the White Sox, Blackburn appeared well on his way to doing the same against the Tigers in his most recent start. But in his final inning of work, the right-hander gave up four runs on four hits. Blackburn is now set to face the Indians at the Metrodome. Last season, Blackburn pitched twice in relief against Cleveland and gave up two runs over his four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook continued his solid '08 season with a quality start -- albeit a no-decision -- against the Red Sox on Monday. He went 6 1/3 innings, allowing just two runs (one earned) on seven hits with three walks and five strikeouts. While he got ahead and got some big ground-ball outs with his trusty sinker, he also had a nasty slider working. Westbrook is 7-8 with a 3.61 ERA in his career against the Twins and 1-6 with a 4.61 ERA in nine career appearances at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander found a bit of trouble late in his last outing getting pitches up in the zone. It led to Baker giving up three home runs to the Tigers, although all were solo shots. Baker said that he's been working better out of his stretch than his windup. It's something he will try to work on during his bullpen session this week. The hope is that he can make more pitches down in the zone from his windup and limit the number of mistakes to another difficult lineup -- the Indians. Baker was 1-1 with a 2.80 ERA in two starts against Cleveland in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd shook off the struggles of his first two starts of the season with a solid outing against the Red Sox on Tuesday. In six innings of work, all he allowed was an unearned run on six hits with no walks and six strikeouts. The fact that he didn't walk anybody was the most encouraging stat. Byrd had endured some uncharacteristic control problems against the A's and Angels, so he was happy to get back to form in this no-decision effort. Byrd is an impressive 6-1 with a 2.11 ERA in nine career starts at the Metrodome, which can be a difficult ballpark for contact pitchers like him.

home_pitcher_note: Meche finally got his first victory, beating the Angels, 3-2, in his fourth start on Wednesday night. Although not at his best, he was better than in his previous outing. This time he limited the tough Angels lineup to two runs in six innings. Manager Trey Hillman thought that Meche was fighting himself a bit, and Meche admitted that he was pitching angry too often. With his first win in hand, Meche feels he can revert back to his old, more relaxed approach and enjoy himself as he did last season. At least that's his plan.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia's velocity is intact, which doesn't lead one to believe his career-high innings total from '07 has caught up to him. But his lack of command in his first four starts of '08 has been downright shocking. It's been particularly damaging in his last two outings. He allowed nine runs in 3 1/3 innings against the A's on April 11, and another nine runs in just four-plus innings against the Tigers on Wednesday. Sabathia has walked 14 batters in just 18 innings of work this season. He only walked 37 batters in 241 innings last season.

home_pitcher_note: Tomko liked the way he threw last Thursday night against the Angels. Well, except for that hanging change-up curve that Garret Anderson belted for a three-run double. He went seven innings, his longest outing of the season, and gave up five runs. Yet Tomko believed his pitching was better than in his previous outing when the Twins got just two runs in six innings. Tomko has been throwing strikes and has walked just four in 20 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona shook off the control problems that plagued him in his first three starts of the season to turn in an impressive outing against the Tigers' potent lineup on Thursday. He limited Detroit to a run on seven hits with a walk and two strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings. Carmona's mechanics had been out of whack in his first three starts of the season, particularly in an eight-walk outing against the A's on April 12. But he seemed to have things back in check this time out.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister felt sluggish from the get-go on Friday night at Oakland and it wasn't a performance up to his previous 2008 standards. He absorbed his first loss. Bannister pitched five-plus innings and finally was ousted by four straight hits in the sixth inning. His stuff wasn't quite as sharp and he used up 86 pitches, just 54 of them strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Cliff Lee just keeps getting better and better with each outing. On Friday against the Twins, he pitched eight scoreless innings of two-hit ball to earn his third victory of the season. Lee struck out eight Minnesota batters and walked just one, throwing 109 pitches. Lee confused Twins hitters all night and lowered his ERA to 0.40.

home_pitcher_note: After two especially rough starts to open the year, Byrd has regained his command of the strike zone and come on strong in recent weeks. He has given up just one earned run over his last two starts. That run came on a Brendan Harris homer in Byrd's outing against the Twins on Sunday, and it cost him a decision. Still, he gave up just that homer and five other hits, walking none and striking out three in seven innings. The Indians kept Byrd on another tight pitch count, as he threw just 43 pitches in his second start of the season against the Angels on April 9.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte again filled the role of stopper for the Yankees on Sunday, retiring the first 14 batters and needing only 89 pitches to blank the Orioles for seven innings and end New York's four-game losing streak. Satisfied that his velocity and command are finally coming around, the Yankees used an off-day Monday to insert Pettitte between Phil Hughes and Ian Kennedy in hopes of saving the bullpen. Pettitte beat the White Sox in his only start against them last year, but is 3-7 with a 6.83 ERA lifetime at U.S. Cellular Field.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers gets the starting nod Saturday as the Indians fill the rotation spot vacated by the injured Jake Westbrook. Sowers is 0-2, but with a 3.18 ERA in four starts at Triple-A Buffalo. Sowers opened the '07 season in the rotation before a demotion to Buffalo.
away_pitcher_note: The tough times are continuing for Kennedy, who is winless in his first four starts and suffered a loss last Saturday at Baltimore, lasting just 2 2/3 innings and needing 86 pitches to get through that four-run, five-walk showing. The Yankees want Kennedy to challenge hitters more and trust his stuff; a control pitcher, he has already walked 13 in 14 innings this season, well above his previous ratio at any professional level. Kennedy has never faced the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia was knocked around in his first four starts of the season because he struggled to command his fastball and he couldn't establish his cutter, especially against right-handed hitters. Virtually all of his problems went by the wayside when he pitched six scoreless innings against the Royals on Tuesday night. Sabathia allowed just four hits with two walks. He struck out 11 batters, looking very much like the Cy Young Award winner he was in '07. It all starts with the fastball. If Sabathia can command that pitch, he can work his secondary stuff off it and be his old, dominant self.
away_pitcher_note: Wang didn't have his best stuff early on Tuesday at Chicago, but he gritted through and found a way, turning to his changeup and splitter to limit the White Sox to three runs on 10 hits over 6 1/3 innings. The victory, in Wang's 85th career start, made him the fastest Major Leaguer to record 50 wins as a starter since the Mets' Dwight Gooden, who won his 50th game in his 82nd start on June 29, 1986, at Chicago. Wang will be facing the Indians for the first time since his dreadful 2007 AL Division Series, when he suffered a pair of losses. In the regular season, Wang is 0-1 with a 8.44 ERA in his only career start at what is now known as Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Because of Thursday's doubleheader with the Royals, the Indians need a spot starter for this game, and the 23-year-old Laffey will get the call. Laffey filled in admirably in the last two months of '07, after Cliff Lee was demoted to Buffalo. He went 4-2 with a 4.56 ERA in nine starts, and he pitched 4 2/3 scoreless innings against the Red Sox in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series. In his first four starts at Buffalo, the 23-year-old Laffey was 3-1 with a 3.13 ERA, striking out 20 and walking six in 26 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Mussina had his best outing of the young season on Wednesday in Chicago, limiting the White Sox to a pair of solo homers over seven innings. Mussina shied away from his curveball and induced ground balls with his two-seam fastball, passing Bob Gibson for sole possession of 42nd place on baseball's all-time wins list with 252. Mussina is 4-3 with a 5.88 ERA in 10 career starts at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona's control, an issue in his first few starts of the season, was again a bit out of whack in his start against the Royals on Thursday. After sitting for a week because of an off day and a rained-out game, Carmona wasn't at his sharpest. He allowed four runs on nine hits with four walks and one strikeout in five innings. Still, he was able to pick up his third win. Carmona was 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA in one start against the Mariners last season.
away_pitcher_note: Tightness in his right thigh spoiled Silva's 29th birthday as it prevented him from having a chance of improving his record to 4-0 in his last start. He shrugged off the ailment afterward, saying he would definitely be good to go in his next start, which would be the game that begins a three-game series against the Tribe. Of the 84 pitches he threw against the Orioles, 51 of them were strikes. That's the name of the game for the veteran right-hander, who was stopped short of pitching into the seventh inning for the fifth straight time this season.

home_pitcher_note: In his strongest start of an already impressive season, Lee held the Royals to a mere three hits in the first complete-game shutout of his career on Thursday. He walked none and struck out nine. Lee continues to pound the zone early in the count with his fastball, and his command of that pitch has been precise in each of his four starts. He's been able to successfully work in his secondary stuff as well, but his fastball has led the way. Lee is 5-1 with a 3.83 ERA in nine career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander continues to pile up the pitches, throwing 97 over five innings in his most recent start. It was the first time in five starts he didn't reach the 100-pitch mark, but the second time he has been lifted after five innings. He has logged six innings twice and seven innings once. Washburn has a career record of 7-6 against the Indians, most of his success coming in Cleveland, where he is 6-2 with a 3.31 ERA in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd is known for his fly-ball-inducing tendencies, but he had trouble keeping those fly balls in the park in his last outing against the Yankees on Friday. In 5 2/3 innings, he gave up four runs on six hits with no walks and no strikeouts. All the runs he allowed came on three homers. In fact, Byrd has now given up seven homers in 26 innings of work this season. Byrd is 6-3 with a 3.38 ERA in 10 career starts against the Mariners, but he was 0-1 with a 9.58 ERA in two starts against them last year.
away_pitcher_note: The 37-year-old right-hander had his fourth start of the season come to a screeching halt barely after it got started. He lasted just one-plus innings against the Athletics before a mild groin strain sent him to the trainer's room. He threw 47 pitches and only 21 of them were strikes, a total flip-flop from the game he pitched against the Angels five days earlier, when he tossed 7 2/3 scoreless innings. Batista has an 0-3 career record against the Indians, all three losses coming in Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia has firmly established that his early April issues are behind him. He has regained command and control of his fastball and cutter and is back to establishing himself on the inside part of the plate, against both right-handers and lefties. But Sabathia still couldn?t come through with a victory Sunday. He held the potent Yankees lineup to a mere run on four hits in eight innings, but the solo shot he allowed to Melky Cabrera was his undoing, because of a lack of offensive support. Still, Sabathia?s last two starts have proven he is back to his Cy Young form of ?07.
away_pitcher_note: It's really been this simple for Hochevar in his first two starts: Use the slider and be successful. In his first game, manager Trey Hillman said he started to get away from using it, and the Oakland Athletics had a big inning. Against the Blue Jays last Saturday, Hochevar stuck with the sinker. He recorded 11 groundouts and three strikeouts in six innings and picked up his first Major League victory. Hochevar also worked his way out several situations when Toronto had a runner in scoring position.

home_pitcher_note: Laffey is officially in the Tribe's rotation, filling in for the injured Jake Westbrook. For five innings in his first start back in the big leagues on Monday, the 23-year-old Laffey looked worthy of a full-time job. He consistently worked ahead, held the potent Yankees hitless and retired 14 in a row at one point. His outing unraveled in the sixth, though, as he served up three straight singles and hit a batter with the bases loaded. In all, Laffey was charged with four runs on three hits with a walk, a strikeout and two hit batters in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Meche pitched decently in his last start, but he still isn't pitching as well as the Royals hoped after his breakout season last year. He lasted 6 2/3 innings in a loss to Toronto and gave up three runs on nine hits. Meche threw 129 pitches in the game. He started his windup differently by moving his hands to waist-level at the beginning of his windup. That start came after one of his worse outings as a Royal against Cleveland, when he gave up eight runs in a 15-1 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte got off to a strong start, winning three of his first four starts. But he has struggled a bit in his last two outings. Over those two starts, losses to Cleveland and Detroit, the veteran has given up nine earned runs on 15 hits and four home runs. Pettitte hasn't pitched particularly well against Cleveland at Yankee Stadium. He is 1-4 against them in the Bronx with a 5.48 ERA in seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona was effective in his last outing against the Mariners on Tuesday, but he was hardly efficient. He needed 103 pitches to get through 6 2/3 innings of work in which he allowed two runs (one earned) on eight hits with four walks and two strikeouts. He worked himself out of some jams to avoid disaster, getting two double-play balls. Carmona is 0-0 with a 3.24 ERA in three career appearances at Yankee Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Wang will be facing Cleveland for the fifth time in his career. He�s 3-1 against the Tribe after being on the top end of a 1-0 victory in Cleveland on April 27. Wang improved to 6-0 with a win over Seattle on Friday night.
away_pitcher_note: The dilemma that comes with being Cliff Lee these days is that allowing any runs at all can be viewed as a disappointment. Lee could toss a complete game against the Yanks, allow just one run and his road ERA will still receive a noticeable rise. The next road run Lee allows will be the first this season, and he?s already made three road starts. His stretch of 27 straight scoreless innings overall came to an end Wednesday night at home against the Mariners, when he allowed three runs on eight hits with no walks and three strikeouts in six-plus innings. But it was still another strong outing from the resurrected Lee.

home_pitcher_note: Mussina will be in quest of his fourth straight victory when he takes the mound on the final day of this homestand. He beat the Tribe in Cleveland on Saturday, working five innings and giving up two runs on seven hits. Mussina, who is 12-9 lifetime against Cleveland, has been a master of control to date this season yielding just five walks in 38 1/3 innings. His last start, his seventh, was the first in which he didn't give up a home run.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd was magnificent against the Mariners in his last start on May 1. He held them scoreless on just four hits with a walk and four strikeouts in 7 2/3 innings. Byrd has really turned his season around after two brutal starts to open it. He has a 1.71 ERA over his last four starts, but only one win and three no-decisions to show for it because of shaky support. Byrd is 0-2 with a 3.46 ERA in four career regular-season starts in Yankee Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Skirting trouble through six scoreless innings, Sabathia unraveled in the seventh inning against the Royals on May 3. In the end, Sabathia allowed four runs on 10 hits while striking out four over 6 1/3 innings. It was Sabathia's third straight solid start, putting firmly to rest any questions that stemmed from his disappointing start. Despite his disappointment in the way his start ended, he said he has confidence again in commanding all of his pitches. And he was encouraged by his ability to make pitches when it mattered most to get out of several early jams.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday, Halladay fell short of his bid to become the first pitcher since 1999 to turn in five consecutive complete games, but the right-hander still walked away with an impressive win over the White Sox. Over 7 1/3 innings, Halladay allowed three runs (one earned) on three hits with seven strikeouts and no walks. He retired the side in order in six innings and induced nine outs via ground ball. Halladay is 5-0 with a 3.77 ERA lifetime against the Indians and is 1-0 with a 3.44 ERA in three career starts at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Laffey continues to look the part of a full-time big leaguer. In his second start filling in for injured starter Jake Westbrook, Laffey was solid once again. No-hitting the Royals through 4 2/3 innings after doing the same to the Yankees his start before, Laffey allowed no earned runs on four hits while striking out five over seven innings. He worked ahead of nearly every hitter, throwing 20 of 28 first-pitch strikes. And after commanding his fastball and baffling Kansas City's left-handed bats with his slider inside, Laffey said he has more confidence than ever in his ability to pitch in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: On Monday night, McGowan stifled the White Sox for 7 1/3 shutout innings en route to his second win of the season. The right-hander struck out six, scattered four hits and induced 11 outs via the ground ball in the win. Over his past two starts, McGowan has posted a .061 ERA with one earned run allowed over 14 2/3 innings, in which he's fanned 11 and walked one. He's only received 16 runs of support, including two over his past two outings, in seven starts this season. McGowan is 0-1 with an 8.10 ERA in two career games against Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona's troubles with command and efficiency this season continued in his start against the Yankees on Tuesday. Carmona allowed three runs on six hits with five walks and two strikeouts. He only lasted five innings, as his pitch count was run up to 95 because of his trouble finding the strike zone. Carmona has made one previous start against the Blue Jays -- it came last year when he allowed three earned runs over 5 1/3 innings of work in a victory.
away_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Burnett struck out a season-high 10 batters, marking the most strikeouts in a game for a Jays starter this year, but the right-hander still picked up a loss against the Rays. Burnett allowed five runs on nine hits with one walk and a wild pitch over six innings. It was the first time in 10 games that Toronto's pitching staff allowed more than three runs and it was the shortest outing by a starter since April 24. Burnett is 1-3 with an 8.46 ERA in four career games against Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: Lee's sizzling start to the season reached an important litmus test against the Yankees on Wednesday night in the Bronx, and he passed with flying colors. Lee went seven scoreless innings, allowing six hits with no walks and seven strikeouts. He extended his streak of consecutive innings without a walk to 28 and held an opponent scoreless for the third time this season. Opponents are batting just .163 (25-for-153) off Lee, who is the first Indians pitcher to win his first six starts since Greg Swindell did so in 1988.
away_pitcher_note: On Wednesday, Marcum limited the Rays to no runs on one hit through eight innings before surrendering two runs on a trio of hits in the ninth. The right-hander still picked up the win, finished with two runs allowed on four hits with nine strikeouts and one walk over 8 2/3 innings. Over his last two starts, Marcum -- Toronto's leader with 44 strikeouts through seven outings -- has fanned 18 batters over 15 1/3 innings. Marcum is 0-2 with a 6.48 ERA in five career games against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd has had an up and down season, because he can't seem to consistently keep the ball in the park. He has been hammered for 10 home runs in the early going, including the three he served up in a loss to the Yankees in his last start on May 8. In that game, he had trouble getting the ball down and away, and he was burned for five runs on eight hits with no walks or strikeouts in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Duchscherer tossed a career-high-tying seven innings against the Orioles in his fourth start of the season and ninth of his career. The former setup man proved he belongs in the starting rotation, throwing seven effective innings while using only 85 pitches (56 for strikes) to limit Baltimore to two runs on four hits and two walks while striking out four. Duchscherer faced Cleveland just once last year, pitching a scoreless inning in a relief appearance. In his career, he is 0-2 with a 6.48 ERA against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: In a duel of Cy Young winners on Friday, Sabathia looked the part of a past winner. He displayed dominating stuff, dazzling Toronto with power and finesse. Sabathia was as sharp in his outing at Progressive Field as he's been at any other time this season. He fanned nine in beating Blue Jays ace Roy Halladay. In his next start, Sabathia will be taking on an Oakland team that has proved troublesome. During his Major League career, he's posted un-Cy Young-like numbers against the A's. He's 2-6 with an ERA over 6.00.
away_pitcher_note: In his Major League-leading ninth start of the season, Blanton threw for 5 2/3 innings, scattering eight hits and three walks while allowing two runs and striking out three in a no-decision en route to the A's 10th-inning 6-5 win over the Orioles. It marked the fourth time of the year the pitcher allowed two runs or fewer. The right-hander compiled a 1-1 record with a 4.26 ERA against Cleveland last year, allowing nine runs on 21 hits -- three of them home runs -- while striking out 12 through 19 innings in three games vs. the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: If Laffey is trying to prove he belongs in the bigs for the long haul, he just needs to keep pitching as he has. Since returning to the Major Leagues to fill Jake Westbrook's spot, Laffey has been downright impressive. His latest outing might rank as his best ever. He threw strikes, pitched ahead in the count, went seven innings and gave up six hits in shutting out the Blue Jays. His performance, if it continues, will present a pleasant problem for manager Eric Wedge once Westbrook is ready to come off the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Smith, a rookie left-hander, lost his last start to Texas, but the A's are still 5-2 in his starts. He has gone at least six innings in six of his seven starts. The 24-year-old Smith can't get frustrated by a lack of run support; the A's have not scored a run for him in his last three starts. Smith's other concern is the first inning. He has allowed eight runs in the opening frame.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto was roughed up six runs and eight hits, including five extra-base hits, over 4 2/3 innings during the Reds' 8-3 loss to the Mets at Shea Stadium. The 22-year-old rookie had decent velocity but located his pitches to the very hittable middle portion of the plate and got pummeled.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians have not announced it, but the rainout Sunday and doubleheader Monday puts the rotation in a pinch, which means an extra arm will be needed. Sowers looks to be the choice. He's looked good in Triple-A Buffalo, and his one outing he had in the bigs went well, too. Whatever his problems were last season seem to have sorted themselves out. He's throwing with more confidence and with more velocity.

home_pitcher_note: The run support finally came for Harang during an 8-7 win over the Marlins on Monday which snapped a five-game winless streak. Harang allowed four earned runs on seven hits with two walks and four strikeouts. He survived three early homers that put him into a 3-0 deficit. At one point, he retired 15 of 16 batters.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona turned in a gem of an outing against the Blue Jays on Monday. He notched the third complete game and the second shutout of his career by holding the Jays to five hits and four walks with three strikeouts. The walks are still an issue for Carmona, who has issued 35 free passes in 48 2/3 innings of work this season. But in this outing, he negated the threat of the runners by consistently getting the timely ground ball with his two-seamer.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez pitched six innings and allowed one earned run on seven hits with two walks and five strikeouts during a 5-3 win over the Marlins on Tuesday. With a 1.12 ERA, the 24-year-old right-hander has yet to give up more than one earned run over his first eight starts for Cincinnati. No one in MLB has done that since Mike Norris did it for the Oakland A's in 1980.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the Blue Jays on Monday, Lee did his part in his bid to become the first Indians pitcher in 86 years to win his first seven starts of a season. But Lee didn't get any offensive support, so his nine scoreless innings, in which he allowed just seven hits with two walks and five strikeouts, went to waste. This was another remarkable outing for the resurgent Lee, who continues to stymie the opposition with sharp command of his low-90s fastball. He has not allowed a run in his last 16 innings. Lee is 3-1 with a 5.60 ERA in five career starts against the Reds and 2-1 with a 4.08 ERA in three starts at Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: It was another strong outing for Contreras, as he helped the White Sox end their three-game, West Coast losing streak with a 6-1 victory over the Angels on Wednesday. Contreras allowed one run on four hits over seven innings, striking out three and walking three in picking up his third win in four decisions. Contreras has yielded a mere two earned runs over his past 14 innings pitched. Contreras has yet to face Cleveland during the 2008 season, but he has a 4-2 career mark against the Indians with a 3.30 ERA. He also holds a 1-2 mark with a 4.12 ERA at U.S. Cellular Field over three starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: All worry about Sabathia following his dismal four-start stretch to open the season has dissipated. He has gone 3-2 with a 1.49 ERA (36 1/3 innings pitched, six earned runs allowed) over his last five starts, lowering his ERA from 13.50 to 5.47. The key has been his regained confidence in his cutter, particularly against right-handed hitters. Sabathia worked a complete-game shutout against the A's on Wednesday, allowing just five hits with two walks and tying a season-high with 11 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez finished with a tough no-decision during Thursday night's series finale in Anaheim, despite the White Sox emerging with a 4-3 victory. Vazquez allowed two earned runs over 6 2/3 innings, striking out six and not issuing a walk, but it was an unearned run produced by a Joe Crede fielding error that removed the right-hander as the pitcher of record. As of the start of the weekend, Vazquez led the American League with 58 strikeouts. Vazquez is 0-1 in his only start against the Indians this season.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd has had trouble keeping the ball in the yard this season, but he rebounded from a three-homer loss against the Yankees with a tremendous outing against the A's on May 13. Byrd went 7 1/3 scoreless innings, allowing just five hits with no walks and seven strikeouts. He had a lot of help from his defense, but he didn't let the A's burn him with any dingers, either. Byrd is 8-2 with a 4.22 ERA in 13 career starts against the White Sox and 4-0 with a 3.67 ERA in five starts at U.S. Cellular Field.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle's stretch of six starts without a victory came to a close Saturday night in San Francisco, as the southpaw allowed just one run on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings and won for the first time since April 6. Buehrle walked three and struck out one, while also picking up his first hit since 2003. Buehrle lasted just 1 2/3 innings on Opening Day during his only other start this season against the Indians, giving up seven earned runs on seven hits. He did not factor in that decision and has an 8-11 record with a 4.93 lifetime against Cleveland. It's his only career losing record and plus-4.00 ERA against American League Central opponents.
away_pitcher_note: When he was called back up to the bigs in late April, 23-year-old Laffey was viewed as a temporary replacement for the injured Jake Westbrook. But with four sparkling starts the past month, Laffey has proven this is where he belongs and left the higher-ups with some tough decisions. He'll make at least one more start, and he'll look to build off an impressive outing against the A's, in which he allowed just one unearned run on five hits with a walk and six strikeouts in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona was stellar again on Saturday, working 7 1/3 innings and allowing one run on four hits with four strikeouts and, perhaps most impressively, no walks in a 4-2 loss to the Reds. Prior to Saturday, he had issued 35 walks in 48 2/3 innings. Carmona said the game was the best he's felt all season, as all but three of Carmona's outs in the game came on the ground. In nine career games against the Rangers, Carmona is 4-1 with a 2.25 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gabbard took his first loss of the season in a 5-4 loss to Houston on Sunday, allowing five runs in five innings. It was the first time he has allowed more than three earned runs in seven starts this season. The Rangers are 5-2 when Gabbard starts. He has induced 57 ground-ball outs, an average of eight per start. But he struggled with getting the ball up in the strike zone against the Astros. Gabbard is 0-1 with a 6.97 ERA in two games against Cleveland, both at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Lee pitched well early on, but struggled at times with his location as the game progressed in his last start -- a 6-4 loss at Cincinnati on Sunday. He posted season-worst marks in innings pitched (5 2/3), runs allowed (six total, five earned), hits allowed (10) and strikeouts (two) in earning his first loss of the season. Lee held a Major League-best 0.67 ERA heading into the game only to have it jump to 1.37. Brandon Phillips' RBI groundout in the first inning snapped Lee's 16 consecutive scoreless inning streak. Lee is 3-2 with a 6.52 ERA lifetime in five games against the Rangers. He faced them once last year when he went 6 2/3 innings and gave up seven earned runs in a losing effort.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman is 1-1 with a 3.45 ERA in five starts. He has pitched at least six innings in all five starts, and the first four were quality starts. That streak was broken when he gave up five runs in six innings in his last start against the Twins on Monday. He has made five career relief appearances against the Indians, and has a 1.42 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the White Sox on Tuesday, Sabathia was saddled with a loss he didn't deserve for the second time this season. In seven strong innings of work, Sabathia allowed just two runs on seven hits with eight strikeouts. The runs came on two solo homers. A lack of offensive support did Sabathia in. Still, he has continued to distance himself from those rough four starts to open the season. Sabathia is 2-2 with a 2.15 ERA in four May starts.
away_pitcher_note: Mathis pitched a scoreless inning each in three relief appearances before making his first Major League start on Tuesday against the Twins. He allowed nine runs, six earned, in 2 1/3 innings in an 11-4 loss. He is filling in for Kevin Millwood, who could be close to returning when this spot in the rotation comes around again. Mathis was 5-0 with a 3.55 ERA in seven games for Triple-A Oklahoma before being called up on May 11.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd simply can't seem to get a consistent run of quality outings going this season. He was at his best when working 7 1/3 scoreless innings against the A's on May 13, but he followed that up by giving up five runs on five hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Sox on Wednesday. In the outing against the Sox, all the runs came in the sixth, after Byrd had worked five seamless innings in which he allowed just one hit. He's had trouble keeping the ball in the yard this season, serving up a team-high 11 homers.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez has all but assumed the ace status of the White Sox rotation. The hard-throwing righty has made 10 starts this season, seven of which have been quality starts. He was dominant in his last outing against the Indians, going seven strong innings, allowing four hits and two runs. He struck out seven batters to tie him with Cleveland's C.C. Sabathia for the league lead. He's walked only 12 batters against 65 strikeouts on the year, by far the best ratio in the Sox rotation this season.

home_pitcher_note: Laffey has been filling in for an injured Jake Westbrook (who will rejoin the rotation Wednesday), and Laffey will remain in the rotation now that Fausto Carmona is out for a month. Laffey has filled in quite well. Facing the Sox on Thursday in Chicago, Laffey allowed just two runs on six hits with a walk and six strikeouts in seven-plus innings. He was done in by a lack of offensive support and absorbed the loss. Laffey likes to work quick, and his efficiency has been a plus for the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle has looked better in recent starts, allowing only one run in each of his last two. He picked up a no-decision against Cleveland on Thursday, pitching seven strong innings and allowing just two hits. It was a much-improved performance than his first outing against the Indians, who banged him up for seven runs on Opening Day. Buehrle said pitching coach Don Cooper found a flaw in his motion from the stretch Thursday that was causing him to leave the ball up to hitters, which may be the cause for his high walk numbers in his last few starts.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook will make his return to the rotation after missing more than a month with a strained left intercostal muscle. Before the injury, Westbrook was off to a strong start to the season. Each of his first four starts were quality starts, and opponents were batting just .255 off him. Westbrook faced the White Sox on April 3 and held them to a pair of runs on six hits over 7 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd overcame a rocky fifth inning against the Angels on Friday to pick up his second career complete game, the first being a five-inning, rain-shortened 2-0 win over the Mets in 2006. Despite picking up the loss, Floyd pitched well, allowing three hits and four walks. He hit back-to-back batters in the fifth with the bases loaded, and those runs turned out to be the difference in the 3-1 defeat. This will be Floyd's second career start against Cleveland, the first coming on Sept. 10, 2007. Floyd pitched well in that game, but once again picked up the loss. He allowed just two earned runs in 6 1/3 innings and surrendered five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Meche pitched well despite suffering a loss against Toronto in his last start. He allowed just two runs on five hits over six innings, walking two and striking out five. Meche did struggle with his location, however, needing 115 pitches to get through his six innings. The right-hander is 3-7 with a 5.54 ERA in 14 career starts against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Lee hasn't been quite as sharp his last two starts, giving up eight runs on 17 hits with five walks over 12 1/3 innings against the Reds and Rangers. But in the outing against the Rangers on Saturday, he did a nice job of recovering after looking shaky in the first and second innings. He never found his breaking ball, but he found command of his fastball. Command of that fastball has been the key to Lee's splendid '08. He'll look to keep it going against a Royals team he limited to three hits in nine shutout innings at Kauffman Stadium on April 24.

home_pitcher_note: Davies is being recalled from Triple-A Omaha to step into the rotation. He replaces Brett Tomko, who was re-assigned to the bullpen. Davies, acquired in a trade from the Braves last July 31, made 11 starts after joining the Royals and was 3-7 with a 6.66 ERA. He failed to make the club during Spring Training but did well for Omaha, going 6-2 with a 2.06 ERA. For Davies to be effective, he has to command his fastball, a problem in his past. Last year he was 0-3 with a 12.27 ERA against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Not much more Sabathia can do to earn a win than what he did in his last outing against the Rangers. If anyone doubted that Sabathia's early season struggles were behind him, all they had to do was dissect his latest performance. He was masterful in stopping cold one of the best offenses in the game. In doing so, he displayed the kind of high-grade stuff that earned him the Cy Young Award a season ago. He pitched ahead in the count, a requirement in beating a good-hitting team. In his last four outings, Sabathia is 2-1 with a 1.20 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Trying to halt the Royals� losing streak last Tuesday night, Bannister went against his usual form against the Twins. Where he typically throws to contact and gives up a lot of fly balls, he was extremely aggressive with low pitches. As a result, he got 10 groundouts and three strikeouts in his five innings and didn't give up any homers or extra-base hits. Bannister also made 111 pitches in that short span, but he was pleased with his effort. He got no decision as the Royals lost in the 12th inning. Bannister faced the Indians on April 24 and pitched well, but lost, 2-0.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd was knocked around for 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings against the White Sox on May 26, but to his credit, he limited the damage to three runs in his fourth no-decision of the season. One ugly trend that has followed the fly-ball-inducing Byrd around this season is his penchant for dishing out the long ball. He has now given up 12 of them on the year, and that's significantly affected him in the won-loss ledger. Byrd is 1-4 with a 5.20 ERA in his career against the Royals, including an 0-1 record and 6.00 ERA in one start last year.

home_pitcher_note: In just two starts this season, Mathis has had a case of the Jekyll and Hydes. In his first start, on May 20 at Minnesota, he coughed up nine runs (six earned), which were his first runs allowed of the season, in just 2 1/3 innings, on eight hits and four walks. Mathis rebounded nicely though in his last start on May 25 at Cleveland, holding the Indians to just one run on seven hits and three walks in six innings. Mathis has depended on his defense so far this season, to say the least. In 11 1/3 innings pitched, he has only four strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Last season, Fausto Carmona filled in when two Indians starter suffered injuries, and he ended up winning a permanent job and 19 games. This year, it's Laffey filling in more than admirably -- first for an injured Jake Westbrook and now for Carmona. Laffey is coming off a six-inning outing in which he gave up just two runs (one earned) on seven hits and a walk to get his third win. He has allowed just three earned runs over his last five starts. This will be his first career appearance against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Murray's only start of the season wasn't sparkling, but it was effective. On May 3 at Oakland, Murray lasted 5 1/3 and held the Athletics to three runs, two earned, en route to a victory. In that outing, he allowed only six hits and two walks while striking out two. In his career, Murray has pitched a grand total of one inning, spread out over two appearances, against the Indians. But he's flawless in that one inning with one strikeout.
away_pitcher_note: This was supposed to be Jake Westbrook's second start since his return from the disabled list and an intercostal strain. Instead, Westbrook is headed right back to the DL with right elbow inflammation. Mastny, a reliever in parts of three seasons with the Indians, gets his first Major League start. He is 7-3 with a 5.00 ERA in 68 big league relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson got back on track in his last start, earning his fourth victory of the season on May 31 by holding the Athletics to four runs in seven innings. Ponson gets the start in the series finale with Cleveland, which will be his first meeting with the Indians this season. Ponson is still in search of his first victory against the Tribe, as he's winless in 12 appearances -- 11 of which starts. In those 12 games, he's 0-7 with a 9.47 ERA, having allowed 83 hits and 35 walks to just 31 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Lee has given up 11 runs in his last three starts after giving up four in his first seven starts of the season. In his last outing, against the Royals, Lee picked up the win, but only lasted six innings, giving up four runs. It was his second-shortest outing of the season. Lee has struggled lately, but who could've expected him to continue pitching as brilliantly as he did in April and early May.

home_pitcher_note: In his return from the DL on Friday against the Athletics, Millwood was superb, holding the Athletics to one run in six innings on five hits while striking out five and walking none. Millwood earned the victory against Oakland, which was his first since April 30 against Kansas City. Millwood's groin, which landed him on the DL, gave him no problems as he located pitches with ease. He returns to the mound Wednesday against Cleveland, which will be the first time he's faced his old club this season. Millwood is 2-1 in three career starts against the Tribe, with a 4.12 ERA and 23 strikeouts to just six walks.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia lost the fifth of his career Saturday night against the Royals. Sabathia went eight innings, allowing four runs, three of which came in one inning. Again, he didn't get much run support, which contributed him to losing his seventh game. In his last three starts, Sabathia has gone a combined 22 innings and given up just seven runs. Yet he hasn't won any of those games.

home_pitcher_note: See that loss total? The Tigers have scored two runs or fewer in seven of those defeats, giving him a run support average of 3.12 runs per nine innings as the pitcher of record -- fourth-lowest among qualified AL starters. The other problem, of course, is his pitching, and Felix Hernandez purely outpitched Verlander in his last start. With four runs allowed over seven innings, one of them on a botched squeeze bunt attempt that became a steal of home, Verlander saw his three-game streak of quality starts come to an end. He's 3-6 with a 7.03 ERA in 10 career starts against the Indians, but 2-1 when facing them at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd gave up a home run to Jose Guillen against the Royals on Sunday and never recovered. He lasted just 4 1/3 innings and gave up all six runs in a loss. Mark Grudzielanek, who hadn't homered since last year, hit a two-run shot off him. Byrd lamented the fact that he struggled so much when his team really needed a series win. In his last three starts, Byrd has now given up 14 home runs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers is now back in his customary spot between Justin Verlander and Jeremy Bonderman, giving the Tigers a finesse left-hander between their two power right-handers for the weekend series against the Indians. It also allows Rogers to pitch on his normal four days' rest after tossing quality starts in his last two outings. He pitched into eighth inning Monday at Oakland for the first time since the 2006 World Series, allowing two runs but keeping Detroit in the game. Rogers owns a 17-16 career record against Cleveland with a 5.12 ERA, but he's 4-2 against the Indians since joining the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe it was the Texas heat or just the hot Texas bats that got to him, but Laffey had his first rough outing of the season Monday against the Rangers. In five innings of work, he gave up eight runs on 11 hits with two walks and two strikeouts. He served up two home runs, including a game-tying grand slam. In his first six starts, Laffey had shown an ability to consistently work himself out of trouble by getting double-play balls, but he didn't have as much success keeping the ball down in this one. He has never faced the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga will return to the rotation after pitching three innings of relief in an unconventional piggyback start last Tuesday at Oakland. He walked two batters and allowed a three-run home run before retiring the last seven batters he faced. His return to the Tigers rotation gives him a rematch against the team he beat for his first Major League victory April 16 at Jacobs Field. He held the Tribe to a hit and two runs with six strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings that night, starting him on the roll that has made him stick on the Tigers staff.
away_pitcher_note: With Jake Westbrook back on the disabled list with elbow inflammation, the Indians will once again have to dip into their starting depth to round out the rotation. Sowers has made two spot starts for the Tribe this season, and now he'll get his first chance at a more sustained stay in '08. Through 10 starts at Triple-A Buffalo, Sowers had a 4-3 record and 2.08 ERA that ranked fourth in the International League. Sowers struck out 43 batters and walked just 17 in 60 2/3 innings. Sowers is 1-1 with a 6.30 ERA in two career starts against the Tigers and has never pitched in Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Willis makes his first full start since coming off the disabled list with a hyperextended right knee. He started a game in Oakland last Tuesday, but piggybacked the start with Armando Galarraga. Willis threw four innings, giving up no runs, two hits and five walks, and Galarraga relieved him. Willis is 0-1 with a 2.25 ERA in two career starts against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: The hitting-friendly conditions at Rangers Ballpark did not work in Lee's favor in his last start Wednesday in Texas, when he gave up six runs on nine hits in five innings but won thanks to an outpouring of offensive support. In general, though, Lee hasn't been nearly as dominant of late as he was in the first six weeks of the season, when he was putting up downright historic numbers. He's allowed 16 earned runs over his last four starts, yet he's won his last three in a row. He'll be in more pitching-friendly conditions Monday, when he faces the Tigers for the first time this season. Lee is 3-6 with a 5.23 ERA in 14 career starts against the Tigers and 1-1 with a 3.53 ERA in six starts at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: The hitting-friendly elements of Rangers Ballpark and a costly fielding error made behind him might have contributed to his demise, but it was nonetheless apparent Sabathia wasn't quite as dominant in Texas on Thursday as he had been recently. In six innings, he gave up five runs, four of which were earned, on nine hits with three walks and eight strikeouts. Before the outing, Sabathia had posted a 2.01 ERA over his previous eight starts. He'll look to get back to that trend in the comforts of home against a Twins team he has yet to face this year. Sabathia was 4-1 with a 1.51 ERA in five starts against Minnesota last year.
away_pitcher_note: Baker reclaimed his spot in the rotation on Thursday. He was effective, going five innings and giving up two earned runs to get the no-decision in a 3-2 loss. Baker didn't appear to be bothered by the strained groin that put him on the 15-day disabled list. Baker went seven innings and allowed only one run while striking out eight against the Indians on April 20, a 2-1 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd earned his 100th career win Friday the way he earned the vast majority of the others. He worked ahead, mixed up his pitches, commanded the ball to both sides of the plate and generally left the Tigers perplexed for seven innings in which he allowed just two runs on four hits with no walks and two strikeouts. Byrd needed just 80 pitches to get through the outing. But he's still having trouble keeping the ball in the yard. He gave up another two homers to bring his league-leading total to 16. Byrd held the Twins to a run on six hits in seven innings in a no-decision on April 20.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since taking a Bobby Abreu line drive to the face, Blackburn appeared on track early to perhaps make up for his streak of failed wins. Instead, he found trouble �- and lots of it �- in the fifth inning. Blackburn allowed five straight hits before being pulled, giving up a total of seven earned runs on eight hits in his four-plus innings. Next up for Blackburn will be his second start of the year against the Indians. The right-hander held the Indians scoreless for 7 2/3 innings in that start at the Metrodome on April 19.

home_pitcher_note: Injuries this season to Jake Westbrook and Fausto Carmona have allowed Laffey to claim a rotation spot, but he's certainly earned the position. After enduring his first rough start of the season in Texas, he rebounded nicely against the Tigers on Saturday, giving up just two runs on six hits with two walks and two strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings. Laffey has the confidence and ability to get out of jams with his grounder-inducing sinkerball. He's held the opposition to two runs or less in six of his eight starts. Laffey went 0-1 with a 7.71 ERA in two starts against the Twins last year.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching a near shutout against the White Sox in his first start vs. the club, Hernandez struggled mightily in his second outing at Chicago. The right-hander allowed seven earned runs on eight hits over just four innings. Next up for Hernandez will be to face the only team in the Majors he's never pitched against, the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers has claimed a rotation spot for at least a couple of weeks as Fausto Carmona is on the mend and Jake Westbrook is on the shelf. But in his return to the rotation Sunday against the Tigers, Sowers didn't show the aggressiveness that had made him so successful at Triple-A Buffalo this year. Instead, he got into the bad habit of nibbling, and the Tigers roughed him up for five runs on seven hits with two walks and two strikeouts in four innings. He'll try to pitch more to his strengths against a Padres team he's never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Consider the case of Banks. Claimed off waivers from the Blue Jays last month for $20,000, Banks has been a boost to a team that's missing three starting pitchers. Banks finally saw his consecutive-innings streak (22) without yielding an earned run end in his last start, though he allowed little else in a victory over the Mets Thursday. That streak also is the longest in franchise history for a pitcher to start his Padres career. Banks has shown good command of all his pitches in his limited time with the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Because he had to sit through a 57-minute rain delay, Lee's outing against the Tigers on Monday didn't last very long. But it did last long enough for him to earn his 10th win of his bounceback season. The All-Star candidate allowed two runs on six hits with two walks and five strikeouts in five innings. He had given up 10 runs over his previous two starts, so this was an improvement. Lee has come back down to earth after his scintillating start to the season, but he's still showing strong command of the strike zone. He hasn't faced the Padres since 2005, when he held them scoreless for seven innings in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Baek, acquired from the Mariners two weeks ago for a Minor League reliever, pitched well on June 7 against the Mets. Baek allowed one run over six innings and was able to pitch out of several tight spots. The Padres are encouraged by Baek's progress and how he's getting stretched out after pitching in relief while with Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia had it all working Tuesday night against the Twins. In nine innings, all he allowed were five hits with no walks and five strikeouts in picking up his second shutout of the season. The Twins didn't have a runner reach second base after the first inning, and Sabathia retired the last 17 batters he faced. This was Sabathia showing off the form that earned him the Cy Young Award in 2007. That form has eluded him at times in '08, but it was quite present here. He'll look to keep it going against the Padres, who he held to two runs in 7 2/3 innings in a victory in his lone career appearance against them 2005.
away_pitcher_note: Same old Greg Maddux. The future Hall of Famer allowed one run over six innings in his last start on June 10 against the Dodgers but left with no decision, the fifth time that's happened this season. That happened a lot last season, too, as the Padres, for some reason, never seem to score many runs for him. Maddux was his usual efficient self against the Dodgers and made several nice plays with his glove.

home_pitcher_note: Reynolds followed his first career win, against the Brewers, with his worst performance of the season against the Giants. Reynolds struggled to keep his sinker down in the strike zone, and the Giants tagged him for eight runs on 10 hits in 3 1/3 innings. Reynolds pitched into the fifth inning in each of his first six starts, and his ERA was 5.24 before Thursday's game against San Francisco. This will be Reynolds' first start against an American League team.
away_pitcher_note: It's fortunate for Byrd that the humidor is in use at Coors Field these days, because he's turned his share of ballparks into launching pads this year. Byrd served up his league-leading 17th homer of the season in a rough start against the Twins on Wednesday. Coming off an extraordinarily efficient outing against the Tigers, he was beaten up for six runs (five earned) on six hits with a walk and a strikeout in just three innings of work. He'll look to have better luck at Coors, where the fly-ball pitcher is 0-2 with a 9.82 ERA in five career appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Francis got through a clean first inning -- a problem for much of the year -- and pitched well for nearly all of his six-plus innings Friday against the White Sox at U.S. Cellular Field in his last start. However, four of the final six batters he faced reached, and he ended up with a no-decision. Still, Francis showed an effective two-seam fastball and continued his recovery from a slow start to the season.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey's last start against the Twins on Thursday wasn't the most efficient of outings, as he needed 101 pitches to get through six innings. But he was nonetheless effective, allowing just a run on five hits with a walk and four strikeouts. He got himself into some jams and some three-ball counts, but he remained confident in his sinker and it paid off. Laffey, who has been a key contributor to the Indians' injury-ravaged rotation, has never faced the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa is making his second straight start after he was demoted to the bullpen on May 28. De La Rosa has struggled with his command this season, but was extremely sharp in a spot start against the White Sox on June 14. He threw five shutout innings and struck out a career-high eight batters in the no-decision. In six career games against the Indians, De La Rosa is 1-3 with a 7.67 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Sowers once again showed an inability to put away hitters. He'd get ahead in the count, but he couldn't make the pitch that would turn a favorable count into an out. That ended up hurting him badly in his last outing, which a late Tribe rally turned into a no-decision. Sowers gave up nine hits and four runs in 4 2/3 innings. Having squandered a 3-0 lead, he left the ballgame trailing and with his pitch count at almost 100. That's not what the Indians need from him, particularly with the troubles of their bullpen. He will need to pitch deeper into the ballgame if he plans to stick in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw was locked in a scoreless duel through four innings when rain delayed his start against the Tigers. Management wouldn't let him restart the game 47 minutes later. He struck out two and walked two, escaping a first-inning mess with a double-play grounder. The two walks continue to illustrate the highest hurdle he needs to clear.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Lee was hardly the pitcher who had displayed razor-sharp control in opening the season. Pitching against the Padres, he threw 105 pitches in 6 1/3 innings, and just 67 of those pitches were strikes. His problem was getting his pitches too high in the strike zone, a lethal combination for a pitcher. Still, Lee kept the damage to a minimum, and he would have picked up his 11th win if the Indians bullpen had held onto a 3-2 lead he gave it.

home_pitcher_note: Park will fill in and start for the injured Hiroki Kuroda on Saturday. Kuroda was diagnosed with tendinitis and an impingement in his right shoulder on Wednesday, prompting Dodgers manager Joe Torre to give Park the start. Park's only start this season came May 17 against the Angels when he gave up two runs on three hits through four innings of work. Park was also tabbed as a possible one-time replacement for starter Brad Penny, is also on the disabled list. Eric Stults was called up from Triple-A Las Vegas to start instead.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia only seems to get stronger as this season progresses. After his disastrous four starts to open the season, he has posted a 2.39 ERA over his last 10 starts. He had just one bad inning against the Padres in a win on Sunday, as he allowed three runs on six hits with a walk and 10 strikeouts over eight innings. It marked the 14th time in his career he had posted a double-digit strikeout game. This will be Sabathia's first career appearance against the Dodgers, and the lifetime .297 hitter is probably more excited to pick up a bat than he is to take the mound at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley was solid in his last outing, pitching 6 1/3 innings and giving up just one run on five hits with three walks and nine strikeouts. It was his first win since beating Cincinnati on May 21. All of his pitches were working, and the right-hander never ran into trouble until he gave up a couple soft base hits in the seventh inning.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd has been very inconsistent this season and especially shaky in his last two starts. He has allowed 10 earned runs over those two outings, lasting a total of just seven innings. The long ball continues to prove his undoing. He gave up another pair in a loss in Colorado on Tuesday -- one of which was an inside-the-park job by Jeff Baker. For the season, Byrd has allowed 19 homers -- the most in the league. He has had trouble commanding his slider of late. Byrd is 0-3 with a 3.79 ERA in six career appearances at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Laffey continues to find ways to work himself out of trouble, which is a testament to his confidence in his sinkerball. Facing the Rockies at Coors Field on Wednesday, he gave up eight hits with three walks and a hit batter in just six innings of work but limited the damage to three runs, mainly because he induced three double-play balls. Still, he took the loss, because of a lack of support. Opponents are batting .177 off Laffey with runners in scoring position this season. This will be Laffey's first career appearance against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Sanchez no-hit Detroit for five innings, striking out seven and issuing two walks in that span, before Curtis Granderson singled cleanly to open the sixth. Sanchez lasted three batters into the eighth inning, marking the second time in 15 starts this year that he had pitched into the eighth. Sanchez is averaging a little more than a strikeout per inning (88 in 87 1/3), harnessing his fastball and employing his slider to greater effect. The inconsistency he displayed early in the season is becoming more and more of a memory with each outing.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers gave up 10 hits to the Rockies on Thursday, but several of those were of the infield variety. Sowers took the loss by giving up four runs (three earned) with no walks and four strikeouts in six innings. Still, this outing was an improvement over the two that preceded it. Sowers will remain in the rotation for a while, as Fausto Carmona suffered a setback on his road to recovery from a hip strain, so the young left-hander will look to be more efficient and, yes, a little more lucky against a Giants team he's never faced.
away_pitcher_note: After a promising May in which he turned in a 3.49 ERA in five starts, Zito's problems have returned in June, reaching a low point in his last start, in which he only made it through two innings while falling to 2-11. Zito has walked at least four batters in all four of his June starts, which has added to the problem. Zito is 5-3 with a 2.71 ERA against the Indians in nine career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lee was dominant early and resilient late in his last start against the Dodgers on Friday. When the Dodgers put the heat on Lee in the game's later innings, he didn't blink. He left runners stranded on the corners in the sixth and two runners stranded in scoring position in the seventh. In all, he allowed just a run on six hits with a walk and three strikeouts in the close ballgame, but he was unable to come up with his 11th win because his bullpen let him down. Still, Lee seems to have successfully readjusted after a brief stretch where his early season dominance departed him. He is 1-0 with a 1.29 ERA in one career start against the Giants and is 10-2 overall in Interleague Play.
away_pitcher_note: Could Cain be ready to turn his season around? It sure appeared that way Friday night in Kansas City. He gave up three runs in the first and then dominated. Cain went eight innings, allowing just those three runs and striking out eight. He said he's felt more comfortable in his last few starts mainly because he's been taking an approach where he goes at the hitters more with his fastball. Cain has won two of his last three outings.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia's overall command hasn't been better at any point this season than it is right now. He has found the form that made him the AL Cy Young Award winner in '07, giving up just four runs on 16 hits with two walks and 25 strikeouts over 24 innings in his last three starts. Making his first career start against the Dodgers on Saturday, he allowed just a run on five hits over seven innings. Unfortunately for Sabathia, when he hit a solo shot for his second career homer, that was his only run of support, and he took a no-decision on a day he pitched well enough to win. Sabathia is 2-0 with a 2.68 ERA in seven career starts against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start, Thompson blanked a tough Yankees offense through five innings to come away with a no-decision. The right-hander got off to a shaky start when he loaded the bases with no outs in the second inning. But he retired the next three batters, striking out two, to get out of the jam.
