It came at a cost to his pitch count, though, as Thompson racked up 47 throws in the first two innings and ended the day with 96. He gave up four hits and walked four in his first Reds start.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd gave up four runs before he recorded an out in his start against the Dodgers on Sunday, and he ended up taking the loss. Still, the outing felt like a victory, of sorts, for him, because he righted himself after those first-inning foibles. In all, he gave up just the four runs on seven hits with no walks and a strikeout in seven innings by finding confidence his curveball, particularly against left-handers. Byrd, who is 4-1 with a 3.04 ERA in 14 career starts against the Reds, hopes the Dodgers outing is a sign that he's recovered from the two rough starts that preceded it.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto threw five innings of one-run ball against the Yankees on Sunday, but a lack of run support from the Reds' offense gave him the loss. It was a solid performance from the right-hander, who struck out seven with no walks. Cueto gave up just four hits, but long at-bats led to a high pitch count, and he did not return to the game after a rain delay, leaving with a total of 75 throws. It marked the fourth straight loss for the righty.

home_pitcher_note: Laffey continued to show his ability to get the double-play ball when he needed it Tuesday against the Giants. He gave up just one run on four hits with three walks and a strikeout over 6 2/3 innings in a no-decision. The damage might have been worse if he didn't use his sinker to get a pair of double plays. Laffey has pitched much better than his record indicates, and he's taken three no-decisions in his last six starts. He has never faced the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo posted what he called the worst outing of his career in his last start -- a 14-1 drubbing at Toronto on Monday. The Blue Jays lit up Arroyo for 10 earned runs and 11 hits, including three home runs as the right-hander lasted a career-low one-plus innings. The earned runs were a career high, and the hits allowed tied a career high. He's 0-3 with a 10.07 ERA over his last five starts. Over his last two, he's given up 16 earned runs and 18 hits. The drubbing at Toronto caused Arroyo's 5.55 ERA to skyrocket to 6.52.

home_pitcher_note: The Dodgers jumped on the White Sox right-hander for two runs on three hits in the first inning of Wednesday's 5-0 loss, and Floyd never seemed to recover. He allowed four earned runs on six hits over 5 1/3 innings, striking out two and walking two. Floyd also has some trouble pitching around mistakes behind him, giving up his 13th unearned run against the Dodgers, tops in the Majors. Floyd has a 1-0 record with a 6.00 ERA against the Indians this season and is 1-1 with a 4.38 ERA lifetime against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Although he picked up the loss, Sowers gave the Tribe a quality start in his last outing, going seven innings in Wednesday's effort against the Giants. Yes, his control was a bit erratic at times (five walks), he seemingly couldn't keep the ball in the infield (nine hits) and he found trouble early (two first-inning runs), but the left-hander showed better command of his fastball, which allowed him to mitigate the damage (three runs). Up and down from Triple-A Buffalo all season, Sowers has yet to face the White Sox in 2008. He faced them last year, though, giving up two runs in six innings for a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Danks closed out the month of June with another quality start, hurling six scoreless innings against the Dodgers during Thursday afternoon's series finale. Danks now has thrown 11 straight scoreless innings and ranks third in the American League for lowest ERA. He struck out three and walked four against the Dodgers, throwing 106 pitches overall, and worked out of two jams with a runner on third and less than two outs. Danks has no record in one start against Cleveland this season and has a 1-2 mark with a 4.44 ERA lifetime against the Indians. Danks also picked up his first career Interleague victory and first big league hit on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Lee continued his campaign to be the American League's starting pitcher for the All-Star Game with another impressive start Thursday against the Giants. And this time he was actually awarded for it. The left-hander went eight innings, striking out a career-high 11 and, thanks mostly to his precisely located fastball, never really had to escape trouble to pick up his 11th win of the season. He continues to be bright spot for the Indians in 2008, especially after a rough 2007, where he was sent to Triple-A Buffalo to work out of a season-long funk. Lee has yet to face the White Sox this season, but he has faced them the most out of any opponent for his career. In 17 appearances -- 15 starts -- Lee is 4-5 with a 6.61 ERA against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Contreras gave up three runs in six-plus innings in his second start against the Cubs on Friday. The performance was good enough for the right-hander to pick up his seventh win, though manager Ozzie Guillen knew how much his pitcher struggled throughout the start. The win snapped a three-game losing streak during which he'd allowed 18 runs in 16 innings. His ERA has gone from a season-low 2.76 before the losing streak to just under four. Contreras has faced Cleveland once this year, giving up just one run over six innings at U.S. Cellular Field on May 20.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia continued his hot streak since late April with another strong start. His latest victim, the Reds on Friday, managed just four hits while striking out 11 times over eight innings. The big left-hander was nearly unhittable after the second inning, retiring 15 batters in a row at one point. He's had mixed results against the White Sox this season, though, allowing five runs in 5 1/3 innings of work in an Opening Day no-decision. He pitched much better the second time around, but this time picked up the loss after a seven-inning, two-run effort. Lifetime against the White Sox, Sabathia has been much better, as he carries a 14-4 record and 3.61 ERA in 25 starts.

home_pitcher_note: After two dominant outings against his former National League foes, Hernandez gave up five runs -- four earned -- on seven hits in his start against the Brewers, – all of which were scored by the third inning. Despite the early troubles, Hernandez managed to pitch seven innings to help save the Twins bullpen. The leader of the Twins staff has seen his share of ups and downs this season and he’'ll try to fix one disappointment in his second career start against the Indians. Hernandez delivered his worst start of the year in Cleveland last month, allowing seven runs on 12 hits in just three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd scuffled again in his last outing, but he didn't let the game get out of hand. Struggling to find his command in Saturday's loss to the Reds, Byrd threw just 57 strikes out of 95 pitches. He again had trouble keeping the ball in the park, allowing his Major League-worst 21st home run of the season to Adam Dunn. Byrd has had mixed results against the Twins this season. He allowed just one run in seven innings in April at the Metrodome, but when he faced the Twins in Cleveland two months later, he was torched for six runs in three innings. The veteran right-hander is 10-4 with a 3.79 ERA in his career against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey continues to demonstrate why he was so coveted by other teams during his rapid ascent through the Twins Minor League system. The right-hander pitched his first career shutout on Sunday against the Brewers, holding Milwaukee to just three hits while striking out eight batters and not issuing a single walk. It was the fourth straight quality start for Slowey and he is now 3-0 with a 0.93 ERA over that span.  Next up for Slowey will be his first start of the season against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Constantly having a knack to find trouble  but somehow being able to escape it, the left-handed Laffey finally got punished. Laffey's ability to get crucial double-play balls has been his way out of sticky situations, but he couldn't do it on Sunday. The Reds erupted for a five-run fifth inning to give the rookie his fifth loss of the season. In his only start against the Twins this season, Laffey was the benefactor of a 12-run outburst from the Indians lineup, but wasn't too shabby himself, allowing just one run in six innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: The Twins have preached to their pitching staff to throw inside this season and one pitcher who has listened is Perkins. The southpaw has found particular success in doing that against the Tigers. He limited Detroit to just two runs over 6 1/3 innings while striking out a career-high seven batters in his last start. Perkins will try to continue that same approach when he faces the Indians for the first time this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians will take advantage of Thursday's off-day to keep Lee on his fifth day. They have every reason to do so, given that Lee has had a first half worthy of an All-Star starting bid. He has refined his command, regained the confidence that helped make him an 18-game winner in 2005 and been a steady force in the rotation. His bid for his 12th win was thwarted by the lack of run support he received Tuesday against the White Sox, when he gave up just one run on six hits with a walk and three strikeouts but took a no-decision. Lee worked eight shutout innings in a win over the Twins on April 18.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Jim Leyland used Monday's off-day to move up Verlander in the rotation and keep him on track to pitch every fifth day. Verlander has picked up his game since the opening month, but he has struggled with rapidly rising pitch counts and long innings in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The first start in the post-CC Sabathia era goes to Sowers. He might have better velocity on his fastball than a year ago, but the hard truth is that Sowers is much more like the guy who couldn't hold onto his big league job in '07 than the guy who dominated as a rookie in the second half of '06. His command has been out of whack -? never moreso than in his last outing against the White Sox on Monday. Sowers lasted just three innings in that loss, giving up eight runs on six hits with two walks and two strikeouts. He gave up a three-run homer to Jim Thome and a grand slam to Nick Swisher.

home_pitcher_note: Bonine was pushed back a day from his original rotation spot, which was slated to fall on Tuesday. That makes this his final start before the All-Star break. He'll still have the same opponent, facing an Indians club that has struggled offensively this year. That could provide the opportunity for Bonine to get back into quality pitching if he can attack the strike zone on the corners rather than the middle of the plate, which was his downfall his last time out at Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd has had a very inconsistent season, but one constant has been his penchant for dishing out the home-run ball. He might fare a little better in the pitching-friendly confines of Comerica Park. He had a strong outing there on June 6, when he held the Tigers to a pair of runs on four hits over seven innings for his 100th career victory, but he nonetheless gave up a pair of homers in that start.

home_pitcher_note: Laffey had his second consecutive poor start on Saturday. The rookie allowed four earned runs in five innings on five hits and four walks against Minnesota. This came after an Interleague start where Laffey allowed a five-run fifth inning to the Reds. The lefty will next take on the Rays, a club he has never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine earned his seventh win of the season Saturday after blanking the Royals for seven innings while limiting them to five hits and a walk while striking out two. The right-hander is a master of deception employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to setup the other pitches. Sonnanstine is 0-1 with a 4.50 ERA in one career start against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: On the same day Lee was announced to the All-Star team, the lefty went seven innings and gave up four earned runs on six hits and two walks against the Twins in a 4-3 Indians loss. Lee sailed through five scoreless innings before running into trouble in a one-run sixth and three-run seventh. Even so, Lee continues to be a stabilizing force on an otherwise disappointing team. Lee's next start, his last before the All-Star Break, will come against Tampa Bay. Lee has not faced the Rays in 2008 during the club's breakout campaign.
away_pitcher_note: Shields picked up his seventh win of the season Sunday when he held the Royals to two runs on four hits and a walk while striking out eight in seven innings. The 26-year-old right-hander's best pitch has always been his changeup, but he also has a plus fastball and curve and he's added a cutter that has helped him throw inside to left-handers. He is 0-1 with a 2.66 ERA in three career starts against the Indians and is 0-1 with a 2.84 ERA in one start at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: With reigning Cy Young Award winner CC Sabathia dealt to the Brewers, the Indians have a hole in their rotation that will need to be filled Saturday. Ginter, who is 6-6, 4.14 ERA in 18 appearances, including 17 starts, at Triple-A Buffalo appears to be the most obvious candidate, though that's not yet confirmed. Ginter was pulled from his last start against Syracuse on Tuesday after tossing three scoreless innings. Ginter, 30, has appeared in 92 big league games, including 15 starts, compiling a 4-4 record and 5.46 ERA with the White Sox and Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his 17th start of the season after earning a no-decision Monday against the Royals despite pitching well enough to win -- allowing three runs on nine hits in 6 2/3 innings. Garza has a mid-90s fastball that sinks, a curve, a slider and a changeup. He is 0-1 with a 3.60 ERA in three career starts against the Indians, and is 0-0 with a 1.50 ERA in one career start at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Under ordinary circumstances, Sowers would be working out his command issues at Triple-A Buffalo right about now. But the Indians' circumstances, because of injuries, ineffectiveness and the CC Sabathia trade, are not ordinary, so Sowers' spot in the rotation is a permanent one. He has given up 15 runs on 16 hits over 8 2/3 innings in his last two starts, though he did feel his fastball command improved in his loss to the Tigers on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir picked up the loss despite a solid performance against the Yankees on Monday. The left-hander gave up two runs and five hits in five innings, but lacked run support. He struck out nine and walked just one, but the Yankees worked him for long at-bats, and Kazmir exited after the fifth inning for his second straight start with a pitch count total of 97 throws. The lefty again struggled against the bottom of the opponent's lineup, but manager Joe Maddon said he liked Kazmir's slider and thought he had better command of his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Well, the first four innings were a blast. Hernandez dazzled against the Royals in his first start back since sustaining ankle sprain on June 23 until the fifth inning rolled around. He gave up three runs and was pulled out before the sixth. His numbers were still good: Five innings pitched, eight strikeouts, four hits and three earned runs. Manager Jim Riggleman thought that Hernandez might have lost some of the bite on his breaking ball in the fifth. Hernandez said he could've thrown 40 more pitches than the 83 he threw in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey finished up an impressive first half with a quality start and victory over the Rays on July 10. He limited the Rays to a pair of runs on four hits with three walks and four strikeouts over six innings. What stands out about Laffey is his poise in pressure situations. He is often able to get the big double-play ball to get out of jams. He's certainly taken advantage of the opportunity presented to him by the Indians' injury-ravaged rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Batista was moved up from Monday because of Jarrod Washburn's bout with the flu. The veteran right-hander makes his first post-All-Star Game start as one of five MLB pitchers who have won at least one game this season and also registered at least one save. He has held opposing hitters to a .172 batting average as a reliever, but opponents are batting .309 against him as a starter. Batista's 53 walks have been a problem, as it averages out to be 6.6 free passes every nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sowers set a career high with eight strikeouts in his last outing, but it didn't make up for the control problems he had in a no-decision on July 13 against the Rays. The lefty couldn't pick up his first win because he simply couldn't throw a strike when the count was full, piling up a career-worst seven walks and racking up his pitch count in the four-inning effort. If anything might be able to rectify Sowers' disappointing season, it might be a date with the Mariners. Sowers picked up one of his two career complete-game shutouts in 2006 against Seattle and threw five scoreless innings at Safeco Field in a spot start near the end of last season.

home_pitcher_note: Maybe now the pitcher Seattle broke the bank for is starting to live up to the expectations. After a mechanical change a couple weeks ago, Silva has had two solid outings. His most recent one came in a no-decision at Kansas City on Sunday. He went six innings, allowing just two runs while striking out five. Silva has now given up just two runs in consecutive starts after giving up five runs on July 3. It was after that game when Silva made the mechanical change.
away_pitcher_note: Lee wasn't lights out in his last outing, but he was good enough to keep the Rays scoreless in six innings of work. The left-hander never had a 1-2-3 inning in his 12th win of the year, but he allowed just one baserunner in each frame, facing four batters each time. It capped a surprising 12-2 first-half start, which helped earn his first-ever nomination to the AL All-Star team. In his one start against the Mariners this season, Lee went six-plus innings and allowed three runs in the winning effort. All-time against Seattle, Lee has been strong, going 6-1 with a 3.90 ERA in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Santana continued his dominance against the A's on Saturday and carried some positive momentum into the All-Star break and his first All-Star appearance Tuesday. Santana pitched seven scoreless innings, allowing just five hits and two walks while striking out 10 batters. He improved to 9-1 with a microscopic 1.36 ERA against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd finished up an underwhelming first half with a start that showed some improvement. He held the Tigers to three runs on nine hits with a walk and five strikeouts on July 9. Still, it wasn't enough to earn his victory since June 6, because his bullpen let him down. Byrd has really struggled keeping people off the basepaths this season, particularly left-handed hitters, who are batting .332 off him. Byrd has already given up 23 homers after allowing 27 all of last year and 26 in '06.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver continued his recent run of solid outings by throwing six strong innings against the Rangers on July 9. He allowed just one earned run on seven hits but the Angels lost the game on Josh Hamilton's game-winning home run in the ninth inning off Angels closer Francisco Rodriguez. Weaver has allowed two earned runs or fewer in each of his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start since 2005, Ginter gave the Indians more than they could have expected in a pinch. The 30-year-old righty tossed five scoreless innings and rarely sniffed trouble in his first Major-League win in four years. He struck out five and walked none, while only using an efficient 65 pitches. Ginter has struggled against the Angels, compiling a 8.72 ERA in one start and eight relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey returned from the All-Star break with a solid effort in beating the Red Sox on Friday night, holding them to three earned runs on five hits across seven innings with two walks and six strikeouts. He became the sixth pitcher in franchise history to reach 1,000 strikeouts. The Red Sox had given Lackey fits in the past, the win raising his career record against them to 2-6. He's 3-5 in 10 career outings against the Indians despite an excellent 2.85 ERA. He hasn't faced the Tribe this season.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey was knocked around by the Mariners on Friday and got a tough break on a Jhonny Peralta error in the second inning that eventually yielded five Seattle runs �- all unearned. The big blow in that bunch was a grand slam from Raul Ibanez. Laffey lasted just 3 2/3 innings, giving up nine hits and eight runs (three earned). Laffey continues to neutralize left-handed hitters with a .224 opponents' batting average, but he has had a tough time on the road this year, with a 5.94 ERA away from Progressive Field. He hasn't faced the Angels so far this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lee was pegged for 11 hits against the Mariners on Sunday, but that didn't prevent him from turning in his second complete game of the season. In nine innings, he limited the damage to a pair of runs with no walks and four strikeouts. He threw 77 percent of his pitches for strikes in the outing, and that's really been the key to his impressive '08 season, in which he became the first AL pitcher to reach 13 wins. Lee is 1-1 with a 2.41 ERA in two starts against the Twins this season.
away_pitcher_note: The lone veteran in the Twins rotation continued to show his dominance at home in his last start. Hernandez extended his record at the Metrodome to 8-1 after holding the Rangers to just two runs on five hits over seven innings. But it's away from the Metrodome where the right-hander has found trouble. He's just 2-5 with a 7.48 ERA in nine road starts. And next up, he'll face a Cleveland team that pounded him at Progressive Field in his first start there on June 12, allowing seven runs on 12 hits in just three innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona will rejoin the Indians' rotation after missing two months with a left hip strain suffered May 23 against the Rangers. He made two rehab starts with Class A Lake County and Double-A Akron and has had no physical problems after a brief setback in late June. The Indians hope Carmona's return will see him return to his form of 2007, when he won 19 games. He was struggling with his command before getting hurt, walking 38 batters in 58 innings. Carmona was 3-1 with a 1.45 ERA in four starts against the Twins last year.
away_pitcher_note: Baker continues to be the unfortunate recipient of some bad breaks. Although he allowed just one run on two hits over eight innings against Texas, Baker picked up the loss in a 1-0 defeat. Baker has delivered 10 quality starts in the 15 games he's pitched this season. His consistent performance has him emerging as the true ace of this young Twins staff. In his next start, he'll try to see if his offense can have better luck while he's facing the Indians. Baker is 0-1 vs. Cleveland this season, despite having allowed just one earned run in each of his two starts against the club.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers received a permanent spot in the Indians' rotation because of injuries to Jake Westbrook and Fausto Carmona and the trade of CC Sabathia. Generally, he's struggled to prove he's worthy of the job, though he had an encouraging outing against the Mariners on July 19. Sowers gave up four runs on five hits with three walks and three strikeouts in six innings. The Indians believe he is taking baby steps toward becoming a reliable member of their starting five. He'll look  to take more steps against the Twins. He is 1-1 with a 3.13 ERA in three career starts against Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn won't remember his first two starts against the Yankees fondly. After being struck by a Bobby Abreu line drive in the first of those starts, Blackburn exited his second outing vs. the Yankees early once again -- this time due to a poor start. The right-hander lasted just 1 2/3 innings, giving up six runs (three earned) on seven hits. A failure to make adjustments proved costly in that start and Blackburn will try to rebound against the Indians. Blackburn is 2-0 in two starts against the Tribe this season, allowing just two runs over 13 2/3 total innings.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd's fourth win was a long time coming. He was winless in six starts from June 11 to July 9, but he finally got in the win column against the Angels on July 21, allowing just one run on nine hits with two walks and five strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings. Byrd ran into some trouble with baserunners but never gave up the big hit, and he had some success with his changeup against left-handed batters, who have given him fits all season. Byrd is 1-0 with a 3.46 ERA in two starts against the Tigers this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers was on track to seven, maybe eight innings in his last start, against the Royals. Rain changed that. A long delay meant that Rogers had to leave after just six innings, albeit a good six. He gave up just one run and four hits. If not for Mark Grudzielanek's three hits, Rogers would've had a one-hitter. After the game, Rogers said he feels better now than he did a month or two ago. His numbers reflect that: his ERA has gone from 6.66 on May 21 to 4.48.

home_pitcher_note: The benefactor of Aaron Laffey's demotion to Triple-A Buffalo, Ginter will get his third start of what could be a full rest of the season with the Indians. Ginter has certainly earned his spot in the Tribe rotation, tossing 11 innings and allowing just three runs. His stuff isn't the greatest and he's not going to blow opponents away, but he's had a knack of dodging trouble, which is all Eric Wedge can ask for at this point of the season. He has been fairly successful against one of his former teams, albeit in relief appearances. Lifetime against the Tigers, the 30-year-old righty has a 1.80 ERA over 10 innings of work in five appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga pitched six perfect innings against Kansas City last Wednesday and still thought he had thrown better before. He talked about his 8 1/3-inning performance against Anaheim in late May as his best of the season. Maybe so, but Galarraga sure was good. He gave up just one run and three hits in seven innings, while striking out a career-high seven. It was also his first win since June 18 against San Francisco. In his last three starts, Galarraga has given up a combined seven runs.

home_pitcher_note: Lee became the Majors' first 14-game winner with another outstanding effort against the Twins on Friday night. Working ahead and pounding the zone all night, he gave up just two runs on six hits with no walks and 10 strikeouts in eight innings. Lee has now won three straight starts, and he's given up two runs or less in eight of his last nine outings. He only seems to get stronger as his amazing 2008 season progresses. He gave up two runs on six hits with two walks and five strikeouts in five innings in a win over the Tigers on June 9.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson exited his last start to a standing ovation from a sellout Comerica Park of 44,000-plus. He started quick, throwing just 14 pitches in the first two inning, and finished his six innings allowing three runs on five hits. He encountered a pair of jams, but each time he ended the threat by retiring American League home run leader Carlos Quentin. The left-hander departed with a 4-1 lead in the seventh after back-to-back singles, which the bullpen allowed to score. Nonetheless, Robertson rebounded nicely from a rough outing at Baltimore. He faces the Indians for the first time this season. In his career, Robertson is 2-5 with a 4.74 ERA against Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: The only thing Carmona can take away from his first start back from the disabled list was that he didn't go back on the DL. Carmona was out of control from the start and never got settled in a shellacking at the hands of the Twins on Saturday. Carmona lasted 2 1/3 innings, allowing nine runs on seven hits in an atrocious welcome back to the big leagues. Luckily, Carmona will have two things working in his favor Thursday. It will be daytime and he will be facing the Tigers. Carmona is 11-4 lifetime when the lights are off and is  4-2 with a 3.05 ERA all-time against Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander had one of the shortest outings of his career his last time out. He lasted only four innings, allowing seven runs on nine hits to give him double-digit losses for the first time. It also marked the first time Verlander went just four innings since Aug. 22 against the Indians. The star righty's impressive stretch came to an end. He yielded more than three earned runs in a start for the first time since May 31. He had allowed two earned runs or fewer in his last eight starts. In his last two starts against the Tribe, Verlander has given up a combined five earned runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn takes the mound against the Indians, five days after facing the Tribe in Cleveland. The right-hander ended up with a no-decision, but pitched well, allowing one run and four hits in seven innings. He left with a 2-1 lead but the Indians tied the game in the eighth. Blackburn is 2-0 in three starts against Cleveland this season. He has allowed three earned runs in 20 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sowers had his best start in nearly two years Sunday and it looks like the left-hander may have found a groove. In his longest outing since July 28, 2006, Sowers flirted with perfection, retiring the first 15 Twins in order, before bowing out after eight innings of the work. The only damage he allowed were two runs on a couple soft hits, but they were more than enough to force him to settle for a no-decision. Sowers has not faced the Twins this year, but in 2006 he picked up one of his two career complete-game shutouts against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey capped a difficult July on a stellar note. The right-hander had struggled mightily in his first three starts of the month -- going 1-1 with a 9.00 ERA. But Slowey pitched a gem against the White Sox in his last July start, throwing a complete-game shutout in the 7-0 Twins win. Slowey's first start of August will come against the Indians, whom he beat on July 5, going six innings while surrendering five earned runs in a 9-6 Twins victory.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd picked his second consecutive win Monday with his best start of the season. Over 7 2/3 strong innings, Byrd was barely touched, allowing just four hits and striking four to pick up his fifth win of what has been a disappointing season for the veteran right-hander. It was unlike most of his other starts where he's struggled keeping the ball in the park and runners off the bases. Over his last two starts, he has allowed just one run in 13 innings of work. He has struggled against the Twins this season, compiling a 0-2 record with a 7.04 ERA in three starts. Lifetime, he is 10-5 with a 4.06 ERA against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano struggled with the club in April after returning from injury. The 24-year-old left-hander was 0-3 with a 11.32 ERA in three starts. But he was dominant at Triple-A Rochester prior to being recalled on Friday. In his last 11 starts with the Red Wings, Liriano was 10-0 with a 2.67 ERA. His return to the Twins will come at the Metrodome on Sunday against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: After two quality starts in a spot role for the Tribe, Ginter has been given a more extended look in the Indians' rotation, and ran into trouble Tuesday in a loss to the Tigers. Ginter lasted just four innings, allowing four runs on eight hits with a walk, three strikeouts and one homer allowed. He didn't have quite the command he had in his previous two starts, as he burned 77 pitches to get through the short outing. Until the Indians feel Aaron Laffey has righted himself at Triple-A Buffalo, Ginter will remain in the rotation. So he'll get his first crack at the Twins in three years.

home_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his 21st start of the season after claiming his ninth win with a complete-game shutout of the Blue Jays on Tuesday night in Toronto. Garza was masterful, allowing no runs on five hits and a walk while striking out five. Garza has a mid-90s fastball that sinks, a curve, a slider and a changeup. He is 0-2 with a 5.85 ERA in four career starts against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Lee had a bizarre outing against the Tigers on Wednesday -- bizarre from the standpoint that he actually gave up more than a couple runs. In just five innings, Lee was roughed up for six runs on 10 hits with no walks and five strikeouts in a no-decision. Lee gave up two homers. Actually, Lee cruised through the first two innings, gave up a run each in the third and fourth and was tattooed in the fifth. This marked just the third time this year that Lee gave up more than four runs. He'll look to recover against a Rays team he held scoreless on six hits in six innings on July 11.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson picked up his seventh win of the season Wednesday in Toronto when he battled through five innings, holding the Blue Jays to two runs despite giving up seven hits and walking two. Twice the 24-year-old right-hander faced jams in which the Jays had a man on third with no outs and he did not allow the run to score. If Jackson is locating his 97-mph fastball, his other pitches can work well, particularly his slider. Jackson is 0-1 with a 2.61 ERA in four career appearances against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona rebounded from a woeful return from the disabled list with a more typical performance Thursday against the Tigers. Going 6 1/3 innings, the right-handed sinkerballer induced a number of groundouts, struck out three and found his way out of a number of jams, which were mostly the result of poor fielding and a glaring sun that played havoc on Tribe fielders. He allowed four runs (two earned) to pick up his fifth win of the season. He has yet to face the Rays this season, but in his one previous start against Tampa Bay he went seven innings and allowed two runs to pick up the victory.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir struggled with his control on Friday night when he picked up a no-decision against the Tigers. The 24-year-old left-hander threw 32 pitches in the first inning alone before leaving the game with two outs in the fifth and having thrown 110 pitches. Despite all the balls -- which led to six walks -- Kazmir only allowed two runs while striking out five. Kazmir is still working to gain command of his slider, which has historically been his best pitch. Without his slider, he has primarily used a fastball-changeup combination this season. He is 3-1 with a 3.08 ERA in four career starts against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander took a perfect game into the sixth inning for the second straight start, but couldn't get the win last Friday in Minneapolis. Sowers got ahead early in the count, before Twins hitters became more patient. He finishing line shows four earned runs in 6 2/3 innings, after a two-run homer and run scoring double in the seventh ended his night. Sowers allowed two earned runs on three hits against Tampa Bay July 13, but walked seven batters in four innings of work. He threw 93 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: The good news: Purcey allowed just three hits in his last start. The bad news: All three hits were home runs. Purcey started out hot, facing the minimum through three innings and striking out four of the nine batters he faced. He faded fast, though, allowing five runs the next two innings -- all on home runs -- before departing. Purcey will try to keep his pitches in the park in his next start Friday against the Indians, whom he's never pitched against.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians will see if Reyes can get back to being the guy who won Game 1 of the 2006 World Series or if he's still the guy who struggled with the Cards the past two seasons. After joining the Indians in a July 26 trade, Reyes impressed the Tribe with his first two starts at Triple-A Buffalo, where he went 2-0 with a 2.77 ERA. He owns a career Major League record of 10-24 and ERA of 5.38 in 53 games, including 38 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay was in fine form on Monday, limiting Oakland to one run on four hits over eight strong innings. The Blue Jays ace added eight strikeouts, upping his season total to 149, and he issued just one walk in the 113-pitch effort. Over his past seven starts, Halladay has turned in 48 shutout innings among the 56 frames he's logged, posting a 2.00 ERA during that span. He is 5-1 with a 3.97 ERA in 11 career games against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd continued his stellar performance as of late, allowing one earned run on six hits in seven innings Saturday in Minnesota for his third straight victory. His ERA is 0.90 in his last three starts because he's been keeping the ball in the park and men off base, something he struggled with earlier this year. Rumored to be traded before the July 31 deadline, Byrd tossed 7 2/3 scoreless innings July 28 against Detroit, and one earned run in his start before that. Byrd has not pitched against Toronto this year, but is 3-3 lifetime. He allowed one run in 8 1/3 innings in his lone start against the Blue Jays last season.

home_pitcher_note: A late rally by the Blue Jays on Tuesday night helped Richmond avoid what would've been a second hard-luck loss in a row. The 28-year-old rookie turned in an effective outing against the A's, allowing three runs on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings in his second career start in the Majors. Richmond struck out four and walked one in the no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Lee rebounded from perhaps his worst start in an otherwise stellar season by going seven innings, allowing just a pair of runs on eight hits with two walks and two strikeouts, in a win over the Rays on Monday. In doing so, he became the American League's first 15-game winner. The Rays had Lee on the ropes several times, and he needed 48 pitches just to get through the first two innings, but he never buckled. He pitched a gem against the Jays on May 12, giving up just seven hits in nine scoreless innings but nonetheless walking away with a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona has struggled to find his groove since coming back from the DL. His control was out of whack on Tuesday in Tampa Bay, as he allowed four runs on three hits with five walks and four strikeouts in four innings. The Indians want him to more consistently find the proper release point on his pitches, most notably his once-trusty sinker. Carmona was 2-0 with a 0.59 ERA in two starts against the Orioles last year.
away_pitcher_note: Sarfate has yet to complete five innings in either of his first two starts, and he'll be watched closely for progress in his next outing. If Sarfate isn't able to throw a better strike-to-ball ratio or work deeper into the game, he may head back to the bullpen. And if he does, the Orioles would probably swap in Hayden Penn from Triple-A Norfolk.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers' command betrayed him against the Rays on Wednesday, but he still turned in a decent outing. He struggled early, giving up three runs in the first, but settled down after that. In all, he gave up four runs (three earned) on six hits with three walks and two strikeouts in six innings. He'll try to have a more consistent outing against the Orioles, against whom he has a 11.57 career ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Olson seemed to have turned a corner for the Orioles three starts ago. The left-hander was superb against the Angels in the Orioles' final game before embarking on a nine-game road trip and followed that up with a strong performance in Seattle on August 1, but in his last start Olson took a few steps back, reverting to the pitcher who hadn't been able to make it through the sixth inning in six of his last 10 starts. Olson pitched just 2 2/3 innings, getting tagged with the loss in a 9-4 shellacking at the hands of the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes, acquired from the Cardinals on July 26 and initially sent to Triple-A Buffalo, gave up just one run on seven hits with a walk and four strikeouts in 6 1/3 innings in a win over the Blue Jays on Friday in his Tribe debut. The Indians were intrigued by Reyes because he was once the top prospect of the Cards and the winner of Game 1 of the 2006 World Series. This was but a single start, but it was a promising one for an Indians team trying to figure out its rotation options for 2009 and beyond.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie followed up what was arguably his best performance of the season -- a complete-game four-hitter against the Mariners -- with an equally outstanding outing on Friday. Guthrie threw seven innings, allowing just one run on five hits against the Rangers, earning his ninth win of the season in the Orioles' 9-1 victory over the Rangers on Friday night. The one run Guthrie allowed was a solo homer to Chris Davis and outside of that one at-bat, the right-hander was in control all night, using an especially effective slider to fool the Rangers hitters. Guthrie has now been able to get the win in his last three consecutive starts.

home_pitcher_note: The left-handed Jackson was recalled from Triple-A Buffalo to fill the void left by Paul Byrd, who was traded to the Red Sox. Considered a throw-in part of the deal that sent CC Sabathia to the Brewers in early July, Jackson has been solid over the past five weeks with the Bisons and was added to their starting rotation on July 21. In eight appearances (four starts), the 25-year-old was 3-1 with a 4.05 ERA. He struck out 20 while walking just five batters over 26 2/3 innings. Those numbers are far from what he put up earlier in the season at Triple-A Nashville, where he was 1-5 with a 7.85 ERA in 22 appearances (eight starts). Jackson owns a Major League lifetime record of 2-2 with a 5.36 ERA in 10 appearances, seven of which were starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cabrera will be looking to put together consecutive wins for the first time since May 8-20, when the he was 3-0 in three starts. Cabrera, who has struggled with his control, shutout the league's best offense for six innings in his last outing, as the Orioles routed the Rangers, 9-0. Cabrera worked best with his two-seam fastball and set down 15 of 16 batters from the first through sixth innings. Even when he did get in trouble, the 6-foot-9 right-hander escaped without any damage done. Cabrera has a 4.45 ERA on the road this season and has yet to face the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Lee continued his bid to become the Indians' first 20-game winner in 34 years and the Tribe's second Cy Young Award winner in two years with eight scoreless innings in a win over the Blue Jays on Sunday. He allowed eight hits, walked none and struck out one, and he was so in command of his fastball that just 21 of his 104 pitches went for balls. Lee hasn't faced the Angels this season and is 4-3 with a 3.56 ERA in seven starts against them in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver wasn't at his best against the Yankees on Friday night at home, but it didn't matter on a night the Angels' bats exploded. Weaver wasn't happy departing after six innings, having yielded five earned runs on seven hits, but the W was attached to his name, so it wasn't all bad. He yielded a pair of solo homers and lost his command during a two-run third inning, walking in a run. Weaver is 1-1 with a 5.19 ERA in five career starts against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Before and after the left hip strain that cost him two months of action, Fausto Carmona hasn't been the same pitcher in 2008 that he was in '07. He's lost precise command of his once-trusty sinker, as evidenced by the 51 walks he's issued in 71 innings. Four of those walks came in a rough no-decision against the Orioles on Monday, when Carmona also gave up seven runs on six hits with four strikeouts in 6 1/3 innings. He was staked to a big lead early, but couldn't hold on.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey showed his resolve in an uneven performance against the Yankees on Saturday, leaving two runners stranded on three occasions by striking out Xavier Nady, Derek Jeter and Alex Rodriguez. A-Rod and Jason Giambi hit back-to-back homers in the sixth, and three straight singles gave the Yanks a two-run lead that they would surrender. Lackey walked one and struck out five while scattering nine hits. Lackey is 4-5 in 11 career outings against the Indians and is a deceptive 2-2 at Progressive Field, with a 0.99 ERA in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers gave the Tribe another so-so outing Wednesday against the Tigers and, in turn, the young lefty received another no-decision. Sowers turned in 6 1/3 innings, giving up four runs on six hits and two walks. He found trouble early, allowing two quick runs, but settled down throughout the majority of the start before finding trouble again in his final inning of work. With the trade of Paul Byrd earlier in the week, Sowers has never had a sturdier spot in the Indians' rotation, and he will need to take advantage of it if he hopes to be in it next season. Sowers has yet to face the Angels this season, but all-time he is 0-1 with a 4.74 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bell was solid in his Major League debut, allowing four runs on nine hits over 5 1/3 innings along with four strikeouts and one walk against the Rays on Wednesday. The key was his efficiency as he threw just 75 pitches and first-pitch strikes to 20 of the 25 batters he faced. Tuesday will mark his first road start in the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: In his second start with the Indians, Reyes put together another solid start and likely solidified his place in the Tribe's ever-changing starting rotation. Over six innings, Reyes allowed two runs (both in the second inning) on six hits, but couldn't come up with the win as he wasn't given much run support. He didn't strike out a single batter in Wednesday's outing against the Orioles, but made up for it with a consistent approach that led to numerous groundouts. In his only start against the Royals, Reyes went 5 2/3 scoreless innings to pick up the win.
away_pitcher_note: Hochevar still hasn't won since July 11, when he beat Seattle. But he was tough against the White Sox in his last outing, holding them to five hits and three runs in his seven innings. He got 11 groundouts, an indication that he was on, and also struck out four. In two different stretches he got 10 and nine straight outs. Hochevar pitched against the Indians on May 3 at Cleveland and got the victory, holding them to two runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson didn't dazzle in his Tribe debut, but he certainly didn't have a meltdown. After allowing two quick runs in the first inning, the 25-year-old left-hander settled down and gave up just one more run to cap his five-inning effort. Not the flashiest pitcher, Jackson had to grind his way through the effort, failing to record a 1-2-3 inning throughout the 97-pitch outing. A National League product before he landed with the Tribe in the CC Sabathia trade, Jackson has never faced the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Meche pitched well enough to win on Friday night and left the game with a 3-1 lead over the Yankees. But the bullpen gave it up, and Meche took a no-decision, although the Royals came back to win. At least he extended his string of starts without a loss to eight; the right-hander is 4-0 with four no-decisions in that stretch. Meche rang up eight strikeouts against the Yankees and has 31 in his past four games, covering 25 1/3 innings. Meche has faced the Indians three times this season, going 1-1, but he hasn't seen them since May 30 �- before his season kicked into high gear.

home_pitcher_note: Lee had an average outing on Friday against the Angels. It just so happens that his personal average is extraordinary. Lee went the distance for the third time this year, holding the Angels to a mere two runs on eight hits, with two walks and six strikeouts. He induced four double-play balls, preserving his pitch count. In doing so, he became the AL's first 17-game winner and further helped his chances of becoming the Tribe's first 20-game winner in 34 years. Lee is 2-0 with a 2.40 ERA against the Royals this year.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke pitched well enough to win last Saturday at Yankee Stadium, allowing just two unearned runs in his 6 2/3 innings. Hurt by three errors in one inning, he got no decision as the game stretched into 13 innings and was won by the Yankees, 3-2. Greinke will try again to get into double-digit victories for the first time in his career against the Indians. This is the first time he'll face them this season. In his career, he's 3-6 with a 4.14 ERA against the Tribe.

home_pitcher_note: What was the most impressive stat from Harrison's last start? Take your pick. He had recorded just seven strikeouts in seven games entering the start and left after eight innings with eight strikeouts -- more than doubling his season total. Or there were the mere three baserunners he allowed -- all of which came on singles -- even though he entered the game with 19 walks against seven strikeouts. Finally, there were the 18 straight Rays he retired. Harrison is now 4-1 with a 4.03 ERA in his past five starts. Having allowed just two runs in his past two home starts, Harrison will try to continue his successful stretch at home in his first career start against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: In what has become a tough 2008 season for the young sinkerballer, there was, perhaps, something to build off in his most recent outing. Carmona went seven innings and allowed four runs (two earned) to the Angels on Saturday, but his command was better and he got back to keeping the ball on the ground, as he induced three ground-ball double plays. Carmona was the victim of some shaky defense, but he didn't do himself any favors either, uncorking two wild pitches and committing an error of his own in his fifth loss of the season. In his only outing of the season against the Rangers, Carmona lasted just two innings and gave up six runs before he was pulled with a strained hip, which would keep him on the disabled list for more than two months.

home_pitcher_note: At long last, McCarthy will join the Texas rotation. It will be his first start with the Rangers since Sept. 20 of last season, as severe right forearm inflammation has kept him on the shelf in 2008. Even after beginning a rehab assignment in July, McCarthy wasn't happy with his results. So, on Aug. 7, he made a trip to Rangers Ballpark in Arlington to meet with team president Nolan Ryan, pitching coach Andy Hawkins and bullpen coach Jim Colborn, who helped streamline McCarthy's mechanics. Since then, McCarthy has thrown 13 innings of shutout ball with 11 strikeouts and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Sowers did his usual thing on Sunday against the Angels. He allowed two early runs to lift his first-inning ERA to 9.60 before settling down to finish with another non-flashy 6 2/3 innings of work. He allowed three runs and scattered eight hits, walking two and striking out two to collect just his second win of the season. Sowers has yet to face the Rangers in his three-year career.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching after a 10-day layoff, Padilla was solid through six innings in his last start; until the seventh, he'd allowed just one run, five hits and a walk. In the seventh, though, he allowed a walk, a single and back-to-back home runs before exiting. Padilla had been bothered by inflammation in the right side of his neck, but the righty said after the game that the pain wasn't an issue. In his past five starts, Padilla is 1-2 with a 7.14 ERA. He will look to end that trend on Sunday in his first start against Cleveland this season. It won't be easy, though. He's 2-2 in five career starts with a 7.09 ERA against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes allowed just two runs for the second consecutive outing Tuesday against the Royals, but he couldn't get past the fifth inning because of a high pitch count. His three walks contributed to that, but the long at-bats he faced in the first inning, when he threw 27 pitches, ultimately led to his early exit. He went five innings, never had a 1-2-3 inning, scattered six hits and struck out three to set himself up to be the winning pitcher. Since he was brought up from Triple-A Buffalo, Reyes has worked 17 1/3 innings and allowed five runs. Reyes has never faced the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Now that Galarraga has dispensed his revenge on the Rangers for trading him last offseason by beating them last Tuesday, he'll try to get back to business as usual with a chance to beat Cleveland for the fourth time this season. The Indians have batted just .159 in three starts against him this year, during which he has lasted 17 2/3 innings. He's 4-0 in his last five starts, pushing him into a battle with former Tiger and current Atlanta Brave Jair Jurrjens for the Major League rookie wins lead this season.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson scuffled a bit in his second start since being called up from Triple-A Buffalo, but he gave the Tribe innings -- something he couldn't deliver in his first outing. Acquired in the trade that sent CC Sabathia to the Brewers, Jackson went seven innings and gave up five runs (four earned), which was more than enough to prevent him from picking up his first Major League win since July 17, 2006. Most of the damage came in a four-run fifth inning, where he surrendered a three-run double to Mike Aviles. Jackson has never faced the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers will purchase Lambert's contract from Triple-A Toledo to fill Nate Robertson's old spot in their rotation. It will mark the Major League debut of Lambert, a first-round pick of the Cardinals in the 2004 First-Year Player Draft who came to the Tigers system last summer in the Mike Maroth trade. He owns a 12-8 record and 3.50 ERA in 26 starts for the Mud Hens, including three complete games and a shutout. He ranks fifth in the International League in ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lee notched his American League-best 18th win of the season on Thursday with yet another quality start. The 29-year-old took a no-hitter into the fifth inning, ultimately saw it disappear and then proceeded to allow three runs, before settling down to escape after seven innings with just the three runs of damage. Lee skirted trouble throughout, inducing four double plays, but he was still able to strike out seven batters. Lee is just two wins shy of becoming the Indians' first 20-game winner since Gaylord Perry accomplished the feat in 1974. In two starts against the Tigers this season, Lee is 1-0 with a 7.20 ERA -- largely the result of a five-inning, six-run outing on July 31. Lifetime, Lee is 4-6 with a 5.46 ERA in 16 starts against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: The young right-hander, who has struggled for much of this year, has gotten back on a little bit of  a roll lately with back-to-back wins. His victory against the Royals on Friday saw him display some of the better mix of pitch selections that he's had this summer, including a good dose of curveballs. If he can take that into his latest meeting with the Indians, he'll give himself a better chance than he has lately against a club that has hit him well. He's 4-8 with a 6.51 ERA lifetime against Cleveland, including 1-3 with a 5.84 ERA in four starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona was arguably as sharp as he's been all season his last time out against a potent Rangers lineup. In six innings, he allowed an unearned run on six hits and three walks and struck out five. It was just his fourth start of the season where his struck out more batters than he walked -- and his first since July 31. It was also his first victorious outing since that July 31 start against the Tigers, who Carmona will be facing his next time out. Wednesday will be his third start of the season against Detroit and he'll be going for his third victory against the Tigers this season. In 13 innings against Detroit in 2008, Carmona has a 2.08 ERA and five strikeouts to two walks.

home_pitcher_note: The Cleveland offense saved Sowers from earning his seventh loss of the season. Against the Rangers in a tough park for pitchers, Sowers allowed seven runs on eight hits and a walk and struck out only two in 3 2/3 innings. Manager Eric Wedge said Sowers struggled out of the stretch and that was evident when he allowed six runs in the fourth inning and couldn't get out of it. But he was solid early on, which hasn't always been the case. He faced the minimum through the first two innings and Texas manufactured a run off him in the third before its big innings. Sowers' next start will be against the Mariners, against whom he earned one of his two victories this season. It wasn't a glorious victory though as he allowed four runs in six innings in the start.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez pitched six innings in his last start, against the Athletics on Sunday, and struck out seven. The mistakes he made ended up in the seats, as all three runs allowed came on solo homers. Hernandez threw 106 pitches (67 strikes) and picked up the win. In his last start against the Indians, on July 18, Hernandez gave up two earned runs in six innings and struck out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes did everything he could to earn a victory his last time out except go the distance. He pitched his longest outing of the season, seven innings, and tallied his highest pitch count of the year, 107 pitches. Those were the only high numbers he put up, though, holding the Rangers to just one run on four hits and four walks as he struck out four. He left in line for his third victory in four starts with the Indians, but the bullpen didn't hold his lead. Saturday will be Reyes' first career start against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn makes his final start of August still looking for his first win in the month. The veteran has lost all five of his starts this month, and the latest one was the 100th of his Major League career. Three of the losses occurred in games in which he surrendered three or fewer runs in at least six innings -- a quality start. Since the start of the 2005 season, he has the lowest run support among American League starters. This will be his second start of the season against the Indians, who beat him in Cleveland on April 30.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson notched his third no-decision in as many starts with the Indians on Monday in Detroit, though he certainly deserved a better fate. In 6 1/3 innings of work, Jackson limited the Tigers to three runs on seven hits with no walks and six strikeouts. He served up a pair of home runs, but both were solo shots. Jackson, who has never faced the Mariners, did a good job commanding his fastball and has shown improvement with his breaking and offspeed pitches.
away_pitcher_note: The Australian left-hander picked up his first career win as a starting pitcher in his outing Tuesday against the Twins. He went seven innings for the second straight start, allowing two runs and just five hits. The 25-year-old has looked solid in three of his four starts since returning from Triple-A Tacoma, where he went for a few weeks to stretch his arm out in late July. In two appearances out of the bullpen against the Indians this season, Rowland-Smith has given up one earned run over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lee has put himself in a position to become the Indians' first 20-game winner since Gaylord Perry in 1974. Already, Lee has put himself in historic company, as he is just the eighth pitcher since 1920 to start a season 19-2 or better, according to Stats Inc. Lee has done it with impeccable command of his fastball and unshakable confidence in his stuff. He limited the Tigers to a pair of runs on six hits with a walk and four strikeouts in 7 2/3 innings on Tuesday. He'll be facing a White Sox team that he limited to a run over eight innings in a no-decision on July 1.
away_pitcher_note: Ozzie Guillen on Saturday anointed Richard as the man to open the Cleveland series on Monday against Cy Young frontrunner Cliff Lee. That honor held through Richard's one-inning relief effort later that night against the Red Sox, which was used as a side session in between starts. The left-hander earned his second straight win since getting called back up from Triple-A Charlotte, pushing the White Sox past the Orioles on Monday night at Camden Yards. Richard allowed three runs on six hits over six innings, fanning four.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona had an uneven outing against the Tigers on Wednesday, but he got enough support to earn the victory. In six innings of work, Carmona allowed four runs on seven hits with three walks and three strikeouts. He had trouble locating his sinker early but he settled in late. Carmona is at his best when he doesn't try to overthrow that sinkerball. The pitch has better action when he lets it flow out of his hand, rather than forcing it. He'll be facing a White Sox team he held to a run on four hits in seven innings in a victory in his first start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Wednesday's 11-3 loss at Baltimore served as one of the few negative moments from what has been an outstanding season to date for the left-hander. Danks allowed four runs on seven hits over four innings, his shortest outing since July 20 against Kansas City. Danks struck out one, walked three and needed 93 pitches to complete his work. Danks has no record in two starts against Cleveland this season but only has allowed two runs over 14 2/3 innings when facing the Indians in 2008. Danks has a 1-2 career record against Cleveland and a 1-1 mark at Progressive Field. He also will receive an extra day's rest, having his start pushed back from Monday to Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers had some trouble locating his pitches against the Mariners on Friday night. While he avoided major damage, he didn?t last long. He needed 95 pitches to get through five innings in which he allowed three runs on seven hits with no walks or strikeouts and one homer. It was another short outing for Sowers, who lasted just 3 2/3 innings in his previous start against the Rangers. He'll look to go deeper against the White Sox, who roughed him up for eight runs (three earned) in three innings in a loss on June 30.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez gave up five runs, three earned, on 10 hits over 5 2/3 innings on Friday in an 8-0 loss at Fenway Park to the Red Sox. But even if Vazquez had given up just one run, as he did once before during a setback in Boston, it probably would have been one too many with the way Daisuke Matsuzaka was pitching. Vazquez did strike out seven and walked two in suffering his second straight loss to an American League East playoff contender. Vazquez has a 1-1 record with a 4.50 ERA against the Indians this season and holds a 6-4 lifetime mark when facing Cleveland, including a 3-3 record at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Duckworth has fashioned two victories in two starts against the Tigers since being recalled from Triple-A Omaha. Last Saturday, he pitched six innings and gave up three runs in a blowout victory. Oddly all three runs scored as a result of leadoff triples and groundouts. In nearly five months with Omaha, he was 5-11 with a 4.75 ERA. Duckworth has faced the Indians four times in his career, all in 2007, with a 1-0 record and 2.84 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes deserved a better fate than a no-decision in his outing against the Mariners on Saturday. He worked seven strong innings in which he allowed just one run -- a Tug Hulett solo homer -- on seven hits with a walk and three strikeouts. Reyes has been solid since joining the Tribe's rotation on Aug. 8, and this was his best start yet. He worked both sides of the plate and had effective command of all his pitches. Reyes gave up two runs in five innings to get a win over the Royals on Aug. 19.

home_pitcher_note: Meche rebounded nicely from a rare off-day when he held the powerful Tigers to two runs in seven innings on Sunday. However, he left with the score tied and had no decision in a Royals loss. Meche has pitched very well since a rocky start. Since June 10, for example, he's 7-2 with a 2.97 ERA in 16 starts. This season, he's faced the Indians four times with a 1-1 record and a 4.84 ERA, most of that from eight runs in 3 1/3 innings of his loss back in April.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson suffered his first Major League loss Sunday against the Mariners in which he was done in by a five-run fifth inning. His own throwing error didn't help his cause. Jackson allowed six runs and seven hits in five innings. He did strike out five and issued only one walk. He gave up two home runs to Adrian Beltre, a solo shot in the second and a two-run blast that finished off the fifth. Jackson had no-decisions in his first three starts with the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke picked up his 10th victory with seven solid innings against the A's on Tuesday night. Although four of the six hits were for extra bases, he walked just one and struck out eight. That gave him 159 strikeouts, the most the Royals have had since Kevin Appier's 196 in 1997. Greinke is continuing to throw hard with good control. Of his 28 starts, 19 of them rank as "quality starts." This is Greinke's first appearance against the Indians this season; in his career, he's 3-6 with a 4.14 ERA in 15 outings against the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander continued his outstanding season Monday by winning his 20th game, a 5-0 shutout of the White Sox. Lee's 20-2 record gives him a .909 winning percentage, tops in the American League. His only losses have come to the Reds on May 18 and the Twins on July 6. He leads the league in wins, winning percentage and ERA (2.32). He also has won nine straight decisions, which is tied for the longest streak in the league. Lee has allowed two or fewer earned runs in 21 of his 27 starts. He also has two complete games and four shutouts.

home_pitcher_note: Olson got lit up for six earned runs in his return from Triple-A Norfolk, but two of those runs scored after he had left the game. The southpaw has had major difficulty getting Major Leaguers out since the All-Star break, and O's manager Dave Trembley wants to see him command his fastball more and stick with it through the later innings.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona was cruising early in a victory over the White Sox on Tuesday, but he gave up three runs in the sixth and didn't make it out of the inning. Those three runs were all he allowed in 5 2/3 innings of work. This season has been an uphill battle for Carmona, who missed two months with a left hip strain. His command of his sinker has been inconsistent from outing to outing and, sometimes, from inning to inning. Still, he's been able to string together three straight victories. Carmona was 2-0 with a 0.59 ERA in two starts against the O's last year.

home_pitcher_note:
After his latest outing -- another short start where the right-hander allowed copious amounts of 
runs early -- Liz is likely glad to be getting his next start inside the confines of Camden Yards. Although he has 
not been stellar at home this season -- Liz has a 6.03 ERA in Baltimore -- he has been markedly better than his 
performances on the road, where he's pitched to a 10.96 ERA. In his last start on Tuesday -- his second straight 
tough outing inside Fenway Park -- Liz saw his overall ERA rise almost a full run after allowing nine earned runs 
over 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sowers cruised early but hung two fastballs that resulted in home runs against the White Sox on Wednesday. In all, he gave up four runs on six hits with one walk and five strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings to take a loss. Sowers has shown spurts of his 2006 self this season, but he's struggled to put complete outings together. He allowed four runs in 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision against the Orioles on Aug. 12.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Waters worked into the sixth inning for just the third time in seven outings, but he lost control late in the game and watched as the relievers walked home four runs in the eighth inning. Waters has held his own as a stopgap starter, and he's pitched at three different levels this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians are skipping Anthony Reyes, who was originally scheduled to make this start, after he experienced right elbow tightness and soreness on Friday night in Kansas City. The starting nod will now go to Double-A Akron left-hander Scott Lewis, who was active with the Aeros in the postseason. Lewis was 6-2 with a 2.33 ERA in 13 starts for Akron and 2-2 with a 2.63 ERA in four starts for Triple-A Buffalo this season. This will be the Major League debut for the third-round Draft pick from 2004.

home_pitcher_note: The Orioles acquired Bass on Sept. 5 from Minnesota and immediately added the right-hander to the Major League roster. Bass has never started in the Major Leagues but will be called on to do so with the Orioles pushing ace Jeremy Guthrie back to Saturday to recover from the flu. Bass went four innings once this season in relief, but it was all the way back in April, so the length of his outing will be questionable at best. Bass has made one appearance as an Oriole, pitching an 1 2/3 innings and allowing two earned runs off no hits and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson is still searching for that elusive first win with the Indians. He turned in a quality start against the Royals on Saturday, allowing three runs on nine hits with no walks and two strikeouts in seven innings, but he still suffered the loss. All three runs came in the second inning, and Jackson got more aggressive around the plate from that point forward. The lack of wins aside, Jackson, acquired in the CC Sabathia trade, has been a pleasant surprise for the Tribe in five starts. He'll look to nail down that win against an Orioles team that notched three runs off him in five innings in his Tribe debut on Aug. 14.

home_pitcher_note: Lee already became the Tribe's first 20-game winner since 1974, and now he has a chance to become their winningest left-hander of all-time. The honor currently rests with Vean Gregg, who won 23 games in 1911. Lee became the Majors' first 21-game winner since the Marlins' Dontrelle Willis in 2005 with 7 1/3 strong innings against the Royals on Sunday. He allowed just one run on seven hits, with a walk and five strikeouts, to improve to 4-0 with a 2.15 ERA in four starts against the Royals this season.
away_pitcher_note: Meche was sharp on Saturday in a 3-1 win over the Indians, striking out 10 and giving up just one run on three hits in seven innings. Meche credited the increased use of a changeup against right-handed hitters with helping his strikeout total, which has reached a career high of 158. The right-hander's ERA is below 4.00 for the first time all season. This will Meche's sixth start against the Tribe this year. He's 2-1 in his previous five outings, having allowed eight earned runs in the first of those starts but just four earned runs in his past four.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona turned in another unpredictable outing in a loss to the Orioles on Monday. He had plenty of potential trouble for his first five innings of work, but he limited the damage to a pair of runs. Then he completely hit a wall in the sixth, walking three batters and giving up two hits. He was charged with seven runs on six hits with four walks and five strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings. Carmona has had a tendency to overthrow this season, and it's hurt him consistently. He gave up four runs in five innings in a win over the Royals on April 24.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke, as he has so many times, pitched well enough to win on Sunday against the Indians. But he ran into Cliff Lee, who prevailed, 3-1, for his 21st victory of the season. Greinke did run up his pitch count a little more than usual -- throwing 105 pitches in six innings -- but he allowed just five hits and struck out eight. The right-hander had trouble controlling his four-seam fastball, which threw him off and forced him to resort to his two-seamer. This will be Greinke's third start against the Tribe this year, and he has lost both previous times to Lee.

home_pitcher_note: Bullington, the former No. 1 overall pick of the Pirates in the 2002 Draft, and one of many reclamation projects the Indians had going at Triple-A Buffalo, will make a spot start. Because Buffalo's season ended Sept. 1, the Indians weren't expected to call on any of the Bisons for this start. But Bullington, who was on the 40-man roster already, started that final game on Labor Day, and he threw a bullpen session Monday. He was 1-3 with a save and a 4.75 ERA in 10 games, including eight starts, for Buffalo. While with the Pirates' Triple-A club in Indianapolis earlier this year, he was 4-6 with a 5.52 ERA in 15 starts before he was designated for assignment on July 3.
away_pitcher_note: Tejeda will likely make the spot start in Saturday's nightcap. The game, however, will be shared by numerous members of the bullpen, manager Trey Hillman said. The skipper mentioned Kip Wells and Joel Peralta as candidates to pitch a few innings. Tejeda is 1-2 with a 3.31 ERA in 23 relief appearances with the Royals this year and was 5-9 with a 6.61 ERA in 19 starts for Texas last year.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers had his best stuff and his best start of the season Tuesday in Baltimore, holding the Orioles to a mere run on four hits with a walk and a season-high seven strikeouts for his first win in four starts. Sowers has shown improved velocity on his fastball this season, but this start was the first where he showed consistent command of the pitch and consistent variation in speeds between his fastball and changeup. Sowers is 2-1 with a 2.50 ERA in three career starts against the Royals, but has not faced them this year.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister is winless in 13 consecutive starts. He was lit up by Minnesota for seven earned runs on 10 hits in 3 2/3 innings on Tuesday. There was optimism surrounding a Bannister resurgence after he had made three consecutive effective starts prior to the poor start against the Twins. Bannister will next conclude a four-game weekend series against the Indians. He is 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA in two starts against Cleveland this year.

home_pitcher_note: If Lewis is looking to improve on his big-league debut, he better be entertaining thoughts of a no-hitter. Lewis would have trouble topping what he accomplished against the Orioles on Wednesday. He limited them to just four hits with no walks and three strikeouts in eight scoreless innings. All that separated him from a potential shutout was a closely watched pitch count, as he was held at 97. Lewis was called up from the playoffs at Double-A Akron to fill in for an injured Anthony Reyes. He doesn't have overpowering stuff, but he has impeccable command when he's on, and he was certainly on against the O's.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander delivered his 12th quality start in 24 outings this season when he faced the Royals his last time out. Slowey held Kansas City to just one run on four hits over his seven innings. He continues to limit his number of walks in outings and show improvement in his ability to recover from early troubles. Slowey will see if he can continue that trend in Cleveland when he faces the Indians for the third time this season. Slowey is 1-1 against the Tribe, having allowed a total of 10 runs over 12 innings in his two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson has shown spurts of potential for the Tribe, but he's still searching for his first win and he's now lost three straight starts. His outing against the Orioles wasn't particularly pretty, as he allowed five runs -- four earned -- on eight hits with two walks and two strikeouts in six innings. He needed 92 pitches to get through the abbreviated outing. He'll look to be more efficient an effective against a Twins team he's never faced before.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano delivered yet another strong start for the Twins, pitching eight innings and allowing just two runs to the Royals, but he walked away with a no-decision. It was the first time that Liriano had pitched into the eighth inning this season for the Twins and marked his longest start since July 28, 2006 vs. Detroit. Next up for Liriano will be a start against the Indians at Progressive Field. Liriano has not been nearly as dominant on the road as he's been at home. Liriano is 1-2 with a 5.63 ERA in five road starts, including two very rough ones in his first stint with the club in April.

home_pitcher_note: Lee notched his 22nd win on Friday with another strong outing against the Royals. He went 8 1/3 innings before running into trouble in the ninth, allowing five runs on 11 hits. Lee has won each of his last 11 decisions since July 11. At 22-2, Lee is the first pitcher to be 20 games over .500 since Bob Welch was 27-6 in 1990. He is now just one win shy of becoming the Indians' winningest left-hander in a season. That honor currently belongs to Vean Gregg, who won 23 games in 1911. The Twins were the last team to beat Lee, but that hasn't happened since July 6. In three starts this season, Lee is 2-1 with a 2.35 ERA against Minnesota. Lifetime, he is 7-3 with a 3.74 ERA in 15 starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Baker was extremely effective in the early game of the Twins' doubleheader on Saturday, holding the Orioles to just one run on four hits over six innings. The right-hander was all set to come back out for the seventh, but a long top of the inning prevented Baker from running back out to the mound. Baker will be throwing on short rest, but manager Ron Gardenhire seemed convinced that of all the young pitchers on his staff, Baker would be the easiest hurler to do that with. Baker is 1-1 in three starts against the Indians this season, allowing seven earned runs in 18 combined innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona continued to prompt head scratches as he once again ran into trouble in the sixth inning on Saturday against the Royals. Staked to a 2-2 tie, the young right-hander gave up two quick runs, which stood to be enough for him to pick up his seventh loss of the season. In his last three outings, Carmona has given up 10 runs in the sixth inning. All told, he went 6 1/3 innings, allowing seven runs on 11 hits and three walks. Carmona has been dominant against the Tigers this season, picking up three wins in three appearances while allowing just seven runs over 19 innings pitched. Lifetime, Carmona has had similar success, going 6-2 with a 3.34 ERA in 11 appearances (eight starts).
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers wanted to give Galarraga some extra rest after he looked like he was tiring down the stretch over his last couple outings, but they weren't planning to sit him for this long. Thanks to rainouts at Chicago last Friday and Saturday, Galarraga hasn't pitched since giving up five runs over four innings against Oakland on Sept. 10. He hasn't won in his last four starts, but he'll get a chance to rebound against a Cleveland club he has beaten three times in four meetings this season.
