home_pitcher_note: Sowers continues to be a mystery this season, as he put up one of his shortest outings on Sunday against the Royals. Coming off his best start of the season, in which he held the Orioles to a run over eight innings, Sowers resumed his knack of nibbling to no avail and giving up big hits in tight situations. Over three innings and an obtuse 75 pitches, the 25-year-old left-hander gave up three runs on five hits to pick up a no-decision. In his two starts against Detroit this season, Sowers has labored, going 0-2 with a 10.24 ERA. Sowers is 1-3 with an 8.24 ERA in four career starts against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander gets the start after going 7 2/3 innings allowing four runs, all earned, on nine hits against the White Sox on Sunday, which he took the loss in. In 14 career starts against the Indians, Verlander is 4-9 with a 6.59 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Anthony Reyes, who was scheduled to make this start, was shut down for the rest of the season on Tuesday because of lingering inflammation in his right elbow. But the Indians certainly have a viable backup candidate in Lewis, who has made two starts in Reyes' place and has not allowed a single run. After tossing eight scoreless innings in his big-league debut against the Orioles on Sept. 10, Lewis worked six scoreless against the Twins on Monday, allowing just three hits with two walks and five strikeouts to get his second win. He gets by with less-than-electric stuff because of his precise command. Lewis will face the Tigers for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: In his first big league start since June 11, Willis had a solid game on Monday night against the Rangers. He went five innings, allowing three runs on two hits with four strikeouts and five walks. Both manager Jim Leyland and pitching coach Chuck Hernandez said they were pleased that Willis made progress. Although Willis was disappointed, the Tigers eventually lost the game, he said he felt good on the mound and left the clubhouse on a positive note. Willis will try and improve on that outing against the Tribe, a team he's 0-2 with a 7.42 ERA against in three lifetime starts.

home_pitcher_note: The ace has rediscovered his dominance since returning from the disabled list, allowing just two runs over 19 innings, going 1-0 in that span. Beckett's last start -- a no-decision against the Rays -- was one of his finest of the year. He allowed one run and three hits over eight innings, striking out eight. In 11 starts at Fenway this season, Beckett is 5-4 with a 5.61 ERA. This is Beckett's first start of the season against Cleveland. In his career against the Indians, Beckett is 1-3 with a 6.57 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson didn't look much better in his start Tuesday against the Twins, and was still unable to collect his first win of the season. Jackson, acquired in the CC Sabathia deal, has yet to show dazzling stuff since he was called up after the Paul Byrd trade. He went 5 1/3 innings, allowing seven runs on nine hits. After allowing a run in the first inning, Jackson gave up the bulk of the damage in a four-run fifth inning, when the Twins strung together a double and four singles to creep back into the once-lopsided game. This will be Jackson's first action against Boston.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer has been hit hard in two out of his last three starts, both of which were fewer than three innings. Most recently, Wakefield gave up six hits and six runs in 2 1/3 innings of a loss to the Tampa Bay Rays. But the start in between was perhaps his finest of the year, when he reeled off eight shutout innings in a win over the Blue Jays. Wakefield last pitched against the Indians on April 15, when he gave up seven hits and two runs over six innings in a no-decision at Progressive Field. Wakefield has pitched well at Fenway this year, going 6-4 with a 3.08 ERA in 12 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lee's bid to become the Majors' first 23-game winner since 2002 fell short Wednesday, when he gave up four runs (three earned) on 10 hits, with three walks and five strikeouts in a no-decision against the Twins. But he's still undefeated in his last 13 starts, going 11-0 with a 2.40 ERA in that span, and he's still just the fourth pitcher since 1900 to win 22 of his first 24 decisions. He'll take another shot at No. 23, which would tie the club record for most wins by a left-hander, when he faces the Red Sox. Lee is 2-3 with a 4.91 ERA in seven career starts against Boston and 1-1 with a 5.51 ERA in three starts at Fenway Park.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander produced a quality start in his last outing, giving up three runs over six innings in a no-decision against the Blue Jays. For Byrd, this will be his first start against the Indians since being traded by Cleveland to the Red Sox on Aug. 12. For the Indians this season, Byrd was 7-10 with a 4.53 ERA. Byrd is 4-2 in seven starts since joining the Red Sox. Only once since coming to Boston has Byrd gone fewer than six innings. In three Fenway starts, Byrd is 1-2 with a 6.05 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona has appealed a six-game suspension for his role in Friday's bench-clearing brawl with the Tigers and, barring a quick appeals process, will make his final start of '08. Before he duked it out with Gary Sheffield in the seventh inning, Carmona showed much improvement from what he's done in what has become a disappointing 2008 campaign. The right-hander commanded the strike zone and induced a number of ground balls by locating his nasty sinker where he wanted it. His tendency to overthrow in tight situations wasn't a problem because, well, he didn't have many to deal with. His only problem was Miguel Cabrera, who knocked a pair of two-run homers off Carmona before the righty was ejected after 6 1/3 innings. Carmona has yet to face the Red Sox this season, but is 1-2 with a 5.00 ERA in three career appearances (one start).

home_pitcher_note: Lester will make the final start of what has been a breakout regular season. The lefty had mixed results in his last outing. After putting his team in a 5-0 hole after two innings at Toronto, Lester was unscored on for the final five runs of his outing. He has been nothing short of brilliant at Fenway Park this season, going 10-1 with a 2.54 ERA in 16 starts. Lester last pitched against the Indians on April 14, giving up five hits and four runs over 4 1/3 innings of a no-decision. Lester will add to his career-high total of 204 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sowers' up-and-down season hit a bit of a peak Saturday against the Tigers, when the left-hander worked six solid innings to pick up his fourth win of the season. After allowing a quick run in the first inning, Sowers settled down and allowed just two hits over the next five innings, retiring the final seven batters he faced in order. All told, Sowers went six innings, allowed just the one run on five hits, with three strikeouts and two walks. Sowers has yet to face the Red Sox this season, but is 0-1 with a 5.06 ERA in two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Danks responded to the challenge of what Ozzie Guillen dubbed as the team's biggest game of the year by throwing seven scoreless innings during the White Sox 3-0 victory Sunday at Kauffman Stadium. Danks allowed four hits in seven-plus innings, striking out three and walking one, extending his scoreless innings streak to 13 straight. He threw 62 of his 90 pitches for strikes and will come back Friday on regular rest in a start that could lock down the American League Central title. Danks has a 0-1 record and 2.89 ERA in three starts against the Indians this season and is 4-5 with a 3.46 ERA at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis showed that he is, in fact, human in his third career start on Sunday, though he was still able to pick up his third win in as many opportunities. Lewis worked five innings and gave up three runs in the Indians' big win over the Tigers. His 15-inning scoreless inning streak was snapped in the second inning, when he allowed a run in on a double play. Lewis was finally touched up for his first career home run when Edgar Renteria launched one in his final inning of work. Surprisingly, though, Lewis, not known for his velocity or nasty stuff, picked up six strikeouts to go along with three walks. This will be Lewis' first career start against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Since the White Sox find themselves only one-half game out, Vazquez will throw on short rest Saturday. Pitching with an ear infection on Tuesday, the right-hander was tagged for five earned runs on seven hits over four innings. He struck out three and walked one, exiting after 78 pitches, shortening him up for Saturday's return. Vazquez has a 2-1 record with a 4.13 ERA against the Indians this season, and has a 7-6 record at U.S. Cellular Field, but he lost his last start on three days' rest, at Yankee Stadium. In his career, Vazquez is 0-3 with a 6.32 ERA in three starts on short rest.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson turned in the best of his eight starts for the Tribe on Monday night in Boston, and he has his first win as a member of the Indians to show for it. In six innings, Jackson allowed just two runs on six hits with four walks and four strikeouts. Had a potential RBI double by Jeff Bailey not instead hit the third-base umpire and resulted in a bizarre putout, the damage off Jackson might have been worse. But this outing still showed him making some big pitches in big situations. He will face the White Sox for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: It will be interesting to see how Buehrle comes back on three days rest after throwing a season-high 121 pitches in Wednesday's 3-2 loss to the Twins. But White Sox pitching coach Don Cooper said the earliest of plans has Buehrle working Sunday, if the White Sox still have not clinched or been eliminated. Buehrle allowed eighth hits and three runs on Wednesday, striking out three and walking four, as he battled his control all night. Buehrle has a 0-1 record and 9.22 ERA over three starts against the Indians this year, but he also features a 10-3 record with a 2.74 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Cy Young Award favorite Cliff Lee was scratched from this start because of neck stiffness. The Sox will instead run up against Bullington, a former No. 1 Draft pick of the Pirates who was a reclamation project at Triple-A Buffalo in the second half of this season. Bullington (0-1, 5.59 ERA) has made two appearances for the Indians in September -- a spotty spot start against the Royals on Sept. 13 and an outstanding bit of long relief work Wednesday night in Boston, when he worked five scoreless innings. Lee getting scratched was probably welcome news to the Sox, against whom he was 1-0 with a 0.53 ERA in two starts this season.

summary: 2009-03-24 - Chicago White Sox @ Cleveland Indians (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: Millwood is making his fourth straight Opening Day start for the Rangers but still looking for his first victory in that role. He is 0-3 with a 4.50 ERA in his past three Opening Day games. He pitched six strong innings last season against the Mariners at Safeco Field, taking a 1-0 lead into the sixth before allowing two unearned runs. The Rangers ended up losing 5-2. Millwood was 5-3 with a 5.09 ERA in 13 starts at home and is 20-14 with a 5.11 ERA in 45 starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington over the past three years. He went 1-2 with a 6.48 ERA this spring, allowing 30 hits and eight walks in 25 innings while striking out 19. But he made it through the spring without a physical setback for the first time in three years. Millwood pitched for the Indians in 2005 and won the American League ERA title before signing with the Rangers. He is 3-1 with a 4.56 ERA in four career starts against them. He made one start against them in 2008 and won, 9-4, on June 5, although he allowed four runs on nine hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: What will Lee do for an encore, after a remarkable '08 season in which he became the Indians' second Cy Young Award winner in as many years and their second 20-game winner in 34 years? The Indians aren't expecting Lee to turn in a duplicate of that campaign, but they do expect the 30-year-old Lee to be a steady, guiding hand at the top of the rotation. With former ace CC Sabathia long gone, the Indians are relying on Lee more than ever. They need him to set the tone for a rotation that enters the season with no shortage of question marks and concerns. Lee certainly has the mentality for the job, as his unshakable consistency, in terms of fastball command and aggressiveness, carried him to new heights in '08. He was one of just seven pitchers since 1920 to win 22 of his first 25 decisions, and his ERA was the lowest by an AL left-hander this decade. There will, however, be a worry that Lee's career-high workload (223 1/3 innings) could affect him in '09. Lee had a rough Spring Training camp, performance-wise, but he attributed most of his struggles to working on locating his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla went 0-2 with a 4.80 ERA in four Spring Training outings. He was 3-2 with a 3.79 ERA in six April starts in 2008, but is 13-19 with a 4.09 ERA in his career in April. That's his worst won-loss record for any month. He ended up winning 14-plus games for the fourth time in his career and was the Rangers' Pitcher of the Year. He is 2-2 with a 6.82 ERA in six career starts against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Two Carmonas exist -- the guy who used his sinking, 97-mph fastball to great effect in 2007, when he won 19 games and finished third in the Cy Young voting, and the guy who overthrew that sinker with disastrous consequences in his brief closing stint in '06 and his unremarkable '08. Carmona had a hip strain that held him out of action for two months last year, and that was no doubt part of his problem. But the Indians also believe he had trouble controlling his emotions. He showed much better control of himself and his pitches in spring camp, so the Tribe has high hopes for him going forward. They'll need a strong season from him in the No. 2 spot of the rotation if they're going to contend. Carmona was 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA in two starts against Texas last year.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy missed most of last season with severe right elbow inflammation and made just five starts for the Rangers. He made just 22 starts and one relief appearance for Texas in 2007, when he went 5-10 with a 4.87 ERA. For his career, McCarthy is 10-14 with 4.56 ERA in 39 starts with the Rangers and White Sox; McCarthy is 4-2 with a 4.58 ERA in 13 career games against the Indians, who are the only team McCarthy has beaten more than once.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano is the mystery man of the Indians' rotation. It's difficult to predict what the Tribe can expect from a guy who has only logged 45 2/3 innings in the Majors over the past three seasons. A bust in four years that cost the Yankees $40 million, Pavano is looking to repair his reputation and rejuvenate his career with an Indians team that believes he can still be effective, if healthy. Pavano, who won 18 games for the Marlins in '04, returned from Tommy John elbow surgery at the end of last season and made seven starts. And he made it through the Tribe's Spring Training camp with no body woes. His stuff improved as camp went along, so the Indians are encouraged. Pavano has never faced the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis beat out five other candidates for this spot in the rotation by displaying the type of fastball command that won him four games in as many starts at the big-league level last September. But after being named to the rotation, Lewis' spring stats quickly derailed, as he gave up 15 runs on 21 hits in his last 6 2/3 innings of Cactus League play. Lewis is a finesse lefty who needs to have precise command to be effective, because he doesn't have dominant stuff. When he's on, he can be brilliant, as evidenced by the eight scoreless innings he tossed against the Orioles in his Major League debut. He has never faced the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Richmond -- a rookie at 29 years old -- opens the season in Toronto's rotation after making just five starts for the club in his first professional season in 2008. Richmond is a native of North Vancouver, British Columbia, and was signed as a non-drafted free agent two winters ago following three years in the Independent League with the Edmonton Cracker Cats. Richmond opened his first pro tour at Double-A and was quickly moved to Triple-A and then to the big leagues. Richmond had an inconsistent spring after missing time for the World Baseball Classic, but the Jays decided to hand him the fifth spot over prospect Brad Mills.

home_pitcher_note: Lee will be kept on four days' rest for this start, with fifth starter Anthony Reyes held back a day. He's coming off a rough Opening Day loss against the Rangers, as he gave up seven runs on 10 hits with a walk and five strikeouts in five innings. This followed a spring in which he posted a 12.46 ERA, so there are certainly concerns about his effectiveness at this early juncture. Lee didn't give up his seventh run of the '08 season until his eight start of the season -- on May 18. He is 1-3 with 4.02 ERA in seven career starts against the Blue Jays. Last season, he went 1-0 against them, giving up no earned runs in 17 innings over two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay took the mound at Rogers Centre on Monday for his seventh consecutive Opening Day start, extending his own club record for season-opening outings. Doc was sharp through six innings, allowing just two hits among the first 20 batters he faced. Working with an ample cushion of run support, though, Halladay slipped some in the seventh inning, surrendering four runs -- two on a homer to Detroit's Brandon Inge. Even so, Halladay picked up his third Opening Day win, tying a franchise record. He finished with two strikeouts, one walk and 11 outs on ground balls. Halladay is 5-2 with a 3.73 ERA in 12 career games against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired in a midseason trade with the Cardinals last year, Reyes wowed the Indians with his performance in August, when his 2.01 ERA was the third-best in the AL. But Reyes comes with a catch, in the form of a chronic elbow condition that will have to be monitored all season. The Indians are aiming to protect him by placing him in their fifth rotation spot. Reyes tweaked his mechanics over the offseason, and he had a healthy and effective spring camp. He is best remembered for pitching the Cardinals to a victory in Game 1 of the 2006 World Series, but he hopes to keep his elbow in check and make a new name for himself with the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: In his season debut on Tuesday, Purcey gave the Blue Jays exactly what they need from him this season. The left-hander lasted seven innings, yielding three runs -- two earned -- on five hits with five strikeouts and three walks. Purcey, who finished with 101 pitches -- 61 strikes -- didn't use his changeup once, opting to stick with an array of fastballs, sliders and curves. When he did slip out of the strike zone, Purcey was able to correct himself quickly and limit the damage. Purcey faced the Indians once last season, allowing three runs on six hits over six innings in a losing effort.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke began his season with a shutout bang, holding the White Sox scoreless on three hits through six-plus innings. That was a welcome relief after Greinke's up-and-down Cactus League experience (3-3 but with a 9.21 ERA), the inconsistency partly attributable to his constant experimentation with his pitches. Greinke has pitched against the Indians 18 times in his career, more than any other club except the White Sox (also 18), and has a 4-8 record and 4.04 ERA against the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: The progress the Indians both want and need to see from Carmona was not on display in his first start of the season against the Rangers. Carmona lasted just five innings, giving up six runs on seven hits, including a homer, with two walks and four strikeouts. His command wasn't what it needs to be if he's going to be successful. Carmona is 4-1 with a 4.31 ERA in nine career starts against the Royals, including a 1-1 record and 8.74 ERA in two starts last year.

home_pitcher_note: If anyone was skeptical that Davies could carry his September 2008 success into April 2009 got an eyeful last Thursday at Chicago. Davies whizzed through seven shutout innings, allowing the White Sox just three hits. He also walked just two (Carlos Quentin twice) and matched his career strikeout best with eight. The Royals won the game in the ninth so Davies got no decision but he was so sharp he didn't face more than four batters in any inning. He was pulled after 103 pitches. His career mark against Cleveland is 1-3 but the victory came the only time he faced the Tribe last year.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano's Tribe debut was a brutal one. He allowed nine runs on six hits with three walks, two homers and a strikeout in one-plus inning. All that damage occurred on just 39 pitches. Pavano had trouble locating his pitches, and he continually fell behind in the count. He made it through spring camp healthy, but he clearly has some mechanical issues to address. Pavano is 0-1 with a 10.50 ERA in two career appearances against the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson had the difficult task of facing the Yankees in his first start of the year. And he had the extra pressure of taking the mound on the same day Kansas City reopened Kauffman Stadium. Still, Ponson came away with a positive review from Royals' manager Trey Hillman. He went six innings and gave up four runs, while striking out five. Now Ponson faces another test in the Cleveland Indians, a team Ponson has never beaten in his Major League career. Ponson is 0-7 with a 9.15 ERA in 13 appearances against the Indians. The right-hander, who made the Royals rotation during Spring Training, will probably need a better outing against the Indians this time to impress Hillman again.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey was in the competition for a spot in the Indians' rotation toward the end of Spring Training, but wound up starting the season at Triple-A Columbus. As the  AL Rookie of the Month for May 2008, Laffey worked 34 innings with an 0.79 ERA. The Indians would love for the diminutive left-hander to flash that form again as he takes the rotation spot of Scott Lewis, who is on the disabled list with a strained left forearm. Laffey surrendered six hits and five earned runs over 3 1/3 innings in his initial Triple-A start and doesn't have a commitment to remain in the Indians rotation beyond this start.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia draws the call for the first game at the new Yankee Stadium, coming in hot on the afterglow of a sparkling performance against the Royals in his second Yankees start. Sabathia was in control of Kansas City from the first pitch, firing 7 2/3 innings of scoreless ball with six strikeouts and was left wondering why manager Joe Girardi was coming out with the hook after 108 pitches. The difference from his Opening Day start came with a tweak from the bullpen, where Sabathia plants his right foot sooner and stays on top of his fastball better. Sabathia will be facing his former Indians club for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Lee has become just the second Cy Young winner in the last 10 years to lose both of his first two starts the following season (Roy Halladay was the other, in '04). Already, Lee has given up 11 runs on 17 hits in 10 innings of work. He didn't give up his 11th run of '08 until his eighth start and 59th inning pitched. Lee showed some improvement against the Blue Jays on Saturday, but he still only lasted five innings, allowing four runs on seven hits with four walks and five strikeouts. He needs to improve his fastball command to become more efficient. Lee is 3-3 with a 5.63 ERA in seven career starts against the Yankees, but he blanked them for seven innings in a win in New York last April.

home_pitcher_note: Chamberlain's first start of 2009 showcased plenty of reasons why the Yankees would want him in their rotation, as he hurled six solid frames in a no-decision on Sunday at Kansas City. Beginning the year as the Yankees' fifth starter, Chamberlain allowed three runs (one earned) on four hits, walking one and striking out five. He hit two batters and served up a third-inning home run to John Buck in the 88-pitch outing, but was ultimately pleased with his improving command and efficiency. Chamberlain will be making his first career start vs. Cleveland, though is 0-1 with a 4.50 ERA in five regular season relief appearances against them. And then, of course, there's the 2007 AL Division Series 'midge' game, when Chamberlain allowed the tying run in New York's Game 2 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes' final line against the Blue Jays on Sunday wasn't truly indicative of how well he pitched. He went six innings, allowing four runs on three hits with three walks, two strikeouts and two wild pitches. Most importantly, he became the first Tribe starter this season to last longer than five innings and the first to earn a victory. He had good command of his fastball and generally worked ahead. Reyes has never faced the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Wang took a pounding in his last start, charged with eight runs and chased in the second inning on April 13 at Tropicana Field. For a second consecutive outing, Wang was unable to keep his sinker down in the zone and paid the price, serving up six hits while walking three -- including a bases-loaded free pass to Evan Longoria on the last of his 61 pitches. Wang was 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA in two starts against Cleveland last season, hurling seven innings of scoreless, four-hit ball on April 27 at Progressive Field, and is 3-2 with a 2.97 ERA in five regular season career starts vs. the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona endured a rough first inning in his last start at Kansas City, using 42 pitches as the Royals scored three runs. But he battled back to get through five innings on 106 pitches. Carmona said he had such movement on his pitches that the ball was jumping out of the strike zone early. He'll try to fine-tune his repertoire and get back the consistency which made him such a sensation in 2007 when he finished with 19 wins and was fourth in the AL Cy Young voting.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett has proven to be a horse in his first two turns through the rotation, logging victories in both of his starts as a Yankee. He last started Tuesday at Tampa Bay and carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning, showcasing dominant command of his pitches and striking out nine in a 103-pitch performance. Burnett allowed two runs on three hits in the start, with Carl Crawford busting up the bid with a single to left leading off the seventh. Burnett lost his only start against the Indians in 2008, allowing three runs in 7 2/3 innings on May 12 at Progressive Field while pitching for the Blue Jays. He is 1-4 with a 7.20 ERA in five career starts against the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano made big strides from his first outing to the second. After allowing nine runs in an inning-plus at Texas, the veteran delivered six innings and fanned eight on Tuesday in Kansas City. Although he allowed four earned runs and took a loss, Pavano looked more like the impressive pitcher the Indians had seen in Spring Training. Manager Eric Wedge liked the way Pavano used both sides of the plate with his fastball and dropped in his slider against the Royals. The eight strikeouts marked Pavano's highest total since June 27, 2004.

home_pitcher_note: Frustrated over losing the battle for the Tribe's last rotation spot in spring camp, Laffey got an early, unexpected opportunity to come back to the big leagues when Scott Lewis strained his left forearm. Laffey made the most of the opportunity against the Royals last Wednesday, holding them to a pair of runs on three hits with five strikeouts over 5 1/3 inning for a no-decision. And in doing so, he's earned himself a second start against Kansas City. The key for Laffey is getting command of his sinker for ground-ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: Ponson still hasn't beaten the Indians in his career, but at least last Wednesday he pitched well against them. He held the Tribe to two runs on six hits in six innings in what became a 5-4 K.C. loss. He's still 0-7 against them with an 8.60 ERA in 14 games, including 13 starts. Ponson has done well enough in his two starts for the Royals. He also started the home opener against the Yankees and gave up four runs and six hits in six innings. Ponson has proved durable, throwing 104 pitches against the Yankees and 89 against the Indians. So far, no homers allowed. He's in better shape this year, shedding 22 pounds in the offseason.

home_pitcher_note: Lee finally showed his Cy Young stuff in his third start of the season against the Yankees on Thursday. He went six innings, allowing just a run on seven hits with three walks and four strikeouts to get his first win. The lone run came on a Jorge Posada solo shot. Efficiency is still an issue for Lee. The six-inning outing was his longest in three starts. He had to work himself out of some early jams, but his command, on the whole, was much improved. Lee is 12-4 with a 4.47 ERA in 19 career starts against the Royals, including a 5-0 record and 2.63 ERA in five starts last season.
away_pitcher_note: First it was Hector Ramirez dropped into this start, originally assigned to Gil Meche, in order to give Meche, Zack Greinke and Kyle Davies each an extra day of rest. Now it's Bannister, just recalled from Triple-A Omaha to reclaim the rotation spot that he lost in Spring Training. Bannister warmed up with two scoreless innings on Sunday for Omaha, giving him a string of nine shutout innings in his past two starts after a rough first outing. Bannister had a terrific rookie season for the Royals in 2007, when he went 12-9 with a 3.87 ERA, but then last year he slipped to 9-16 and a 5.76 ERA. Now he gets a shot at re-establishing himself against the Indians. He is 3-1 with a 1.91 ERA in his career against the Tribe, including 2-0 at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes turned in another decent, if not efficient, start against the Yankees on Friday. The only runs he allowed came on solo shots from Johnny Damon, Mark Teixeira and Melky Cabrera. Those were three of the five hits served up by Reyes in five innings in which he walked three and struck out one. On the whole, Reyes has done a decent job limiting the damage against him and avoiding the big inning. But the Indians could benefit from a little more efficiency from the right-hander. Reyes is 2-0 with a 1.32 ERA in three career appearances against the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Meche didn't have his best stuff in his last start, but he was still able to win one on Friday night in Texas, where he had lost six of his last seven decisions. Meche threw six shutout innings, allowing six hits. He relied mostly on his changeup, curveball and cutter because he never felt the fastball came out of his hand right on a damp night at Rangers Ballpark. Meche has pitched at least six innings in all three of his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Staked to 14 runs of support in the second inning Saturday in New York, Carmona was able to use his start as a work day, of sorts. He got his work in by going six innings, allowing four runs on six hits with four walks and a strikeout. He induced 11 groundball outs, so that's a sign that he had good action on his sinking fastball. But the walks continue to be a concern. He's walked more (10) than he's struck out (eight) this season -- a trend that began last year. Carmona is 3-3 with a 3.83 ERA in 10 career appearances against the Twins. He gave up nine runs in just 2 1/3 innings in his lone start against them last year.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn managed to pitch into the seventh inning in his last start, but once again, the Twins' offense couldn't produce early enough to get the right-hander a win. He allowed four runs on eight hits in 6 1/3 innings against the Angels, but it wasn't until a seven-run comeback in the eighth inning that the Twins pulled away. The club is 2-1 when Blackburn is on the hill and will hope to improve that record when the righty faces Cleveland at Progressive Field, where he is 1-0 with a 2.08 ERA in two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Silencing the wrath of Yankees fans still bitter about his four unfortunate years in New York, Pavano pitched a gem at Yankee Stadium on Sunday. He went six innings, allowing just a run on four hits with a walk and four strikeouts before the bullpen blew the game and saddled him with a no-decision. Pavano felt he didn't have his best fastball, but he got quality results from his slider and changeup. All in all, he's made major strides since allowing nine runs in one-plus inning of work in his Tribe debut in Texas on April 8.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Slowey finally found the form that he had during Spring Training. After allowing 22 hits in 10 1/3 innings in his first two starts of the season, Slowey held the Angels to just two runs on six hits in seven innings, lowering his ERA from 7.94 to 5.89 in the outing, with his only two runs coming on a two-run homer by former Twins center fielder Torii Hunter. Slowey said that a key to his success was throwing a few more pitches out of the strike zone. Known for his stellar command, Slowey has realized that he has often been throwing too many strikes, and by making his misses less hittable, he feels he can produce better results. Next up for Slowey will be a start against the Indians. He is 1-2 with a 5.48 ERA in four career starts against the Tribe.

home_pitcher_note: Laffey doesn't know how long his spot in the Indians' rotation will last, but he's certainly made the most out of the opportunity, to this point. Laffey was strong against the Royals in his first start on April 15 and even stronger in his second appearance against them six days later. He went seven innings, allowing just a run on seven hits with three walks, two strikeouts and a hit batter. What was most impressive was the way the sinkerball-tossing lefty always had a double-play ball in his back pocket. He induced five double plays in all. Laffey, who is filling in for an injured Scott Lewis, is 1-1 with a 5.75 ERA in four career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins was finally rewarded with a victory after delivering his third straight eight-inning outing, holding the Angels to one run on four hits. Despite getting drilled in the left thigh by a Bobby Abreu liner for the first out of the seventh inning, Perkins managed to make it through eight innings while throwing just 84 pitches. He likely would have completed the game had his leg not started to stiffen up. Perkins is the first Twins pitcher in almost four years to log three successive eight-inning outings. The last to do so was Johan Santana, who accomplished the feat June 2-14, 2005.

home_pitcher_note: Lee appears to have found something more closely resembling his old Cy Young form, but he didn't get any help from his offense in a 2-0 loss to the Royals on Wednesday. Lee went eight innings, allowing a pair of runs on nine hits with a walk and five strikeouts. He's shown better command of his curveball in his last two starts, and that's helped him considerably. Lee has had some trouble with Boston in the past. He is 2-4 with a 5.13 ERA in eight career starts against them, including a loss last year, in which he gave up five runs in seven innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer has been terrific in his last two starts, notching back-to-back complete games, though the last one lasted just seven innings in a game shortened by rain. Wakefield earned the win, giving up five hits and a run against the Twins. Before that was his gem against the A's, when Wakefield came five outs from a no-hitter. In 25 career appearances against the Indians, Wakefield is 10-8 with a 4.50 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes didn't have his best command against the Royals on Thursday, but he didn't give in to the fight. He went six innings, allowing just two runs on four hits with four walks and five strikeouts for a no-decision. His teammates committed two errors behind him, but he limited the damage. Reyes has been a pretty effective fifth starter, to this point. He'll be facing the Red Sox for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Despite his high ERA, Penny has turned in quality starts in two of his first three outings. Most recently, he earned a victory against the Twins, giving up six hits and three runs over six innings. Penny walked one and struck out two in that one. This will be Penny's first career appearance against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Twins, Carmona went six-plus innings, giving up five runs -- four earned -- on eight hits and two walks, striking out seven. Heading into the series finale with the Red Sox, Carmona faces a team that has given him all kinds of problems. In all, Carmona is 1-4 in four starts against Boston, including two blown saves that went for losses from his days in the bullpen in the 2006 season. In his last start of 2008, Carmona gave up four runs on five hits and a walk in an inning of work, taking the loss against the Red Sox.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander worked hard in his last start, throwing 114 pitches over six innings against the Yankees. It turned out to be a quality start, with Lester scattering seven hits and two runs. He walked three and struck out seven to take a no decision in a game the Red Sox won in 11 innings. After struggling in his first two starts, Lester has settled into a nice rhythm in his last two turns. Lester has made four starts in his career against the Indians, going 2-0 with a 4.03 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga allowed just three hits over six innings in his last start at Kansas City but wasn't happy about issuing five walks. He said he will be working on his mechanics so that walks won't be a problem as he goes forward. Galarraga made the big pitch when he needed it in Kansas City, and perhaps it's a good sign for the Tigers that he could hold the Royals to just one run despite those mechanical issues.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano has the ball for the first of a seven-game road trip, beginning in Detroit. The Twins hit Pavano hard in his last start, scoring five runs on 11 hits and a walk in five-plus innings. Pavano, who has spent a good deal of his career in the National League, has never faced the Tigers. He will go against a former teammate in Detroit slugger Miguel Cabrera, who was a part of the Florida Marlins' 2003 World Series Championship team, along with Pavano.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers used an off-day to shuffle their rotation so that Miner and similar sinkerballer Rick Porcello wouldn't be pitching on consecutive days, leaving Miner with six days of rest before he faces the Indians. It also allows manager Jim Leyland a little more flexbility to go to his bullpen early if he sees signs of trouble in Miner. Miner threw five innings of one-run ball at Kansas City last Saturday, but also walked three Royals and threw just 42 of his 83 pitches for strikes. He has never started against Cleveland, but owns a 1-1 record and 5.02 ERA in nine relief meetings with the Indians, walking eight batters over 14 1/3 innings. With Dontrelle Willis progressing quickly through the Tigers farm system in his rehab assignment, this outing could be a big test for Miner.
away_pitcher_note: Called up because of an injury to Scott Lewis, Laffey has been a major sparkplug for the Tribe's rotation. The Indians are 3-0 in games he starts. His ERA would rank among the league's leaders if not for him falling one-third of an inning shy of qualification. Pitching with a chip on his shoulder after losing out in the bid for the last spot in the Tribe's rotation out of spring camp, Laffey has had strong command of his sinker, and he's also using his breaking ball with more effectiveness. He limited the Twins to a pair of runs on five hits over 6 1/3 innings in a victory on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander has pitched well off and on this season, but his last start marked the first time good results and good performance matched up. His seven-plus scoreless innings against the Yankees saw him strike out nine while not walking a batter and scattering seven singles. Considering his struggles against New York over the last couple of years, it was an impressive performance, but his next start against Cleveland at Comerica Park will pit him against a division rival who has roughed him up over the years.
away_pitcher_note: Facing a potent Red Sox lineup on Monday, Lee was brilliant for eight innings in which he allowed just five hits and nothing more. He struck out five batters and induced two double plays, but all he had to show for his efforts was a no-decision. This was Lee truly in the form that made him a Cy Young winner last season, and his improvement is best demonstrated by the fact that his ERA, which was at 12.60 after his Opening Day debacle in Texas, is now under four. He says the key is mixing up his pitches earlier in the game and in the count, getting results out of his breaking ball.

home_pitcher_note: Tallet is coming off a rough outing in an 11-3 loss at Kansas City. He had trouble finishing off the Royals with two outs and was charged with 10 earned runs over four innings. Tallet talked about leaving too many pitches over the plate and up in key situations, but chalked it up as just one bad performance after blanking the White Sox through 5 2/3 innings on four hits in his previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the Red Sox on Wednesday, Carmona went 6 2/3 innings in which he more closely resembled his 19-win form of 2007. Though he walked four batters, Carmona never lost his composure. He allowed just two runs on five hits with three strikeouts. He was saddled with a no-decision after the bullpen squandered the 5-2 lead he left behind. Walks are still very much an issue for Carmona. He's issued 16 walks in 28 2/3 innings. But in this latest start, he showed better command of his secondary pitches. He is 2-0 with a 1.88 ERA in two career starts against the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Considered the Blue Jays' top pitching prospect, Cecil will make his big-league debut after a rough opening month with Triple-A Las Vegas. In four starts in the Minors, Cecil went 0-3 with an 8.31 ERA, amassing nine strikeouts and eight walks over 17 1/3 innings. On Tuesday, the lefty gave up three runs on four hits with five strikeouts and one walk in six innings for Vegas. Cecil, who was the 38th overall pick in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, had a shot at making Toronto's Opening Day rotation during Spring Training.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes' no-decision against the Red Sox on Tuesday was an outing he'd like to forget. He had trouble commanding his pitches, particularly his curveball, and he was battered for seven runs on nine hits with a walk, a strikeout and a hit batter in just two-plus innings. Reyes had success working himself out of jams in previous outings, but his luck ran out in this one. He'll look to post his second victory of the season against the Blue Jays, to whom he allowed four runs on three hits with three walks and two strikeouts in six innings on April 12.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander was on his way to a pretty good performance in his last outing when one ill-fated pitch ruined the entire day. That pitch was a mislocated sinker that Evan Longoria belted for a grand slam in a 6-2 win by the Rays. Masterson went six innings in that game, giving up six hits and six runs while walking three and striking out six. In his three starts, Masterson is 2-1 with a 4.32 ERA. This will be Masterson's first career start against the Indians. He has faced them three times out of the bullpen in his career, striking out four and not allowing a run over 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano turned in a gem against the Tigers on Friday, going 7 1/3 innings and allowing just two runs on five hits with no walks and three strikeouts. He was masterful for the first seven innings, allowing no runs and just three hits and not letting any runner past first base. It was his longest outing since a complete-game shutout of the Mariners way back on May 17, 2005, when he was with the Yankees. He'll look to keep it going against the Red Sox, against whom he is 1-3 with an 8.18 ERA in five career starts. He is 0-2 with a 24.75 ERA lifetime in Fenway.

home_pitcher_note: While his last start was far from his best, Wakefield still got the win, going five innings and giving up seven hits and five runs against the Rays. Overall, the knuckleballer has been Boston's best starter this season, turning in four quality starts in five outings. This will be Wakefield's second start of the season at Fenway. On April 22, he gave up five hits and a run over seven innings in a victory over the Twins. Wakefield hopes to duplicate the success against the Indians that he had in Cleveland on April 27, when he allowed one hit and no runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sowers will be recalled from Triple-A Columbus to start in place of left-hander Aaron Laffey, who is moving to the bullpen. Sowers won his last start for the Clippers, allowing one run on five hits in seven innings at Toledo.

home_pitcher_note: Lee gave the Indians another strong effort Sunday in Detroit, but he was once again hurt by a lack of support from his teammates. Lee went seven innings, allowing three runs on 12 hits with a walk and four strikeouts. He pitched himself out of some jams early, but gave up the go-ahead runs in the seventh. Lee, who is now the Indians' all-time leader in winning percentage among those with 1,000 innings pitched, has allowed just six runs over his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander shook off his traditional struggles against the Indians with seven innings of one-run ball to outduel reigning Cy Young Award winner Cliff Lee on Sunday at Comerica Park. His next challenge will be to follow it up at Progressive Field, where he's 1-7 with a 9.00 ERA in eight career starts. That won't be easy, but it's been a while since he entered Cleveland with as much momentum as now, coming off back-to-back dominant seven-inning performances to beat the Indians and Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona received a no-decision against the Blue Jays Monday in his last start. He allowed four runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings. The right-hander walked one, struck out three and tossed 96 pitches in the outing. Carmona has logged at least six innings in each of his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson has allowed one run or none through six innings in four of his six starts as a Tiger, but has a lone win to show it thanks to one of the lowest run support totals in the American League. His latest defeat came Monday, when he took a 1-1 game against the Twins into the seventh inning before Minnesota plated five runs to take charge. Jackson has a start and a relief appearance for his career at Progressive Field, holding the Indians to a run on eight hits over 8 2/3 innings with nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Though he pitched well against Toronto in his last start, Reyes earned a no-decision after the Tribe's bullpen blew the lead. Reyes yielded three runs on six hits across six innings. He struck out six and did not walk a batter. Reyes has now earned no-decisions in each of his last four outings.
away_pitcher_note: The key to Porcello in good outings and bad over his first five Major League starts has been his ability to throw his sinker for strikes. When he does, he can get quick groundouts and avoid the kind of big hits that inflate his run total in a hurry. When he doesn't, he falls behind in the count and leaves himself to challenge hitters with his secondary pitches. His last start was very much a case of the former, as he held the Twins to four singles over seven innings with three walks and three strikeouts. He'll try for more of the same in his first meeting with the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: After starting the season 0-3 with a 9.50 ERA through his first four starts, Pavano has pitched at least six innings in each of his last two outings, going 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA. On Wednesday, he located all his pitches, ending the Red Sox's nine-game home winning streak, stifling Boston for two runs on six hits and three walks, with four strikeouts and a hit batter in six innings. It was his first career win at Fenway Park, and his first career victory against the Sox since June 7, 1999, while with the Expos.
away_pitcher_note: Ozzie Guillen believes that Floyd needs to be far more aggressive within the strike zone, and Floyd does not disagree with his manager. Floyd was staked to 5-1 and 7-4 leads during Tuesday's game in Kansas City, but he couldn't shut down the Royals for the victory. Floyd gave up six runs on six hits over five innings, striking out two and walking two, while also allowing two home runs. Floyd had a 2-0 record with a 5.25 ERA last year against Cleveland and has a 2-1 record lifetime against the Indians. This will be his first start at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers, called up to take over Aaron Laffey's rotation spot when Laffey was moved to the bullpen, gave the Indians five strong innings in his season debut Thursday in Boston before running into inescapable trouble in the sixth, when the Red Sox hitters became a little more patient. When all was said and done, he was charged with seven runs on seven hits with three walks and a strikeout in five-plus innings of work. Sowers was 0-2 with a 7.56 ERA in two starts against the White Sox last year.
away_pitcher_note: Richard served as a starter for most of Cactus League action, just in case Jose Contreras or Bartolo Colon weren't ready for the start of the regular season, so it shouldn't be too difficult for the southpaw to stretch out for four or five innings on Tuesday. Richard made his 12th appearance in relief on Sunday during a loss to Texas, but it basically functioned as a side day with Richard pitching one-third of an inning and facing two batters. Richard had a 2-5 record with a 6.35 ERA in eight starts last year and is replacing Jose Contreras, who has a 0-5 mark with an 8.19 ERA over six starts in 2009. Richard has made one start against the Indians and has a 0-1 record lifetime against them.

home_pitcher_note: Tough-luck losses are becoming routine for Lee, who has gotten little to no run support the past month. Lee gave the Indians another eight stellar innings Friday night against the Tigers, giving up just one run on seven hits with two walks and five strikeouts. But the Indians didn't give him any run support, and he took the loss for the third time in four starts. That's two runs of support total for Lee over four starts. He is 5-5 with a 5.58 ERA lifetime against the White Sox, including a 2-0 mark and 0.53 ERA in two starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle started a season at 5-0 for the first time in his illustrious career, following Thursday's 6-0 whitewash of the Tigers. But that wasn't the main story coming from this victory. Buehrle was perfect through 6 1/3 innings, retiring the first 19 hitters he faced, before Placido Polanco lined a double to left. Buehrle finished off eight innings on 110 pitches, allowing just the one hit, while striking out five and walking two. The southpaw once again will be pitching with an extra day of rest, as the White Sox flip-flopped Buehrle and Clayton Richard in the rotation against the Indians. Buehrle has a 9-12 record against Cleveland, the only sub-.500 ledger against the American League Central for Buehrle, along with a 4.82 ERA. He is 5-5 with a 4.37 ERA at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Shields seemed to have everything working in his last start Friday night against the Red Sox, when he posted five scoreless innings. But the Red Sox erupted for five runs in the sixth -- all of the runs scored on two home runs -- and Shields took his third loss of the season. The right-hander has earned his reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to pitch his team into the seventh or eighth inning, which is evidenced by two consecutive seasons with 215 innings pitched. The right-hander is 21-8 with a 3.30 ERA in 44 career starts at Tropicana Field. Shields is 0-2 with a 3.76 ERA in four career starts against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona's overall line against the Tigers was solid Saturday, but he blinked first in a pitchers' duel with Edwin Jackson and took the loss. Carmona allowed two runs on four hits with six walks and four strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings. The walks remain the great separator between Carmona recapturing his '07 magic. In this outing, he walked two batters to open the seventh, and both runners wound up crossing the plate for the game's first two runs. Carmona is 1-1 with a 4.91 ERA in three career appearances against the Rays. He lost his lone start against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir made his seventh start of the season on Saturday afternoon against the Red Sox and worked through a couple of early problems to earn his fourth win of the season, holding the Red Sox to three runs on eight hits in five innings. Despite earning the win, Kazmir continued to struggle with his control, walking three batters and throwing just 58 of his 100 pitches for strikes. Kazmir is 1-2 with a 5.47 ERA in five career starts against the Indians, and he is 22-16 with a 3.33 ERA in 63 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes got roughed up in a loss to the Tigers on Sunday. He gave up five runs on seven hits with four walks and three strikeouts in five innings of work. That's the third time in six starts that Reyes has gone five innings or less, and he's gone six innings in the other three. So going deep into ballgames has not exactly been his strong suit. Reyes has never faced the Rays in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Garza has the best stuff on the Rays staff, and at age 25, the right-hander seems to be maturing on the mound, where he has experienced problems controlling his emotions in the past. The one thing he has lacked is consistency, as he has been either lights-out or off his game. Garza needs to better learn how to win when he doesn't have his best stuff. He posted his third consecutive quality start in his last outing, on Sunday night against the Red Sox, by allowing three runs on seven hits while walking two and striking out six in seven innings. He is 0-3 with a 6.12 ERA in five career starts against the Indians and 9-4 with a 3.03 ERA in 19 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano is riding a three-game winning streak in which he's allowed eight runs on 21 hits over his last 19 2/3 innings. He pitched better against the White Sox on Monday than his final line might indicate. He allowed four runs on 10 hits with three strikeouts over 6 1/3 innings, but all the runs came after the offense staked him to a 6-0 lead and he began pitching more aggressively -- perhaps too aggressively -- in the strike zone. Pavano is 4-2 with a 3.91 ERA in eight career starts against the Rays. He gave up six runs over 9 1/3 innings against them in a win last year.

home_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine got hit hard and often in his last start, Tuesday against the Orioles. The right-hander allowed seven runs on nine hits in two innings -- including two home runs to Adam Jones -- to take his fourth loss of the season. When Sonnanstine is going well, he is a master of deception, employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. Sonnanstine is 0-2 with a 7.15 ERA in two career starts against the Orioles and is 9-9 with a 5.06 ERA in 27 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Huff will be promoted from Triple-A Columbus to make his Major League debut. In seven starts for Columbus, Huff was 5-1 with a 4.35 ERA. He struck out 32 and walked 16 in 39 1/3 innings. Huff, 24, was the 39th overall selection in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft. He was in the mix for a rotation spot out of Spring Training camp but was hampered by biceps tendinitis. The Indians had this rotation spot open after Jeremy Sowers was demoted to Triple-A.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister pitched effectively again, giving up two runs on five hits in 5 2-3 innings against the Oakland A's last Wednesday, but he took his first loss of the season. Bannister said he took his demotion to Triple-A Omaha at the beginning of the season as a chance to work on things. Whatever he did worked. He's been impressive in all five of his starts. He pitched six scoreless innings against the Indians on April 22 for his first win.
away_pitcher_note: Lee was impressive again in a win over the White Sox on Wednesday, and he got some significant run support for the first time in five starts. He pounded the strike zone and commanded his pitches, working out of bases-loaded jams in the sixth and seventh innings. In all, he allowed just six hits and a walk with nine strikeouts over seven scoreless innings. Lee gave up just two runs on nine hits over eight innings against the Royals on April 22 but took the loss because of a lack of support.

home_pitcher_note: Meche lasted just 4 1/3 innings, his second-shortest start of the season, in a loss last Thursday night to the Orioles. By the time he departed Meche already had rung up 87 pitches, just 50 of them strikes, as he struggled with his command. The five runs he gave up matched his season worst, reached only when he left a game with back problems in the fourth inning. No back pain this time, he said, but he knows he's got to fix something quick. In his last 19 2/3 innings, he's surrendered 16 earned runs. One of his losses this year came at Cleveland although he gave up just three earned runs in 7 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona was brilliant for five scoreless innings in a win in Tampa Bay on Thursday, but he began to get a little out of control in the sixth, walking two batters and throwing a costly wild pitch. By the time the inning was over, Carmona had been charged with five runs (four earned). Those were the only runs he allowed in 5 1/3 innings of work. He gave up four hits, walked three and struck out two. Carmona has his moments of excellence this season, but the walks tend to bite him. He gave up four runs on five hits with four walks and three strikeouts over five innings in a loss to the Royals on April 13.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a tough 1-0 loss, Greinke endured a two and a half hour rain delay Friday night and then came out with a little too much firepower in the early going against the Orioles. He finally throttled back a bit and, as he put it, started pitching and zipped through innings four-to-seven with barely a blemish. He gave up six hits, just two walks and fanned six in his 8-1 victory. In his 60 innings this season, he's recorded 65 strikeouts, walked only 10 and has given up a mere four earned runs on 40 hits. He has yet to surrender a home run. The Indians were his second victim this year; Greinke shut them out for five innings, in his shortest outing so far.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano's personal three-game winning streak came to a halt Saturday in Tampa Bay, as he surrendered three runs on six hits with two walks, six strikeouts and a homer in five-plus innings. He breezed through the lineup the first time but began to find himself in trouble the second time through. It was the third time this season that Pavano was unable to get through six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo has lost two of his past three starts but pitched well his last time out on Sunday. He just had the misfortune of opposing Padres ace Jake Peavy, who went the distance while shutting the Reds down by a 3-1 score. Arroyo pitched seven innings and allowed three earned runs and six hits with four walks and four strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes turned in another unremarkable outing Friday in Tampa Bay, allowing five runs (three earned) on five hits with a walk and four strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings. Staked to a 7-0 lead, he couldn't capitalize, and the Indians went on to lose the game. Reyes doesn't have great stuff. He's a command pitcher. And when he can't command in the inside part of the plate, opposing batters pounce.

home_pitcher_note: In eight starts this season for Louisville, the 23-year-old Bailey is 3-5 with a 4.57 ERA, 17 walks and 43 strikeouts over 45 1/3 innings. Once heralded as the organization's best young starter, Bailey has gone 4-8 with a 6.72 ERA in 17 Major League starts since 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Huff's Major League debut was a rocky one against the Rays on Sunday. In just 3 2/3 innings of work, Huff was worked over for seven runs on seven hits with four walks and two strikeouts to take the loss. He didn't display the type of command that made him the 39th overall pick in the 2006 Draft and has made him effective in the Minors. He'll likely get another shot at trying to solidify himself at the big-league level with this start against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: In a 4-3 loss to the Phillies on Tuesday, Cueto pitched seven innings and allowed four earned runs and seven hits without a walk and struck out four. It was the sixth straight start Cueto worked at least seven innings but his first non-quality outing (of at least six innings and three or fewer runs allowed) since April 17. The right-hander retired the sides in order during the first, third, fourth and sixth innings, but gave up Ryan Howard's homer in the second inning and four hits during a three-run fifth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Cliff Lee's rotten luck continued in his last start against Kansas City. Lee threw eight innings, allowed two runs and lowered his ERA to 2.90. But Lee had to settle for the no decision when Cleveland's bullpen gave up four runs in the ninth. Lee has allowed six runs in his last five starts, but he's 1-2 during those starts and 2-5 on the season. Before the Indians scored five runs in his last outing, the Indians had totaled just six runs in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona worked six innings and allowed four runs on six hits in his last start against the Royals. It was the eighth consecutive start that Carmona had given up four earned runs or fewer. But Carmona was hurt by four walks and two wild pitches against Kansas City as he settled for the no decision. Carmona's last win came on May 14 against the Rays. He pitched 5 1/3 innings, holding the Rays to four earned runs on four hits as he notched his second win and his first since April 18.
away_pitcher_note: With Scott Kazmir on the 15-day disabled list with a right quadriceps strain, the Rays have a hole in their starting rotation for Monday's series opener against the Indians. Though nothing is official, that spot is expected to be filled by Price. The phenom started off the season in the Minor Leagues and will likely be called up from Triple-A Durham for Monday's start. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, Price is 1-4 with a 3.93 ERA in eight starts at Triple-A for the Bulls. He did not disappoint as a rookie last year, posting a 1.93 ERA through 14 innings during the regular season. In the American League Championship Series, Price pitched 2 1/3 scoreless innings, notching a win in Game 2 and a save in Game 7 against the Red Sox. Price gave up two runs -- one earned -- in 3 1/3 innings against the Phillies in the World Series.

home_pitcher_note: After posting a 9.50 ERA in April, Pavano has gone 3-1 in the month of May and lowered his ERA by more than three runs. Pavano went six innings and allowed three runs against the Royals in his last start. The Indians right hander, who gave up six hits and struck out eight, took a no-decision. After his last start, Pavano has now gone at least six innings in three of his last four starts. Pavano's last loss came against the Rays on May 16, when he went five innings and allowed three runs.
away_pitcher_note: Garza remains Tampa Bay's top starter this season, throwing his fifth straight outing of more than six innings when he faced Oakland on Thursday. He allowed two runs on seven hits and struck out eight, but got a no-decision after the A's tied the game in the eighth, costing Garza a chance for a career-high fourth consecutive win. It seems like his stuff is at its peak right now. He just needs to keep his pitch count down; he threw 107 pitches Thursday, after setting a career-high with 120 two starts ago.

home_pitcher_note: The Indians didn't announce that Jackson would be starting Wednesday's game until after Tuesday night's game. That's how murky their rotation situation has become, with Anthony Reyes and Aaron Laffey both landing on the DL over the weekend. Jeremy Sowers was originally supposed to take Reyes' rotation spot, but Sowers was needed for five innings of relief Monday. Enter Jackson, who opened the season in the big-league bullpen as a long man before getting sent down to Columbus, where he was converted back to starting work. In seven appearances, including four starts, Jackson went 3-2 with a 3.09 ERA, striking out 13 and walking eight in 23 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Spotted with an eight-run lead going into the bottom of the second inning, Sonnanstine was pretty much on cruise control while getting the win in a romp over the Marlins on Friday. The 26-year-old gave up just one run on five hits while striking out two and walking none, leaving after throwing 102 pitches -- 70 of which were strikes. His only mistake was a 2-2 fastball that resulted in a solo home run by Hanley Ramirez. Sonnanstine, who came into the game leading all active pitchers with a .385 batting average (5-for-13), even helped out the offense -- though it didn't need any help at all -- by going 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs scored. For his career against the Indians, Sonnanstine is 1-2 with a 7.41 ERA in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Huff hasn't taken his Minor League success with him to the big leagues, to this point. He's made two starts for the Tribe, and both have been rough ones. On Saturday in Cincinnati, he allowed six runs on seven hits with a walk and three strikeouts in just three innings of work, and he took a no-decision. He gave up three home runs. Huff doesn't have dazzling stuff, so the key is fastball command and a strong breaking ball to work off the fastball. If Huff's stuff isn't up to par, the results speak for themselves.
away_pitcher_note: Niemann may have settled for a no-decision against the Marlins on Saturday, but the 6-foot-9 hurler was lights-out regardless. The right-hander gave up just one through six innings, scattering four hits and one walk while striking out five. He allowed only two runners to reach scoring position in the first four innings, and in the fifth, he got out of a second-and-third, one-out jam with three pitches that resulted in a couple of flyouts to left field. His only real mistake was a 3-1, chest-high fastball to Dan Uggla in the fourth inning, which resulted in a solo home run. Niemann will be facing the Indians for the first time in his short career.

home_pitcher_note: Lee didn't work quickly or ahead quite as often as he usually does, but he nonetheless turned in a quality start in a no-decision against the Reds on Sunday. In six innings, Lee allowed three runs on eight hits with a walk and four strikeouts. It was another outing that would have resulted in a win for Lee had he enjoyed more early run support. Lee earned one of his two wins on the season when facing the Yankees on April 16, giving up a run on seven hits with three walks and four strikeouts in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte looked dominant at times during his last start. If only he could have two pitches back, he may have earned the win. Pettitte allowed two home runs to the Phillies on Saturday -- including a three-run shot by John Mayberry Jr. -- which accounted for all four runs he allowed in seven innings. The left-hander surrendered just five hits in taking a no-decision. The Yankees came back to win the game, saving Pettitte from his first loss since April 26.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona's control problems once again got the best of him in his worst start of the season Monday against the Rays. In just 1 1/3 innings of work, he allowed five runs on three hits with five walks and three strikeouts. In one stretch in the second inning, he threw 16 of 19 pitches for balls, walking four straight batters. The command woes have been a problem for Carmona for a year now, as he's looked less and less like the dominant No. 2 pitcher who won 19 games in '07. Buoyed by 22 runs of support, Carmona gave up four runs on six hits with four walks and a strikeout over six innings in a win over the Yankees on April 18.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia continued his dominant ways in his last start, allowing just three runs in eight strong innings to the Phillies on Sunday. And that was his worst of his last four outings. Since May 8, Sabathia has surrendered just six runs in his 32 innings (1.69 ERA) and has been every bit the ace the Yankees were hoping for. His next start could be interesting, because Sabathia is making his first appearance in Cleveland since being traded by the Indians last season.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano only seems to get stronger and more effective as his comeback season rolls along. Further and further removed from his "American Idle" days in four injury-plagued years with the Yankees, the big right-hander has gone 5-1 with a 3.58 ERA over his Past six starts. Pavano's last outing against the Rays on Tuesday was arguably his strongest start of the season. In seven innings, he allowed just one run -- on a Carlos Pena solo shot in the seventh -- on four hits with two walks and six strikeouts. Pavano was also impressive when he faced the Yanks on April 19. In that game, he gave up just a run on four hits over six innings but didn't get a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes will try for his third consecutive victory on Sunday as he comes off a dominant outing against the Rangers in Arlington, limiting the opposition to three hits over eight scoreless innings. It marked Hughes' second scoreless start of the season, as he also tossed six shutout frames on April 28 at Detroit. Hughes allowed three earned runs or less in five of his six starts this season. He last pitched against Cleveland in Game 3 of the 2007 American League Division Series, when he relieved Roger Clemens and hurled 3 2/3 innings of scoreless relief to earn the Yankees' only postseason victory that year.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers will return to the rotation after getting called back up to the big leagues and serving a brief stint in the bullpen. He was impressive against the Rays on Memorial Day, tossing five scoreless innings in his first career relief appearances. Sowers, who was 0-2 with a 12.00 ERA in two spot starts in May, will have to prove he can still have that type of success in a starting role. He is 1-1 with a 6.60 ERA in three career starts against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Chamberlain will return to the scene of the 2007 American League Division Series 'midge game' on Monday, as he makes his seventh career appearance (second start) in the regular season against the Tribe. Chamberlain had another shaky first inning his last time out at Texas, lasting just four innings while allowing three runs in a 7-3 loss to the Rangers, and has a 10.00 ERA in the first frame this season over his nine starts. Chamberlain is 2-0 with a 2.86 ERA in five road starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey delivered his fourth straight quality start for the Twins in his last outing vs. the Red Sox. The right-hander pitched six innings, allowing just two runs on six hits. He issued a rare walk while striking out five. Since his rough outing in Baltimore on May 6, Slowey has not given up more than two earned runs in each of his last four starts and he's currently on a three-game winning streak. Next up he'll face the Indians for the second time this season.  He pitched eight innings, allowing just one run, in his only other start vs. Cleveland this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rain got in the way of Huff's strong early showing against the Rays on Thursday. The young left-hander, making his third start in the bigs, went four scoreless innings, allowing four hits with a walk and two strikeouts. When rain delayed the game for two hours, 40 minutes, Huff didn't come back out. Still, the early showing was a marked improvement over Huff's first two Major League starts, so he can certainly take some positives from it.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander has been impressive since being called up to fill in for an injured Glen Perkins. Swarzak has allowed just three earned runs over 13 innings, delivering a quality start in both of his outings. That included his start against the Red Sox, in which he pitched six innings and allowed three runs on five hits. With Perkins not scheduled to return for at least another week, Swarzak will get a few more starts to show the club what he can do. He'll face the Indians for the first time in his career at the Metrodome.
away_pitcher_note: For the second outing in a row, Lee didn't work ahead and didn't work efficiently against the Yankees on Friday. But once again, he limited the damage against him and turned in a quality start. Lee allowed three runs on nine hits with two walks and five strikeouts. Keeping with a trend that has been taking place all season, Lee didn't get much run support, and he took the loss. The Indians have averaged just 2.73 runs in the games Lee starts. Lee is 7-3 with a 3.78 ERA in 16 career starts against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Baker failed to deliver a second straight quality start when he faced the Rays, pitching 5 2/3 innings and allowing four earned runs on six hits. Like his previous start, Baker allowed nearly all of his runs at the end of the outing. He held the Rays to just one run on three hits through the first five innings, with the lone run coming on Carl Crawford's two-out solo home run in the third. But in the sixth, Baker gave up three straight hits -- which concluded with Evan Longoria's three-run shot to deep center field.  Next up, Baker faces the Indians. He is 3-5 with a 4.00 ERA in 11 career starts vs. Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: It's not getting any better for Carmona, who has battled control problems all season. In his latest start against the Yankees, Carmona lasted just four innings, allowing seven runs, four of which were earned, on eight hits with three walks and two strikeouts. Carmona didn't get much help from his defense, but he didn't make pitches when it mattered, either. He served up a pair of home runs. In his last start against the Twins, Carmona allowed five runs (four earned) on eight hits over six innings in a loss on April 24.

home_pitcher_note: Danks wasn't exactly sharp during his Sunday start at Kauffman Stadium, throwing 100 pitches in just 5 1/3 innings. But the young southpaw certainly gave the White Sox a chance to win against Kansas City ace Zack Greinke. Danks gave up four runs -- although one came home when Alexei Ramirez lost a two-out pop up in the sun -- along with nine hits in his last start. He struck out five and walked two, exiting with a runner on third and one out in the sixth but finished with a no-decision. Danks has a 1-4 career record with a 5.31 ERA against the Indians, but he has not faced them during the 2009 season. Danks holds a 1-1 record and 3.32 ERA over four starts this year at U.S. Cellular.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano held the potent Yankees bats to three runs on seven hits with no walks and four strikeouts in 7 1/3 innings on Sunday, but he took a no-decision when the bullpen blew the lead he left behind. Over his last seven starts, Pavano is 5-1 with a 3.60 ERA. He has tossed seven innings or more in two straight starts. Facing the White Sox on May 11, Pavano gave up four runs on 10 hits over 6 1/3 innings and took the victory.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd produced his third consecutive quality start on Monday night, earning a no-decision against the A's. Floyd threw 107 pitches in seven innings, allowing two runs on four hits. He escaped a bases-loaded jam in the seventh by striking out A's shortstop Orlando Cabrera to preserve a 2-2 tie in a game the White Sox went on to win, 6-2. Floyd continued to lower his ERA, to 5.75, after it reached a season-high 7.71 on May 17. In four career starts against the Indians, Floyd is 2-2 with a 6.56 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Sowers had a strong start going against the Yankees on Monday, and then he literally lost all control. He walked three batters to open the sixth and threw just one strike in that span. Fortunately for Sowers, he was replaced by Greg Aquino, who left the three inherited runners stranded. In five-plus innings, Sowers allowed just one run on three hits and struck out three, but the five walks he issued marred an otherwise solid outing. Sowers will look to be more aggressive against the White Sox, who roughed him up for five runs on seven hits in four innings when he took a loss on May 12.

home_pitcher_note: Colon's inconsistent season continued Tuesday night in a 5-0 loss against the A's. For the seventh time in 10 starts, he did not make it out of the sixth inning. Colon threw just 81 pitches and lasted 5 2/3 innings, allowing six hits and five runs (two earned). He has not won back-to-back starts this season. Colon owns a 4-2 record lifetime against the Indians in seven starts with a 3.49 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Huff is still in search of his first big league win after losing to Minnesota on Tuesday. The lefty allowed four runs on nine hits through five innings, including a two-run home run to Twins catcher Joe Mauer in the fifth. He had his highest pitch count of the season, throwing 98 pitches (64 for strikes). He struck out five batters, the most of his young career.

home_pitcher_note: The Indians hadn't given much run support to Lee this season prior to Wednesday's game (3.04 runs per game). Lee's latest start was a whole different story. Cleveland scored 10 against Minnesota as Lee cruised to his third win of the season. He went eight innings for the fifth time this season, but recorded just his first win when doing so. Lee's five-strikeout performance against Minnesota was a nice way to rebound from a tough 3-1 loss to New York.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister has been knocked around in his last two starts after doing quite well following his callup from Triple-A Omaha. On Wednesday night at Tampa Bay, he didn't make it out of the fourth inning as Ben Zobrist's grand slam put the Rays ahead 8-0. Bannister gave up nine hits, walked three and had two wild pitches while running up 91 pitches (55 strikes) in his 3 2/3 innings. In his last two games, his ERA has leaped from 2.79 to 4.80. This is his third start against the Indians. On April 22, his first game back in the Majors, he blanked them for six innings. On May 19, however, the Tribe nicked him for five runs on nine hits and he got no decision.

home_pitcher_note: Before the start of the season, it became fashionable to cringe at the idea of Pavano -- coming off four ignominious and injury plagued seasons with the Yankees -- serving as the Indians' No. 3 starter.
