Floyd has a 4-2 career record with a 4.30 ERA against the Indians and has a 16-9 mark at U.S. Cellular.
away_pitcher_note: The big-bodied Masterson has Major League stuff, but can he be effective as a Major League starter? The Indians will find out this season, as Masterson, who was transitioned from relief work with the Red Sox to starting duties with the Tribe after he was acquired in last summer's Victor Martinez trade, will occupy the No. 3 spot of the rotation. Masterson was erratic in spring camp and needs to show improvement with his changeup if he's going to be successful as a starter, and against left-handers in particular. Masterson is 0-1 with a 1.53 ERA in five career appearances, including two starts, against the Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Detroit's annual spring party, the home opener at Comerica Park, will feature the front-line starter who just recently turned 21. Porcello's Spring Training performance seemingly defied the idea of a sophomore slump looming. If anything, he looks physically bigger and stronger than he did as a rookie, and appears ready to use that to his advantage. He allowed just three runs on 11 hits over his 18 spring innings. More importantly, he showed an eagerness to find a middle ground between the sinkerball pitcher he was for the first half of last season, and the power pitcher who used a straight fastball to wear down hitters over the stretch run. Porcello went 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA in four starts against Cleveland last year.
away_pitcher_note: Huff was the Tribe's leader with 11 wins last season, but that didn't ensure him a rotation spot this year. He had to earn one in Spring Training. Huff had an inconsistent spring camp, at times struggling to find the strike zone, but he finished strong. The Indians see room for improvement from Huff, who, in his rookie year, had a 5.61 ERA, .301 average against and a 1.56 WHIP. But they also see big upside, as Huff went 4-1 with a 2.18 ERA over his last five starts of the 2009 season. Huff was in the Indians' rotation from mid-May through the end of last season, but he never came across the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: While Dontrelle Willis' comeback from two lost seasons attracted some well-deserved attention nationally, Bonderman's return from two injury-plagued campaigns means just as much to Detroit's fortunes. He seemed on his way to stardom in 2006 before an ERA jump in 2007 and then circulation problems in 2008 threw his career into question in just his mid-20s. Now 27, he still doesn't have the old strength in his arm or the same life in his fastball, but his workhorse slider is back and his willingness to throw an offspeed pitch is stronger than ever. Bonderman went 1-1 with a 6.92 ERA in five spring outings, but more than half of his damage came in two-thirds of an inning against Toronto in early March.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians acquired Talbot in the December trade that sent Kelly Shoppach to the Rays. His path to the big leagues with the Rays was blocked, and he's out of Minor League options. The Indians are giving him this shot in the rotation based on his 13-win seasons at Triple-A Durham in 2007 and '08 and his strong performance in spring camp. Talbot has four effective pitches, with his changeup getting the most rave reviews. He pitched briefly for Tampa in 2008, but this will be his first real exposure to life as a Major League starter. He gave up five runs in 2 1/3 innings in a relief appearance against the Tigers in '08.

home_pitcher_note: Though a pair of two-run innings denied Verlander a chance at an Opening Day victory and chased him out after five innings, he retired 10 straight Royals in between and felt like he finally found the rhythm he was struggling to locate during Spring Training. His fastball registered at 100 mph, surprising even for him in his first outing of the year, and he would be happy to take that stuff into his first home start of the season against the Indians, whom he beat four times in as many starts last year after going 1-5 against the Tribe in 2008. He went 10-2 with a 2.81 ERA at Comerica Park in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook made his first start in nearly two years when he got the Opening Day nod against the White Sox on Monday, and he showed every bit of the rust that no doubt accumulated in that time. Westbrook went just four-plus innings, allowing five runs on five hits with four walks, a strikeout, a home run, two hit batters and four wild pitches. The wild pitches tied a club record for a single game. But Westbrook said he enjoyed being back on the Major League mound nearly two years after Tommy John surgery, and he's eager to find his old form. He is 4-8 with a 6.05 ERA in his career against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona gets the start in the Tribe's home opener, and he hopes to showcase the improvements he's made on the mental side of the game. Those improvements came in handy Wednesday, when his old control woes crept up again and he walked six White Sox batters in six innings. But to his credit, he never let himself unravel after the free passes, and the Sox never put up a big inning against him. Carmona allowed one hit and limited the damage to three runs, and the bats backed him up in a victory. While the walks remain a concern, the way Carmona kept his composure was a sign of maturity that he hopes to take into the start against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Harden failed to get through four innings in a start against the Blue Jays on Wednesday. He allowed just one hit but walked five and struck out eight while throwing 90 pitches in 3 2/3 innings. The only hit was a home run and he also allowed two unearned runs. Both scored though on bases loaded walks. Harden said his biggest problem was not being able to get the Blue Jays to put the ball in play and get some quick outs. He has made just five starts and one relief appearance against the Indians and is 1-0 with a 4.67 ERA against them. This will only be his second career start against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: The good news about Masterson's first start of 2010 is that he limited the White Sox to a run on four hits with two walks and five strikeouts. What's more, he was effective in limiting the damage by left-handed hitters, who have often been his nemesis in the past because of his low arm slot and lack of a consistent changeup. The bad news was that Masterson lasted just five innings and needed 92 pitches to get through them. That inefficiency forced the Indians to go to their bullpen in the sixth, and the one-run lead Masterson left behind was coughed up, leaving him with a no-decision. Masterson has made four career relief appearances against the Rangers but has never faced them as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis gets bumped up in the rotation to fill in for scheduled starter C.J. Wilson, who came down with a mild case of food poisoning. Lewis beat the Mariners, 6-2, on Friday at the Ballpark in Arlington in his first start for the Rangers after two years in Japan. He went seven innings and allowed one run on five hits. He was annoyed that he walked four, but the Mariners were 1-for-11 with runners on base and 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position. Lewis was 26-17 with a 2.82 ERA in 54 starts and one relief appearance for the Hiroshima Carp over the past two years, striking out 369 batters and walking 46 in 354 1/3 innings. Before he went to Japan, he made just two career appearances against the Indians. One was a start, one was a relief appearance and he has a 13.50 career ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Huff was the recipient of bad bounces on Friday in Detroit. The lefty took the loss despite just giving up one earned run in six innings. He worked his way out of a two-on, no-out jam in the sixth and generally had outstanding control and command throughout the game. That continued a strong trend from last September when Huff went 4-1 with a 2.18 ERA over his last five starts in 2009. "He was locked in all afternoon," Cleveland manager Manny Acta said of Huff in his first performance of the season. Huff did not face the Rangers in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison was supposed to pitch against the Yankees on Friday but was pushed up one day when C.J. Wilson came down with food poisoning. Harrison, the Rangers' fifth starter, made his first start of the season on Saturday against the Mariners. Harrison went six innings and allowed just one run on six hits, a walk and a hit batter. He struck out four. Harrison, who had shoulder surgery last summer and was making his first start since June 23, allowed eight of the first 18 Mariners batters to reach base, but then retired the last seven he faced on the afternoon. He left with a 3-1 lead, but the Mariners rallied in the ninth inning and kept him from getting a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot made just his fourth Major League appearance and second start Saturday, taking the loss in a 4-2 Detroit win. He admittedly didn't have his best stuff, although he regained some feel in the fourth inning and retired the last seven Tiger batters he faced. In the first three innings, Talbot gave up four earned runs and five walks but regained some confidence with his performance in the last two innings.
away_pitcher_note: The following trend is a good one for Mark Buehrle, but not exactly the best one for the White Sox. In Buehrle's two starts this season, the left-hander has a 2-0 record with four runs allowed in 15 innings. That early run leaves Buehrle on pace to win 35 games this season. During the starts made by the remaining four members of the White Sox rotation, the team is winless. Buehrle gave up four runs on six hits over the first three innings of Sunday's victory over the Twins but allowed only two singles in his next five innings of scoreless work. Buehrle threw 113 pitches, with 73 for strikes, although he only fanned one during the contest. He retired the last eight batters faced and 10 of the last 11. Buehrle beat Cleveland on Opening Day, working seven scoreless innings, and quite possibly making the defensive play of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook had a decent outing in Detroit on Sunday, but he didn't finish as strong as he'd like, and the big lead he handed to the bullpen was wasted. Westbrook went 5 2/3 innings, allowing three runs on nine hits with three walks, two hit batters and seven strikeouts. Though he walked three, he showed much more control than in his Opening Day start against the White Sox, which was his first start in nearly two years. With the rust removed, he's hoping to be even more effective against the Sox the second time around.
away_pitcher_note: Perhaps Peavy was trying too hard, or trying to make perfect pitches, but he made too many mistakes in his second start of the season in a no-decision against the Blue Jays. He has been searching to find the downward movement on his fastball. He gave up a pair of two-run home runs to John Buck and Vernon Wells and seven runs in all, and twice lost the lead. Reliever Randy Williams issued a walk with the bases loaded to force in the seventh run charged to Peavy. The White Sox won 8-7 in 11 innings but they need more than the 5 2/3 innings Peavy gave them Monday. To that end, between starts he worked on regaining the command of his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona became the first Tribe starter to reach the seventh inning, let alone the eighth, when he turned in eight strong innings against the Rangers in the Indians' home opener on Monday. Carmona, who took a no-decision against Texas, allowed just two runs on five hits while striking out four. He's still having some control issues, as evidenced by the four walks, wild pitch and hit batter he allowed. But he's been able to stay under control and limit the damage against him, even when he walked six White Sox batters in his first start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd had the misfortune to match up against Ricky Romero in his start against the Blue Jays. Romero had a no-hitter through seven innings as Floyd took the loss in a 4-2 game. Floyd allowed nine hits, two walks and four earned runs while striking out five in six innings. The Blue Jays have been Floyd's most difficult opponent and Tuesday's loss  put him at 0-4 with a 7.22 ERA in five games against them. In this third start of  the season he will face the team he faced in his opening start, the Indians. He did not figure in the decision in the White Sox 5-3 loss on April 8. Floyd allowed two runs on five hits over six innings while striking out seven and walking three. He left the game with the White Sox trailing, 2-1. Since joining the White Sox in 2007, he is 4-2 against the Indians and 2-1 with a  5.79 ERA in Cleveland. Last year, Floyd generally was  much better pitching at home, where his ERA was 2.47, compared to 5.47 on the road.

home_pitcher_note: After two starts, Slowey is still trying to find his groove. Slowey was uncharacteristically wild in his last start against the Red Sox on April 14 at Target Field when he walked four batters in just five innings of work. Slowey also gave up three runs on five hits while striking out five Boston batters during his first loss of the season. In his first start of the season, Slowey earned a victory over the Angels by pitching 5 1/3 innings. Despite the fact that Slowey gave up seven hits, he gave up just one run, walked two and struck out three. Slowey is facing an Indians team that is struggling at the plate with just one hitter, Shin-Soo Choo, who is hitting better than .300.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson had a rough beginning to his start against the Rangers on Wednesday, but then he settled in. Trouble was, it was too late to avoid the loss. Masterson went six innings, allowing four runs, two of which were earned, on nine hits with no walks and nine strikeouts. He improved his performance against left-handed hitters, and he obviously had some dominant moments, as the strikeout totals indicate. Now he just has to apply what he did over the last three innings to the length of his next outing against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano had an impressive start in shutting out the Red Sox on April 15 at Target Field. The left-hander reminded the Twins how dominant he can be when he has his slider working. Liriano gave up no runs and just four hits while striking out eight and walking just two over seven innings of work. Liriano wasn't as impressive in his debut in a no-decision in an extra-inning victory over the White Sox on April 9, but still earned a quality start. Liriano logged six innings giving up three runs on four hits. He also walked five and struck out three. Liriano will look to extend his scoreless inning streak past seven when he next faces the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Huff was masterful in a complete-game victory over the Rangers on Thursday. He turned in a 104-pitch effort, throwing 71 pitches for strikes. He never needed more than 16 pitches to complete an inning, and he threw exactly 12 pitches in five innings. He allowed a two-run homer to Michael Young in the fourth inning, but that was the only real damage against him. He walked one and struck out four. Huff has only 25 starts at the Major League level, and he's won 12 of them. He's an intense competitor who knows how to win. And if he keeps pounding the strike zone like he did against Texas, he's going to keep piling up the wins.

home_pitcher_note: Baker was effective for the second straight outing in a victory over the Royals on April 16 at Target Field. In a workman-like effort, Baker pitched seven solid innings and surrendered just two runs. Baker gave up seven hits, struck out six and didn't walk a Kansas City batter. The Twins' No. 1 starter should be fresh for his next start against the Indians, as he only threw 92 pitches against the Royals. Baker gave up just one run in his previous start against the White Sox and also pitched seven innings in a 2-1 win. He struck out three Chicago batters and walked just one.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot made his first win at the Major League level a memorable one Friday against the White Sox. He went the distance, allowing just two runs (only one of which was earned) on six hits with no walks and two strikeouts. He threw just 97 pitches, 68 of which went for strikes. He did a good job getting his sinker and cutter in on left-handed hitters. Talbot has a deep arsenal, including a changeup that can be devastating the second or third time through an opponent's lineup. The Indians want to see him be aggressive early and then work in the offspeed stuff. He was effective early, middle and late against the Sox and he hopes to take that momentum into his start at Target Field.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer didn't allow an earned run for the second straight outing in his most recent start versus the Orioles, against which he allowed two unearned runs and seven hits while walking two and striking out five through 5 2/3 innings. The A's righty, whose season was in question following a spring that resulted in a nerve ablation procedure and just a handful of starts, still feels he's building up strength to go deeper in games. Still, he's given the A's back-to-back solid outings and will look to do the same against the Indians. In 11 games -- two starts -- against Cleveland, Duchscherer owns a 1-3 record with a 3.60 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It was vintage Westbrook on the mound against the White Sox on Saturday. Whereas the veteran sinkerballer looked a bit shaky and had some control woes on his first two starts after his return from 2008 Tommy John surgery, Westbrook was in fine form in his last outing. He went seven strong innings, allowing just two runs on five hits with three walks and two strikeouts. He induced 15 ground-ball outs, which is an indication that his sinker was working well. Alas, he was saddled with a no-decision because he couldn't protect a 1-0 lead. He hopes to have similar form and a better end result in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start since agreeing to a four-year extension with the A's, Anderson extended his scoreless streak to 14 innings on Sunday before struggling in his first loss of the season, an 8-3 defeat to the Orioles. He gave up five earned runs in five frames in the game as a result of his bread-and-butter pitch -- his slider -- not being effective. Anderson is looking to get back on track against the Indians, against whom he won in his only career start. He tossed six shutout innings of four-hit ball versus Cleveland last year.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona has been much more consistent this season, limiting the damage when he finds trouble and pounding the strike zone more effectively. He gave the Indians six strong innings in a win over the White Sox on Sunday, allowing three runs on six hits with two walks and four strikeouts. He issued first-pitch strikes to 19 of the 25 batters he faced, and that was the real key to his success. Carmona has gone at least six innings in each of his three starts thus far.

home_pitcher_note: In his third start of the season, Gonzalez took a loss against the Yankees after allowing five earned runs on three hits and five walks while striking out five in 4 1/3 innings. An excessive number of walks led to the southpaw's struggles for the second consecutive start. Gonzalez, who tossed 97 pitches in the short outing, issued a pair of walks in the first inning, then again in the fifth -- all of which led to the runs he allowed. In two career starts against the Indians, Gonzalez is 1-0 with a 2.79 ERA and 11 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson is coming off an ugly and inefficient outing against the Twins. In just four innings, he allowed five runs (two of which were earned) on five hits with five walks and six strikeouts. An Asdrubal Cabrera fielding error hurt him, but so did a costly bases-loaded walk, a wild pitch and a fielding error of his own. Masterson threw 96 pitches in that short span, and he once again struggled to tame left-handed hitters. He hasn't done much to dispute the notion that he might be better-served in a bullpen setting, but the Indians are giving him the opportunity to prove himself as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver continued his excellent start to the season with seven strong innings in a no-decision against the Tigers on Wednesday, holding them to two runs on six hits and two walks, striking out six men. Weaver had yielded only one hit and a walk entering the fifth, giving up a solo homer before leaving the bases loaded by striking out Johnny Damon looking. Weaver has had four straight quality starts, walking only five against 27 strikeouts in 26 innings. Weaver is 2-1 with a 4.17 ERA in eight career starts against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Huff went from an incredibly efficient complete game against the Rangers on May 15 to an inefficient, walk-prone start against the Twins on Wednesday. He walked a career-high six batters en route to giving up four runs on three hits in six innings. Such variation from start to start tends to happen for a young hurler like Huff. But he has proven to be capable of pounding both sides of the plate in the past, and it's a matter of doing so with consistency from start to start. He'll be looking for better results in this start near his Southern California roots.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders' uneven start to the 2010 season continued when he lasted only 2 2/3 innings against the Tigers on the heels of eight dominant innings in Toronto. Detroit reached the lefty for five earned runs on six hits and two walks, and he registered no strikeouts. Saunders, who gave up four doubles, has yielded 23 hits and six walks in 21 1/3 innings with eight strikeouts. He has fared well against the Indians in five career starts, going 2-0 with a 2.84 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot wasn't as efficient as he was in his previous start -- a complete-game victory over the White Sox -- but he was very effective in limiting the Twins to an unearned run on two hits with three walks and three strikeouts in a win over the Twins on Thursday. He induced three double-play balls. Talbot has a deep arsenal, including a changeup that can be devastating the second or third time through an opponent's order, because it keeps hitters off-balance. He has been a very effective offseason acquisition for the Tribe thus far.

home_pitcher_note: Santana wasn't as sharp against the Yankees on Friday night at Angel Stadium as he'd been in his previous start when he went the distance in snuffing Toronto, but he kept the Angels in the game and dueled A.J. Burnett on even terms in giving up four earned runs across six innings. Santana's command left him at times -- he hit two batters, one scoring -- but he battled his way through several crises with his premium stuff. Santana is overdue against the Indians. He's 0-6 with a 6.03 ERA against the Tribe in seven career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook was denied his first victory of the season after giving up four runs on eight hits in five-plus innings of work. The righty was pitching to contact in Oakland and the A's finally got to him in the sixth inning. Westbrook was ultimately done in after giving up a two-run homer to Kurt Suzuki in the sixth. Westbrook had command of his fastball and allowed just one walk in the outing, but his inability to put hitters away on two-strike counts caught up with him. He threw 101 pitches in the outing and struck out just one batter. In nine starts against the Angels, Westbrook is 3-5 with a 3.11 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona is coming off his best start of the season, giving up just one run on seven hits -- all singles -- over 7 1/3 innings and picking up win No. 3 against the A's, a team he has struggled against. Carmona, as he has throughout the season, pounded the strike zone. Against Oakland, he didn't walk a batter for the first time this season. He's 3-6 lifetime against the Twins with a 5.11 ERA and has allowed 66 hits in 61 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a masterful eight-inning start against the Indians, Slowey had difficulty finding the strike zone in last outing against the Royals. He threw 104 pitches over 5 1/3 innings as he allowed four runs on eight hits while walking three. Slowey was all around the strike zone, manager Ron Gardenhire said, but he couldn't seem to make enough adjustments. While Slowey's strikeout-to-walk ratio last season was an impressive 5.00, third-best among all American League starters, this year he hasn't been able to deliver the same results as this year it's 2.11. Slowey is 1-1 with a 2.57 ERA in two career starts at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson had his second straight rough outing Sunday in a loss to the A's. He gave up eight hits and seven runs and was chased without retiring a batter in the fifth after Kevin Kouzmanoff ripped a three-run double, putting the A's ahead, 7-0. Masterson again struggled with his control. He walked four and threw 96 pitches in his short stint. In his previous start, he walked five and threw 96 pitches in four innings against the Twins. He has now lost nine straight decisions and is 1-11 since coming to the Indians from Boston in a trade on July 31 last year.
away_pitcher_note: Manship will make his first start for the Twins this season, taking Kevin Slowey's place in the rotation after Slowey filled in for Nick Blackburn on Friday. Manship is 2-2 with a 3.48 ERA in four starts for Triple-A Rochester this season, and in sporadic appearances last season, he was 1-1 with a 5.68 ERA in 31 2/3 innings. His first two outings were against the Indians, and in a combined 2 2/3 innings, he allowed one hit and walked two, giving up no runs. Grady Sizemore, who drew a walk against Manship, is the only current Indian who has reached base against the right-hander.

home_pitcher_note: Huff didn't let walks get the best of him, as he had in his previous start against the Twins, but he nonetheless wasn't very efficient in a loss to the Angels on Monday. Huff allowed five runs on 12 hits with one walk and four strikeouts in just 5 1/3 innings. He worked his way out of a couple jams, but he gave up two home runs en route to his second loss in as many starts. When he tossed a complete game against the Rangers on April 15, Huff pounded the strike zone to induce quick outs. He needs to get back to that mentality when he faces the Twins for the second time in two weeks.
away_pitcher_note: One of the biggest questions for the Twins coming into the 2010 season was whether Liriano could duplicate his fantastic results from winter ball. So far it hasn't been difficult for the left-hander, whose 0.93 ERA is lowest among all American League pitchers. Liriano extended his career-high scoreless streak to 23 consecutive innings in his last start by shutting out the Tigers for eight innings. It's the second-longest active scoreless streak in the Majors behind only the Mets' Mike Pelfrey who has thrown 24 consecutive scoreless innings. A key for Liriano's success has been better command of his fastball as well as increase in confidence. He'll try to duplicate that success when he faces Cleveland for the second time this year. He pitched eight scoreless against the Tribe in that only start at Target Field.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot has been surprisingly stingy with the runs allowed this season. Plenty of balls get put in play against him, but he's done an excellent job limiting the damage on the scoreboard. Talbot has now notched three straight quality starts, allowing just two earned runs over 21 1/3 innings. In his last start against the Angels on Tuesday, he went 6 1/3 innings, allowing just a run on six hits with three walks and a strikeout. He got into a couple jams but was able to work his way out of them, thanks to his deep arsenal. To put it simply, the Indians are getting great value out of their fifth starter, who was the player to be named in the Kelly Shoppach trade with the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Despite losing, Cecil was simply outstanding in his last outing. He was limited to osix innings and 100 pitches, but the left-hander did all he could, surrendering only one run on five hits against a tough Boston lineup. The only run he allowed was on a Dustin Pedroia sacrifice fly in his last inning. Most impressive so far may be Cecil's ability to limit walks (two in 12 2/3 innings) and to throw strikes (62 percent of his pitches). The sophomore has limited Cleveland to one run in 13 career innings.

home_pitcher_note: It could be a product of missing nearly two years because of Tommy John elbow surgery, but Westbrook has had issues with endurance. His last start, against the Angels on Wednesday, was a prime example. Westbrook cruised for the better part of his first five innings, but he lost effectiveness in the sixth. He let the first two men of the inning aboard, then served up a game-tying, three-run homer to Torii Hunter, thereby saddling himself with no decision. Westbrook hasn't notched a Major League win since April 8, 2008. This will be his first start against Toronto since May 2, 2007.
away_pitcher_note: While Romero was not spectacular in his last outing vs. the A's on Wednesday, giving up three runs on four hits and four walks through six innings, he was still able to record his fifth straight quality start on his way to a 6-3 win. Romero was particularly happy with his outing, citing his ability to battle without his best stuff. The young left-hander will look to continue his success against the Indians, whom he has delivered a 1-0 record with a 2.25 ERA over eight career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona followed up his strongest start of the season with his least effective. Whereas he dominated the A's for 7 1/3 innings in Oakland on April 24, he labored in six innings against the Twins on Friday. He allowed six runs on eight hits with two walks, a wild pitch and two strikeouts. He was less efficient than he had been in previous outings, needing 102 pitches to get through the six innings. While the outing wasn't an outright disaster, it was a step back for Carmona, who had been steadily improving with each previous start in April.
away_pitcher_note: This season has been a tale of two Morrows. Through his first two starts of the season, Morrow surrendered 12 runs on 12 hits over nine innings. Through his past three starts, Morrow has pitched 19 innings and allowed only five runs while striking out 25. Morrow has even said that he feels more comfortable working out of the stretch this season, where he has been able to escape several jams via the strikeout. Morrow, who was plagued by the home run in his first two starts (three), has not given up a long ball over his past three outings, a sign of increased control. The right-hander has never started a game vs. the Indians, but is 1-1 with a 4.26 ERA in a relief role.

home_pitcher_note: Huff was victimized by the long ball in a loss to the Twins on Sunday. He allowed four runs on 10 hits with two walks and two strikeouts in five innings. All of the runs came in as a result of home runs. Since tossing a complete-game victory against the Rangers on April 15, Huff has lost three straight starts and given up 13 runs in 16 1/3 innings along the way. He faced the Tigers on April 9 and allowed four runs (one earned) on six hits over six innings in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman's first month back in the Tigers rotation was about slow, steady progress after shoulder surgery to correct a blood vessel restriction cost him the better part of two seasons. His last start was an encouraging one in that regard despite 10 hits allowed over six innings against the Angels. His fastball velocity averaged higher than at any point since surgery, and his top speed of 94 mph is believed to be his best since his younger days four years ago. He's throwing an increasing number of splitters and has been drawing more swings and misses as he sharpens it. Bonderman is 8-9 lifetime against the Indians, including a victory in the Tigers' home opener on April 9.

home_pitcher_note: One reason why Masterson has not been quite as effective as a starter as the Indians hope is his struggles early in the game. He has a 10.80 ERA and a .423 average against in his five first innings this season. The first time through the lineup, the opposition is batting .333 (14-for-42) off him. The second time through, they are batting .421 (16-for-38). Early, middle or late in games, left-handers continue to be Masterson's nemesis. They are batting .414 (24-for-58) with a 1.148 OPS against him.
away_pitcher_note: What used to be a house of horrors for Verlander in Cleveland became a springboard for him around this point last year, when some minor mechanical tweaks and an acrobatic catch by Curtis Granderson put him in line for a complete-game victory. Verlander beat the Indians four times last year and hasn't lost to the Tribe since 2008. He took a no-decision against Cleveland on the season's opening weekend.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot was not nearly as dominant against the Blue Jays on Monday as he had been against his previous three opponents. He had allowed just two earned runs over his previous 21 1/3 innings, but the Jays changed his fortune by roughing him up for five runs on eight hits, including three homers, with four walks and five strikeouts over eight-plus innings. Talbot settled in after a rough early going, but the trouble he had keeping the ball in the park hurt him. He had allowed just two homers in his four previous starts this season. Talbot faced the Tigers on April 10 and gave up four runs on six hits over five innings in his Tribe debut.
away_pitcher_note: The good news for Scherzer is that he won't have to face the Twins again for a while after Minnesota's hitters roughed him up in back-to-back starts. But it won't mean much until he regains his command. Sliders that were meant for the corner ended up over the middle of the plate, and Twins hitters put them in the outfield gaps. He gave up 10 runs on eight hits over 4 1/3 innings Monday at Target Field, and has surrendered 16 runs on 18 hits in just eight innings over his past two outings. He has never faced the Indians, but his three quality starts this season were all on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister lasted just three-plus innings against the White Sox last Wednesday night, giving up seven hits, including a homer, and four walks. That was in direct contrast to his previous outing when he held the hard-hitting Rays to two hits and one run in seven innings. Bannister burned up 63 pitches and, with just 34 strikes, he kept getting behind in the count. And when he did get the ball over the plate, it was too often belt-high and down the middle. Against the Indians, he's been quite successful with a 4-1 record and a 2.34 ERA in eight games started.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook was nearly scratched from his start against the Blue Jays on May 4 because of tightness in his back. It turned out to be a short start, anyway, because Westbrook got roughed up for four runs (three earned) on five hits with five walks and three strikeouts in just 3 2/3 innings of work. He is still searching for his first win since April 2008. Command has been a major issue for Westbrook thus far, and that's no doubt attributable to the nearly two years he missed following Tommy John surgery.

home_pitcher_note: After working back-to-back gems, Davies laid a clunker last Thursday night at Texas. He lasted just four-plus innings and gave up nine runs on nine hits and three walks. However, he escaped the loss when the Royals charged from behind only to lose a 13-12 slugfest. Not surprisingly, Davies classified the outing as his worst of the season primarily because of lack of command (he made 100 pitches, 59 strikes). Davies had good success against the Indians last year, going 2-0 with a 2.31 ERA in two games. In his career, though, it's 3-3 with a 6.18 ERA against the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona was solid in a no-decision against the Blue Jays on May 5, holding a potent lineup to a pair of runs on seven hits over 6 1/3 innings. He began to lose control in his last two innings of work, but Carmona has done a good job limiting the damage against him this season, even on the nights when he walks people. He has gone at least six innings in all of his starts this season, and that's partly attributable to his ability to get ground-ball double plays when he gets in trouble.

home_pitcher_note: Who would have believed after what Greinke accomplished in his Cy Young Award season last year that he would be winless after seven starts this year? But that's the case even though he's pitched well enough to have at least three or four wins by now. That ERA is no mirage. He's allowed three or fewer earned runs in six of his seven outings and pitched at least six innings in six of the seven. But he's been the victim of non-support with the Royals averaging just 2.4 runs a game when he starts and totaling only one run in the last two games. He faced the Indians five times last year and was 2-0 with a 2.16 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Huff had an outing to forget Friday against the Tigers and, lucky for him, he gets to forget it. In just 2 2/3 innings, he was beaten up for seven runs on eight hits with a walk and two strikeouts. He didn't make it out of the third inning. But rain washed the game away after four innings and, because it didn't reach the regulation point, none of the damage against Huff officially counts. Still, it is a matter of concern for the Indians that he had trouble getting ahead with his fastball for the fourth straight start. Huff tossed a complete-game gem against the Rangers on April 15, but hasn't had a quality start since.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie finally wiped the goose egg from his win total on Saturday afternoon, allowing a pair of homers -- which accounted for all three Twins runs -- in Baltimore's 7-3 win over Minnesota. Guthrie has faced tough mound counterparts all year and outdueled Francisco Liriano en route to his first victory, which snapped a personal eight-game losing skid. Coming off a dismal 2009, the right-handed Guthrie has an improved arm angle and approach this season and it shows. He will look to build on Saturday's win with another "W" Friday against the Indians, who selected Guthrie in the first-round of the '02 Draft. He is 1-0 in three games (one start) against Cleveland, posting a 7.56 ERA over 8 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson still hasn't won a game this season, but at least he's trending in the right direction. He went six innings against the Tigers on May 8, allowing three runs on five hits with three walks and eight strikeouts. This came after he allowed four runs on 10 hits in 7 2/3 innings in a no-decision against the Twins on May 1. Masterson still has to prove he can consistently tame lefties, and he has to limit the baserunners against him. But in his last two starts, he's given his team a chance to win, and that's a start.

home_pitcher_note: Every pitcher is prone to the occasional clunker of an outing, and Matusz's first of 2010 came in his last start, on Sunday in a 6-0 loss at Minnesota. The left-hander didn't get out of the fourth inning, the second-shortest outing of his brief Major League career, and was touched for a season-high six runs. When Matusz succeeds, it's all about rhythm and his ability to stay ahead in counts and challenge hitters. When that happens, Matusz seizes control and makes life difficult for batters. When it doesn't, the scales tip in the hitters' favor. However, Matusz has been universally praised for his unflappability, and that poise will serve him well as he tries to rebound from a subpar start.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot has battled without his best stuff his last two times out. He gave up five runs on eight hits, but made it through eight innings against the Blue Jays on May 3. And on May 9, he allowed four runs on six hits with four walks and four strikeouts in five innings against the Tigers. He got offensive backing in the latter effort to walk out with his fourth win. Talbot has four pitches that he can adequately rely on at the Major League level. So even when one or two of them betray him, he has other weapons to help get him through.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez dropped his 11th straight decision Tuesday night, allowing five runs (four earned) on five hits in 5 2/3 innings, walking four and striking out four. The Orioles have lost 14 of 16 games started by the right-hander since he beat Oakland on Aug. 11, 2009."There's one inning that usually costs him, two outs nobody on, something happens," Trembley said of Hernandez, who cruised through Tuesday's first four innings before issuing a two-out bases-loaded walk in the fifth. Despite his struggles, the Orioles still believe in Hernandez, with Trembley saying on Thursday that there are no plans to remove him from the rotation. The young right-hander, who just turned 25, will look to snap his long losing streak in Sunday's finale. He is a 0-1 in two career starts against the Indians with a 3.00 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook's long, long wait for a victory finally ended Tuesday night in Kansas City. He worked six strong innings against the Royals, allowing just a run on five hits with two walks and two strikeouts. It was his first win since way back on April 8, 2008, after Westbrook missed nearly two years following June 2008 elbow surgery. Staying effective into the late innings has been an issue for Westbrook this season, and he ran up his pitch count to 103 in these six innings. But what mattered most is he didn't have as many command woes that have given him trouble at time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Niemann again pitched well Tuesday, when he held the Angels to two runs on six hits in 7 1/3 innings to pick up his third win of the season. Niemann now has six quality starts in seven outings; the only outing in which he did not produce a quality start was in his first start of the season when he got hit by a line drive and had to leave the game after retiring the first four hitters. Because Niemann stands 6-foot-9, he creates a difficult downward angle for hitters, who rarely face a pitcher of his height. Niemann is 0-1 with a 3.00 ERA in one career start against Cleveland; he is 7-3 with a 3.16 ERA in 18 appearances at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona will start the opener of a brief two-game series in Tampa Bay as the Indians close out their eight-game road trip. The right-hander is having a much better season this year than last. He struggled throughout 2009, finishing with a 5-12 record and a 6.32 ERA, also enduring a trip to the Minors to get his form back. But the right-hander won his first three decisions this season and has been more like his old self. Carmona is tied for fourth in the American League in wins, and this will be his eighth start of the season. He gave up no runs on five hits over five innings in his last start, on Wednesday against Kansas City, as the Indians posted a 4-0 shutout. Carmona left after rain delayed the game for a second time. If Carmona can keep improving, it will be a huge help to an Indians team that's been scraping for runs all season.

home_pitcher_note: Price said he had his best stuff of the season Wednesday in Anaheim when he held the Angels to two earned runs in 6 1/3 innings to pick up his fifth win of the season. The No. 1 pick of the 2007 First-Year Player Draft has shown a lot of improvement in his fastball command, which has made his slider and curve even more effective. Price is 0-0 with a 5.40 ERA in one career start against Cleveland; he is 10-3 with a 2.68 ERA in 16 appearances at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: A closed-door meeting with manager Manny Acta and pitching coach Tim Belcher followed Huff's last outing, a loss to the Royals. In that loss, Huff allowed six runs on nine hits over 5 2/3 innings. The point of the meeting was that Huff needs to learn to trust his fastball and not give too much credit to the opposing hitter. He has been rather tentative in the course of allowing 19 runs over his last 22 innings of work. He also got knocked around May 7 in a game washed away by rain. The past month, Huff has not looked like the guy who threw a complete-game gem against the Rangers on April 15.

home_pitcher_note: Just when it appeared Masterson was starting to figure things out, he got knocked around in a loss to the Orioles on Friday. He allowed six runs on eight hits with five walks and four strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings of work. He is still searching for his first win of 2010, and the Indians' decision to place him in the rotation upon his arrival from Boston last year still hasn't paid off.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Chicago White Sox last Friday night, Meche tossed six innings, giving up four hits and one earned run in a 6-1 victory, although he did not factor into the decision. One strength of Meche's last start against the White Sox was his control as he only walked two of the 25 batters he faced. The 6-foot-3 righty is still in search of his first win of the season as the Royals are trying to get back on track under new manager Ned Yost.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot continues to be a surprisingly good find for a Tribe team that acquired him from the Rays for catcher Kelly Shoppach over the winter. He tossed eight effective innings against the Orioles on Saturday. He allowed just two runs on five hits with two walks and three strikeouts. It was the third time Talbot has gone at least eight innings this season. He has yet to face Kansas City this season or in his career, for that matter.
away_pitcher_note: In Hochevar's most recent start, against the White Sox on Saturday night, everything seemed to be going fine for the righty -- that is, until the seventh inning. Before that dreaded frame, Hochevar had given up only two hits, a walk and a run through six innings. That all changed in the seventh, when he was banged up for four runs that accompanied five hits and a walk. Hochevar pitched 6 1/3 innings, giving up five earned runs on seven hits with two walks en route to his second loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Maybe he's not all the way back to being the Westbrook of old, but he's sure getting there. After struggling to find consistent command in his first five starts after his return from 2008 Tommy John surgery, Westbrook has been solid his last two times out. Over his last 15 innings, he's allowed just two earned runs. On Sunday against the Orioles, he tossed his first complete game since April 8, 2008, and he won for the second straight start. He's getting as much effectiveness out of his changeup as he is his go-to sinkerball. He hopes to keep the run going against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo pitched his first complete game of the season in Sunday's 7-2 win over the Cardinals. He allowed two earned runs and seven hits with three walks and four strikeouts while throwing 108 pitches. He eluded danger a few times, including his inducing of inning-ending double plays in the first and second innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona took a no-decision he didn't necessarily deserve Monday night in Tampa Bay. He gave the Tribe 6 2/3 innings in which he allowed just two runs on five hits with one walk and seven strikeouts. Both runs came in the first inning. Once Carmona settled in, he retired 19 of 20 batters he faced in a dominant stretch. He kept his composure after the rough early going, and that's yet another sign that he's a different guy from the one who labored through 2008 and 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto has strung together a couple of nice starts. He gave up one run and seven hits with seven strikeouts in Monday's 6-3 win over the Brewers. After allowing no walks the previous time out, he walked only one batter against Milwaukee. He's trying to take a little off of his pitches lately. Instead of trying to throw 94-96 mph, he's trying 92-93 so hitters will be more likely to put the ball in play and he can let the defense do the work.

home_pitcher_note: Huff had baserunners aplenty in his start against the Rays on Tuesday, and it ended up biting him in the loss. He allowed three runs on seven hits with three walks and two strikeouts in five innings. The Indians wanted to see him show more faith in his fastball, and initially he was successful in pitching his way out of trouble. Ultimately, though, he used too many pitches (103) in too short a time and had to be pulled. Huff has now lost five straight starts, posting a 7.33 ERA in the process, and the Indians' patience with him might be wearing thin.
away_pitcher_note: In a 5-4 win last time out, Bailey did not figure in the decision but had a decent outing. Over seven innings, he allowed two runs and four hits. But he gave up only one hit after a 30-pitch first inning in which Milwaukee took a 2-0 lead. "From there, I did not really cruise but went through the next couple of innings and tried to keep the team in the game," Bailey said. "To get seven in and only give up two is still a pretty good start."

home_pitcher_note: Masterson is still looking for his first win since Aug. 20 of last year. He didn't get it against the Royals on Wednesday. He allowed just two runs on five hits, but he needed 106 pitches to get through only five innings of work in a no-decision. He needs to be more efficient, and he needs to improve his performance against left-handers if he's going to have success as a starter. For now, such success has been very elusive to Masterson.
away_pitcher_note: John Danks has pitched well enough to win his last three games, but he has thrice been thwarted by the opposing pitcher pitching just a little bit better than him. In each of his last three starts he's gone seven innings or more and given up three runs or fewer, but he has emerged the hard-luck loser in each contest. In his last start against the Angels, Danks gave up one hit through seven innings. That one hit was a two-run home run to Torii Hunter, and an unearned run in the eighth doomed Danks to the loss. Against the Indians, Danks is 2-5 in 10 career starts, with a 4.89 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Because he has a four-pitch arsenal, Talbot can be fairly effective, even on the days he doesn't have his best stuff. But he didn't have anything to work with in a loss to the Royals on Thursday, and it showed as he allowed six runs on eight hits with three walks and a strikeout over six innings. In general, Talbot has been a pleasant surprise in the back end of the Tribe rotation. But this start was evidence that without overpowering stuff, Talbot will have his rocky days.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy struggled in his last start, giving up six earned runs and earning the loss against the Los Angeles Angels. The six earned runs was the most he had in a start since April 28 against the Rangers. Strangely enough, Peavy piched well in his six innings, fanning eight batters. But a well-executed hit and run and a two-run homer cost Peavy three runs. After the game, Peavy said that he believed he was the reason for the team's 6-5 loss. "It's frustrating for myself, because I feel solely responsible for this loss tonight. Out there, I felt good," he said. Lifetime, he is 1-1 with a 4.70 ERA against the Indians. In his last start against the Indians on April 17, he went 7 1/3 and gave up just two earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook's streak of two dominant starts ended in his last outing against the Reds, but the veteran righty had only one bad inning against Cincinnati. Victimized by Jonny Gomes' towering two-run shot in the fourth inning, Westbrook gave up three that inning. The Reds ran up his pitch count, and Westbrook checked out after five innings, charged with four runs on seven hits and two walks. Westbrook, who didn't factor into the decision, struck out three. Westbrook had allowed two runs in 15 innings before facing the Reds, winning two straight starts. Westbrook has already faced the White Sox twice this season, losing on Opening Day and taking a no-decision 12 days later. Westbrook has allowed five runs on 10 hits and seven walks in eight innings against the Pale Hose this year, fanning three.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle returned to form in his last start against the Marlins, as he went eight shutout innings, which was enough to snap what had been a five-game losing streak. Buehrle also stopped what had been a 65-at-bat streak in which he went without a strikeout when he fanned Hanley Ramirez in the sixth inning. The win made Buehrle the third pitcher in baseball history to win 20 games in Interleague Play, along with Mike Mussina and Jamie Moyer. Against the Indians lifetime, he is 12-15, with a 6-7 ledger at Progressive Field.

Carmona gave up five runs on seven hits with two walks and four strikeouts over six innings in his start against the Reds on Saturday. Two of the runs were unearned, as the Indians played sloppy defense behind him. Still, Carmona was not at his sharpest. His slider was flat early in the ballgame, and he struggled against the Reds' left-handed hitters. Carmona has a 2.63 ERA over his past four starts. He's lasted at least six innings in eight of nine starts and thrown a quality start seven times.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia takes the mound looking to snap his string of winless starts on Saturday. The lefty allowed six runs (five earned) on 10 hits to the Mets on May 23, a five-inning losing effort. Sabathia has not won since May 3 at Baltimore, a span of four starts, although he was one out shy of qualifying for a victory on May 8 when rain forced him from a 14-3 win over the Red Sox. Sabathia is 1-0 with a 2.84 ERA in two career starts against his former team.
away_pitcher_note: Huff wasn't perfect in his start against the Reds on Sunday, but he was much improved over previous efforts and might have calmed some talk about him possibly getting sent down to the Minors. He ended a streak of five straight starts with a loss. He allowed three runs on six hits with a walk and four strikeouts over six innings. He served up two home run balls but nevertheless gave his team a chance to win and earned his first victory since April 15.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett gets the nod on Sunday, looking for his second consecutive win. Burnett hurled five innings of scoreless, three-hit ball on May 25 at Minnesota, but threw only 75 pitches before rain forced the game to be suspended heading to the sixth. Derek Jeter homered to make a winner of Burnett, who is 2-2 in five May starts. He is 1-4 with a 6.69 ERA in six career starts vs. Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson remains in the Indians' rotation, for now. But suffice to say he's on shaky ground, given his results in a starting role the past two seasons. He hasn't notched a win since Aug. 20, 2009, losing 11 consecutive decisions. That's just two shy of a team record. He has a 1.89 WHIP and a .386 average against when facing lefties. He was roughed up for five runs on nine hits in four innings in a loss to the White Sox on Monday. The Indians might end up moving Aaron Laffey from the bullpen to the rotation. But for now, they're sticking with Masterson, one of three pitchers acquired in last summer's Victor Martinez trade with the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte will get the ball as the Yankees wrap up their set with Cleveland on Monday. He was excellent on May 26 at Minnesota, holding the Twins to two runs on eight hits in eight innings, walking none and striking out four in a 94-pitch winning effort. Pettitte is 3-1 with a 3.33 ERA in four starts this month, with his only loss coming against the Rays on May 20. Pettitte is 7-8 with a 4.41 ERA in 19 career starts vs. Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot righted himself after a shaky outing against the Royals with an effective and incredibly efficient effort against the White Sox on Tuesday. He needed just 77 pitches to get through seven innings in which he allowed just a pair of runs on six hits with four strikeouts. The big key was the zero walks he allowed as he used his four-pitch arsenal to pound the strike zone and get quick outs. He began to lose effectiveness in his seventh and final inning, giving up four doubles. But this was nonetheless another solid effort for Talbot, who has been a pleasant surprise in the back end of the rotation for an Indians team that acquired him in the Kelly Shoppach trade with the Rays over the winter.

home_pitcher_note: Yes, Bonderman owns only one win out of his last eight starts, but with the way he pitched in May, it's hard to blame him for it. He owns quality starts in each of his last four official starts, not counting the rough night he had in a rained-out performance in Cleveland. He allowed just four earned runs on 23 hits over 27 innings in May, walking seven and striking out 26. That includes seven innings without an earned run last Wednesday in Seattle. Now, he'll begin June with a rematch against the Tribe, whose damage against him at Progressive Field consisted almost entirely of one inning.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook was not at his sharpest in a loss to the White Sox on May 26, as he allowed five runs on six hits over seven innings. But Westbrook did keep his team in the ballgame, and the endurance and pain-free outings he's turned in this season are signs that he's made it all the way back from Tommy John surgery in 2008. Now, he just needs to find the consistent command that made him a consistent winner before injuries derailed his career. This will be Westbrook's first start against the Tigers this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers chose Galarraga to stick in the rotation over Dontrelle Willis, who was designated for assignment over the weekend. Now, Galarraga will try to back up the vote of confidence on the mound when he starts for the first time in a week and a half. His future was in serious question after the Dodgers roughed him up over four-plus innings May 22 in Los Angeles. He had an extended side session last Wednesday in which he tried to work on his slider, his workhorse pitch that needs more consistency, then took it into a relief outing Friday against Oakland with some effectiveness. Galarraga earned three of his 13 wins in 2008 at Cleveland's expense, but lost all three of his meetings with the Indians last year.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona hung in there against the Yankees in a loss Friday night, but he had some issues with control that hurt him and ran up his pitch count. He needed 34 pitches to get through the sixth inning, and with his count over 100 after that point, he wasn't able to take it any further. He gave up four runs on seven hits with three walks and three strikeouts in six innings. The good news is that Carmona has gone at least six innings in all but one of his 10 starts this season. He's generally been able to keep the Indians in games. This is his first start against the Tigers this season.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello has alternated wins and losses in his past seven outings, though he owns quality starts in three of his past four assignments. He gave up two runs on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings last Saturday against Oakland, taking the loss. Porcello beat the Indians in the Tigers' home opener back in April, adding to his success against the Indians. He's 4-0 with a 2.10 ERA in five career starts against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Huff is making his next turn in the rotation, and that seems like a miracle to those who saw him whacked in the head by an Alex Rodriguez line drive in the third inning of his start against the Yankees on Saturday. Huff was taken off the field on a motorized cart and taken to a nearby hospital, where a CT scan showed no brain damage and doctors determined he had no signs of a concussion. Huff threw a bullpen session two days later and was confirmed to be making this start. The only question is whether he'll have any lingering fear of another lined shot.

home_pitcher_note: Saturday's 8-5 loss to the Rays marked the lone blemish on an otherwise All-Star-caliber season for the young left-hander. Danks had not allowed more than three runs in a start during his first nine trips to the mound, but was pounded for eight runs on eight hits over four-plus innings at Tropicana Field. It was Danks' first loss at the Rays' home. He struck out two and walked three, but Danks threw 102 pitches. Danks has a 1-0 record against the Indians this season and has a 3-5 career mark. Danks enters the start with a 35-37 career record and has a lifetime mark of 15-21 at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: With plenty of speculation about his fate in the Indians' rotation, Masterson turned in one of his strongest starts as a member of the Tribe on Sunday in the Bronx. He went 6 2/3 innings against a dangerous lineup and allowed three runs on seven hits, striking out eight. But he was a victim of more tough luck, as the bullpen let him down and he was saddled with a no-decision. So Masterson's stretch of 11 consecutive losing decisions remains intact. He hasn't notched a win since last Aug. 20. He's still on somewhat shaky ground, but he improved his standing with this strong start.

home_pitcher_note: When Peavy takes the mound on Saturday night against the Indians at U.S. Cellular Field, the right-hander will be in search of his 100th career victory. Peavy hopes to hit that target with a bit more ease than it took to pick up No. 99 on Sunday in St. Petersburg. Peavy allowed five runs on 10 hits over 5 1/3 innings, striking out five, and exiting in the sixth at 110 pitches. Peavy has given up 17 earned runs over 17 1/3 innings in his past three starts and needed 34 pitches to get through a two-run fifth inning alone against the Rays. Peavy has a 0-1 record against Cleveland this year and a 1-2 mark lifetime against the Indians. He holds a 4-2 record at U.S. Cellular.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot turned in a gritty start against the Yankees on Monday, giving the Tribe 6 1/3 respectable innings against a tough lineup. He was not rewarded for his efforts, as his supporting cast in the bullpen and the lineup let him down. Talbot was charged with three runs on nine hits with no walks and three strikeouts, and he was handed a fourth loss that he arguably didn't deserve. Talbot pitched his way out of several jams, which ran up his pitch count. He hopes to have a little more luck against the Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle struggled through his last start, a 5 1/3-inning effort against the Rangers. After Buehrle threw 34 pitches in the first inning, yet danced out of trouble, the Rangers finally got to him to the tune of five runs in the sixth inning. Buehrle managed to not allow a run through the first two innings, despite allowing four hitters to reach base. In that sixth inning, four consecutive hitters singled, and Buehrle left the game tied at 4. Buehrle walked only one but allowed 12 hits, including 10 singles. In his career, Buehrle is 12-15 in 39 starts against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: If Westbrook wasn't all the way back to his pre-injury form before Tuesday night's start at Comerica Park, he might be now. Westbrook was magnificent in guiding the Tribe to a 3-2 victory over the Tigers on Tuesday. He worked quickly, stayed ahead and allowed just one run on five hits with a walk and a strikeout over 7 2/3 innings. In April, Westbrook returned from a 22-month absence following Tommy John surgery. His rust showed early in the season, but his command has improved as the year has rolled along. And in this game, he was at his best, no doubt fueling speculation that he might be targeted by contenting clubs at next month's Trade Deadline.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona turned in his best start of the season Wednesday night at Comerica Park. He just so happened to do so on the night Armando Galarraga nearly threw the 21st perfect game in Major League history. Still, take nothing away from Carmona, who allowed just three runs (two earned) on nine hits with no walks over eight innings. It was his first complete game of the season. People will remember the missed call at first base that robbed Galarraga of a perfect game, but it was another mistake on another close play at first that wound up costing Carmona two runs in the eighth. He was in top form against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: The Red Sox aren't sure which version of Dice-K they're getting since he returned from the disabled list. When he's been his old self, Matsuzaka has been tough to hit, as he was three starts ago, when he allowed one hit and walked four in eight shutout innings against the Indians. When he's struggled, however, Matsuzaka has walked too many hitters, like the eight free passes he issued versus Kansas City on May 27. Most troubling has been the lack of strikeouts. Matsuzaka has fanned more than five only twice in seven games. Luckily, his most recent outing, Wednesday against Oakland, was a seven-strikeout effort in which he got a victory despite yielding 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Incredibly, Huff was able to make his next turn in the rotation after getting socked in the head by an Alex Rodriguez line drive in the Bronx on May 29. Unfortunately for Huff, his return against the Tigers on Thursday at Comerica Park did not go to plan. He was not sharp, allowing five runs on six hits with two walks, no strikeouts and a hit batter over three-plus innings. Give Huff credit for his ability to bounce back from what could have been a traumatic experience. But he still needs to improve his execution at the Major League level.
away_pitcher_note: The 18-year-veteran is coming off two poor starts, and his knuckleball better start dipping, darting and missing hitters' bats before he works himself out of the rotation, where he's made three consecutive starts. Against Oakland on Thursday, Wakefield surrendered six runs on eight hits in six innings of a 9-8 loss. Eating up innings does the Red Sox no good if Wakefield can't keep the opposition from scoring. He's experienced a mixed bag against Cleveland in his career, posting a lifetime 11-8 record and 4.23 ERA in 27 appearances, including 22 starts. In his eight starts this season, Wakefield has failed to make it through five innings only once.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson grabbed his first win since Aug. 20, 2009, in his last start against the Chicago White Sox. He struggled with his control, walking six and hitting two more batters, but his only run came off Alexei Ramirez's solo home run. The losing streak had lasted 11 games before he finally got that elusive win. "It felt like Justin took about a 3,000-pound gorilla off his back winning tonight, and it was good for him," Indians manager Manny Acta said. Masterson came up in the Red Sox system, but he has never faced them in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Buchholz has been on a tear since losing to the Yankees on May 8. The right-hander has won each of his last five starts. In his last outing, he dominated the Orioles, giving up five hits and a walk in a shutout victory at Camden Yards. Buchholz fanned just two batters that night, but controlled the game and had 11 runs, giving him way more support than he needed. Buchholz last faced the Indians on October 4, 2009, when he allowed six runs on five hits and two walks in three innings. Buchholz will look to improve upon his performance from that night, when he did not factor into the decision.

home_pitcher_note: Mitch Talbot continued to be one of the best starters for the Indians in his last outing, as he outdueled Jake Peavy for the second consecutive time to earn win No. 7 on the season. On two consecutive starts against the White Sox, Talbot has faced Jake Peavy, and both times he has gotten the win. On Saturday, he went seven innings, only giving up a run on Ramon Castro's RBI single in the fourth inning. Lifetime against the Red Sox, Talbot has just one game, a relief appearance from when he was on the Rays. In that game, he gave up four earned runs over three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lester has not lost in nearly two months. Victorious in his last four starts, the lefty went 6 1/3 scoreless innings against Baltimore for his most recent win. He punched out four hitters that night, scattering four hits and three walks. No one has beaten Lester since he lost to the Rays on April 18. Since then, he has won seven of nine starts, reversing his 0-2 start to the season. Lester compiled a 1-0 record in two starts last season against the Tribe. After taking a no-decision during an April game at Progressive Field in which he gave up five runs on seven hits and three walks, Lester turned in a solid performance in the season's final week, pitching 6 1/3 innings of scoreless, two-hit ball.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook struggled in his last start against the White Sox. Despite being staked to an early 6-2 lead on the strength of two early three-run innings, Westbrook fell apart in the fifth inning and got a no-decision in the Indians' 8-6 loss to the White Sox. "I just wasn't very consistent with either one of [my arm slots], over the top or dropping down," Westbrook said after his last start. "I was just very erratic today and didn't get the job done." In his only start against the Washington Nationals, Westbrook lost, giving up seven hits, no walks and three runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Last Saturday, Atilano pitched well enough to win, but the Nationals lost to the Reds, 5-1, at Nationals Park. Atilano had arguably his best-pitched game of the season, throwing seven innings, allowing two runs -- one earned -- on six hits. He struck out six batters and walked one, which pleased manager Jim Riggleman. Atilano ended up being outpitched by Reds right-hander and fellow rookie Mike Leake, who allowed one unearned run in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona logged his ninth quality start of the season Monday, scattering five hits and six walks over six-plus innings of three-run ball in a 4-1 loss to the Red Sox at Progressive Field. Cleveland manager Manny Acta praised the right-hander after the game for maintaining his composure on the mound, which has been an issue for the Dominican sinkerballer in recent seasons. Three years removed from the 19-win season that gained him recognition around the Majors, Carmona has once again emerged as a reliable rotation option for the Tribe in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Since rejoining the Nationals in late May, Martin has walked one batter in 11 2/3 innings. His success on the mound is one of the reasons right-hander Craig Stammen was sent down to Triple-A Syracuse.

home_pitcher_note: Huff recovered from an abysmal outing against the Tigers (not to mention the beaning he took from an Alex Rodriguez liner one start earlier) to give the Indians six strong innings against the Red Sox on Tuesday night. If not for a two-out Trevor Crowe error in center field that opened the door to a three-run fourth inning for Boston, Huff would have been in line for a victory. He allowed just those three runs, all of which were unearned, on eight hits with a walk and six strikeouts. This was an important pick-me-up outing for Huff, who continues to have to prove himself in the Tribe rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Making his Major League debut after 11 sensational Minor League starts, Strasburg pitched seven innings of two-run ball against the Pirates on Tuesday, earning the win and striking out 14 in a 5-2 victory. Delwyn Young's two-run home run with two outs in the fourth was the only damage against Strasburg. A sellout crowd of 40,315 saw Strasburg allow just four hits. The 14 strikeouts established a club record and were one shy of the record in a debut set by Karl Spooner in 1954 and J.R. Richard in '71. Even more amazing was that he struck out no more than nine batters in a game when pitching in the Minor Leagues. Strasburg, who did the job without looking at scouting reports, threw 94 pitches, 65 for strikes, and didn't walk a batter. The righty retired his final 10 batters, striking out his last seven.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson collected his second victory in as many outings Wednesday after going winless since last August. Making his first career appearance against the Red Sox, the 25-year-old right-hander limited his former team to just two hits in a shutout at Progressive Field. He struck out six and induced 17 groundouts and threw 110 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his finest stretch of the season (a 1.42 ERA over his previous six starts), Santana was something less than perfect last Wednesday against the Padres. Walking four, he allowed eight hits -- two of them RBI doubles -- and four runs in 6 2/3 innings, his shortest outing since allowing 10 runs to the Phillies in 3 2/3 innings on May 2. Santana will start Tuesday's opener in Cleveland, a place that troubled him at times during his days with the Twins. In 16 career games at Progressive Field, Santana is 4-4 with a 3.74 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot pitched a career-low four innings Thursday night, yielding five runs (two earned) on six hits in an 8-7 win against the Red Sox at Progressive Field. He walked four and struck out two in the 99-pitch outing. The rookie right-hander is 2-1 with a 2.96 ERA over his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Feeling refreshed in his second start since returning from the disabled list, Niese threw his signature curveball more often -- and with good results. He allowed just one hit to the Padres, a double to Chris Denorfia in the third. And he retired 21 straight batters thereafter to complete the one-hitter. Niese has been a different pitcher since returning from the disabled list, citing a fully-healed right hamstring as the reason. He will look to continue his momentum against the Indians, a team he has never faced.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook earned his fourth victory in five decisions Friday night, scattering seven hits over 7 1/3 innings of two-run ball in the Indians' 7-2 victory against the Nationals at Progressive Field. The veteran right-hander walked two and struck out five in the 113-pitch outing. He has logged seven innings in three of his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Knuckleball specialist R.A. Dickey has been a real find for the Mets and will attempt to continue his magical run against the Indians, against whom he owns a 1-0 lifetime record in eight appearances, including two starts. Dickey has been using an effective power knuckler, which flutters to the plate as high as 82 mph. Hitters claim the increased speed -- about 15-20 mph faster than the typical knuckleball -- and its movement make it a difficult pitch to hit. For now, Mets skipper Jerry Manuel is confident enough with Dickey in the rotation that he's backed off on pleas for general manager Omar Minaya to add an experienced starter to the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm made a bunch of critical pitches with runners on base in his last outing, and he managed to get himself out of almost every jam. Though Detroit had runners swarming the bases all throughout Maholm's six-inning, 104-pitch effort, the left-hander allowed just one run and stranded eight. There's no question that Maholm has been the Pirates' best pitcher this season. He's gone at least six innings in all but two of his 13 starts. And five of his last six starts have been quality ones. The Pirates are 7-6 when Maholm starts, which is better than the team's record with any other starter. Maholm allowed one run in 5 1/3 innings against the Indians in a start against Cleveland in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona fired his fifth career complete game Saturday night, yielding one run on three hits and facing just one batter over the minimum in the Indians' 7-1 victory against the Nationals at Progressive Field. The 26-year-old right-hander struck out seven and did not walk a batter in his 106-pitch outing. He has logged 10 quality starts in 13 outings this season, allowing three or fewer earned runs in all but two appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens deserved to win his second game of the year on Sunday after making his strongest performance to date this season. Through seven innings, he limited Detroit to one solo homer and three singles. He was charged with one more run after giving up a leadoff hit in the eighth, but that would be it. The key for Karstens was terrific fastball command. That helped him through the outing even though he had trouble throwing his breaking pitches for strikes. Karstens has become a pretty stable presence in the rotation, and he'll likely stay in it as long as he continues to give Pittsburgh these types of starts. Karstens pitched 1 1/3 scoreless innings against Cleveland in a relief appearance last year.
away_pitcher_note: Huff worked five solid innings of two-run ball Sunday before coming undone in his matchup against Stephen Strasburg. The Nationals tagged Huff for four runs in the sixth, sending the 25-year-old left-hander to his seventh loss in eight decisions. He scattered six hits over 5 2/3 innings with three walks and four strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Lincoln has two Major League starts under his belt and is still looking for that first big league win. He has finished six innings in each of his first two appearances, allowing five runs in both. Lincoln showed his last time out that he still has things left to learn. He fell behind too often and didn't always pick the right place to throw his breaking ball. All three of the walks Lincoln issued came back to hurt him. Still, the Pirates love his mentality and competitiveness, and that should carry him through this learning curve.
away_pitcher_note: The Mets tagged Masterson for seven runs on 10 hits over seven innings Tuesday in the Indians' 7-6 loss at Progressive Field. The 25-year-old right-hander yielded just one extra-base hit but was done in by three Tribe errors, one of which came in a five-run fifth for the Mets. Masterson walked two and struck out two in the 104-pitch outing.

home_pitcher_note: A night after Phillies ace Roy Halladay was battered around in the Bronx, the 47-year-old Moyer shut down the Yankees. After giving up nine runs in one-plus inning against Boston -- one of the worst starts of his 22-year career -- he allowed only three hits and two runs in eight innings on Wednesday night. Moyer kept the Yankees hitters off balanced all evening, and his command was exceptional (he has walked only three batters over his past three starts). Aside from two solo home runs by New York, Moyer needed to pitch out of the stretch only twice all night. Not including his nine-run blowup at Fenway, Moyer is 2-1 with a 1.95 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot surrendered a career-high eight runs on 13 hits over 5 2/3 innings in an 8-4 loss to the Mets on Wednesday night at Progressive Field. The rookie right-hander did not walk a batter and struck out three in the 95-pitch outing. He has posted a 2.56 ERA in six road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: After being skipped a start, Kendrick was terrific against New York on Thursday, shutting down the Yankees for just four hits and one run in seven innings. He continued a baffling trend of inconsistency, something likely to continue the rest of the season. In his previous start, he allowed five runs in five innings to Florida, a far lesser offensive opponent than New York. Overall, though, he has won three of his past four decisions and has lowered his ERA from 5.87 at the start of May.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook overcame a lack of sharpness to grind out a seven-inning effort Thursday night, allowing five runs on 11 hits in the Indians' 6-4 loss to the Mets at Progressive Field.
