The 32-year-old right-hander walked two and struck out five in the 109-pitch outing. He has logged seven innings or more in five of his past seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton didn't allow a hit for the first five innings Friday against Minnesota, keeping the ball down and forcing groundball outs by 10 of the first 14 batters he faced. Things unraveled a bit in the sixth and seventh, and he eventually gave up seven hits and three runs. But he did enough to earn his first win since May 15 and rebounded well from a nine-run outing against Boston. He still has a long way to go to get his stats back to where they should be, but he took a step in the right direction.
away_pitcher_note: Following his best start of the season, Carmona looked as sharp as ever through six innings against the Pirates on Friday, when he struck out seven and gave up just two hits, facing more than three batters just once. Things unraveled for the right-hander in the seventh, when he was given a three-run lead. The first four batters he faced reached base, resulting in three runs, but Carmona and his relievers survived in a 4-3 win. It marked the 12th time in 14 starts this season that Carmona had not allowed more than three runs, as he climbed back over .500. The 26-year-old has never faced the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: After finally getting back to the .500 mark on June 9 against the Giants, Harang has dropped two starts in a row. In those two outings, the Reds scored zero runs each time. Harang first allowed five runs in 4 1/3 innings of a 12-0, rain-delayed loss to the Dodgers, and in his last start, he gave up one run in six innings but lost, 1-0, to Seattle. Prior to the two losses, Harang had been 3-0 in five starts. Harang did not pitch against the Indians in the series at Cleveland in June, but in his career, he's 3-2 with a 2.84 ERA against the Reds' Interleague rivals.
away_pitcher_note: With David Huff optioned out to Triple-A Columbus, the Indians will lean on Laffey to join their rotation. The Indians had employed Laffey in the bullpen at the outset of the season, but they sent him back to Columbus last month to get stretched out as a starter again. In the time since, he is 0-1 with a 3.98 ERA in four appearances. He's struggled with his control, striking out nine and walking 15 in 20 1/3 innings. He allowed a run on five hits with seven walks and two strikeouts in 5 2/3 innings in a no-decision against Pawtucket on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Welcome to the Majors, Sam LeCure. Since earning a win in his first start replacing the injured Homer Bailey, LeCure has opposed the St. Louis' Chris Carpenter, San Francisco's Matt Cain, Kansas City's Zack Greinke and Seattle's Felix Hernandez in consecutive starts. He lost all four, including, most recently, a five-run, six-inning outing against the Mariners in which Hernandez tossed a complete game. The Cleveland series finally brings LeCure a break from facing ace-caliber starting pitchers. The Reds scored just five runs combined in LeCure's last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson didn't help himself too much in his last outing, a 5-3 loss at Pittsburgh. The right-hander committed a throwing error in the first inning and gave up two runs after being handed a 2-0 lead in the opening frame. But he recovered to record seven strikeouts while walking just one batter. He gave up five hits over six innings, exiting with a 3-2 lead and his second quality start in his last three outings. The 25-year-old has never faced the Reds. He has pitched in 11 games against the National League (four starts), going 1-2 with a 4.17 ERA.

Talbot recovered from one of his few clunkers of the season with a strong outing against the Phillies on Tuesday. Alas, a lack of offensive backing led him to his sixth loss. He did his part to try to avoid that fate, allowing just two runs on four hits with three walks and three strikeouts in seven innings. This came after he had been roughed up for eight runs over 5 2/3 innings in a loss to the Mets in his previous start. Talbot has been at his best on the road this season. He has a 2.56 ERA in seven road starts, one of the top road ERAs in the AL.

home_pitcher_note: Just when it appeared Jake Westbrook was all the way back to his pre-Tommy John surgery form, he's labored lately. Over his past four starts, Westbrook is 1-1 with a 6.38 ERA, allowing 17 runs on 32 hits in 24 innings pitched. On Wednesday in Philadelphia, he was roughed up for four runs on seven hits with a walk and two strikeouts in five innings of work. At one time, it seemed Westbrook might be a valuable trading chip this summer, but until he shows more consistency, he won't have much value in that department. Westbrook lasted just 3 2/3 innings in a no-decision against the Jays on May 4.
away_pitcher_note: Since allowing seven runs in a disastrous road outing against the Angels on May 25, Romero has been on a roll, going 2-1 with a 1.75 ERA across five starts. On Tuesday, he walked away with a no-decision at home against St. Louis after eight shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona took a step back in his outing against the Phillies on Thursday, allowing seven runs on nine hits with no walks and no strikeouts in four-plus innings. It was his shortest outing of the season and only the second time that he failed to work six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Morrow blanked the Cardinals for eight innings en route to a win Thursday. The righty struck out eight and walked one. Morrow has gone 2-1 with a 1.85 ERA over his past six starts. With Jose Molina catching during that stretch, Morrow has fashioned a 1.32 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Laffey, who began the year in relief, returned to the bigs and returned to starting work Friday in Cincinnati. It didn't go very well. Freshly promoted from Triple-A, he surrendered five runs on five hits with three walks and five strikeouts in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Litsch's results through three starts have been inconsistent since being activated from the disabled list following a year-long recovery from Tommy John surgery. On Friday, the righty allowed six runs on seven hits in four-plus innings in a loss to the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson was sharp through four innings against the Reds on Saturday, but his control fell apart in the fifth. He gave up six runs on six hits with four walks, two strikeouts and two wild pitches in five-plus innings. He also committed his fourth error of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum picked up a win with a solid effort against the Phillies on Saturday, limiting Philadelphia to one run on five hits over six innings. Marcum, who struck out six and walked one, is 2-1 with a 2.00 ERA over his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot collected his team-leading eighth victory on Sunday in Cincinnati, limiting the Reds to one run on three hits over seven innings. He walked three and struck out five. The rookie has yielded two or fewer earned runs in five of his past seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez struggled with his control in his latest start on Sunday against the Pirates, walking four batters over six-plus innings en route to getting a no-decision. Gonzalez faced the Indians on April 25, shutting out Cleveland over seven innings in an 11-0 win.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook tossed six-plus innings of one-run ball against the Blue Jays on Monday night to collect his fifth victory. The 32-year-old right-hander scattered six hits and one walk with four strikeouts in the 105-pitch outing. He is 5-2 with a 4.18 ERA in 10 starts since May 11.
away_pitcher_note: Mortensen will make his season debut with the A's in place of the injured Dallas Braden, who is battling elbow tendinitis. In 15 starts with Triple-A Sacramento this year, the right-hander posted a 10-2 record with a 3.58 ERA and 77 strikeouts, compared to just 31 walks.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona rebounded from his worst start of the season to toss his 12th quality start against the Jays on Tuesday. He went 6 1/3 innings, allowing four runs (three earned) on six hits with three walks and two strikeouts. He's induced 15 groundball double plays this season.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro made an emergency start in place of Dallas Braden (elbow) on Tuesday, allowing an earned run on three hits and six walks over six innings for the win. He is now 2-2 with a 3.41 ERA in his last five starts since filling in for an injured Brett Anderson.

home_pitcher_note: Beltre earned a no-decision in his first career big league start Wednesday against the Angels despite a rocky beginning. After surrending a homer to the first major league batter he faced before giving up two more runs an inning later, Beltre settled down.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey on Wednesday earned his first victory as a starter since Aug. 16, 2009, with a six-inning effort against the Blue Jays. The 25-year-old lefty yielded one run on five hits with two walks and five strikeouts in a 97-pitch outing. He had lost his previous seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson was bothered by his lack of command against the Angels on Thursday -- he walked four batters -- but other than that he was effective. He allowed just two runs on five hits over 5 2/3 innings, but took the loss as the Rangers' offense was held in check by Jered Weaver.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the Blue Jays on Thursday, Masterson gave the Indians a strong 8 1/3-inning performance in which he allowed just a run on eight hits with five strikeouts and didn't walk a batter. It was the kind of outing that restores faith in Masterson's abilities as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis received an extra two days of rest prior to his last start vs. the White Sox, but received no decision after yielding three runs over six-plus frames with three K's. Lewis thought his breaking pitches were much better than his previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot suffered his third loss in four decisions Friday. The Athletics tagged the rookie right-hander for three runs -- two earned -- on five hits and four walks with five strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings. He is 3-4 with a 3.83 ERA over his past eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Davis allowed three home runs in 4 1/3 frames vs. the Twins on Saturday, but he received a no-decision to end a stretch of six consecutive losses. Davis will be making his first start vs. the Indians; he is 3-6 with a 4.44 ERA in nine career appearances at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook on Saturday logged his 11th start of six or more innings this season, drawing a no-decision in the Indians' 5-4 victory over the A's. The 32-year-old right-hander surrendered three runs -- two earned -- on four hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Shields snapped an ugly streak of seven consecutive losses on Sunday when he picked up his seventh win, against the Twins. Shields is 0-3 with a 3.73 ERA in five career starts against the Indians; he is 26-18 with a 3.64 ERA in 68 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Just after being named to his first All-Star team Sunday, Carmona tossed his 13th quality start of the year vs. the A's. The 26-year-old scattered seven hits and three walks in seven innings of three-run ball with three K's. He's 3-3 with a 3.69 ERA in his past seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garza threw only three innings, his third-shortest outing for the Rays, as he battled through a four-run, 49-pitch third against Boston. He said he was making his pitches, and he appeared to have good command, but the Red Sox made him throw 84 pitches in three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey struggled to get ahead and put the Rangers away Monday night. He allowed just a pair of runs (one of which was earned) on five hits with three walks and three strikeouts and left with the lead. But he lasted just 4 1/3 innings and wasn't eligible for the win.

home_pitcher_note: Niemann wasn't at his best Tuesday against the Red Sox, but he still went six innings and gave up just one unearned run for his 13th quality start and seventh win of the year. The right-hander has been quietly dominant and arguably been the Rays' most consistent starter.
away_pitcher_note: It's been an erratic first half for Masterson, whose outings seem to be either dominant or disastrous. His penultimate start of the half was the latter as he was bruised for seven runs on nine hits with three walks and a homer in 5 1/3 innings of a loss to the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander will look to pick up his sixth win of the year as the Tribe's No. 1 starter after the All-Star break. He gave up five runs on eight hits in six innings while taking his fifth loss of the year despite striking out seven batters against Tampa Bay.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer has the tough task of throwing the first game back after the All-Star break. He threw a bullpen on Sunday and said he will play catch on Tuesday and Wednesday to help keep his arm fresh. But even he doesn't know what will happen coming off such a lengthy break.

away_pitcher_note: Stripling excelled as a "bulk pitcher" in his last outing, tossing seven scoreless innings of relief against the Rays. He's slated to resume traditional starting duties this turn, rather than follow an opener. He has a 7.20 ERA in six starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Hentges had to wait an extra day to get his start after expected inclement weather postponed Saturday's game. The righty is hoping to carry the momentum he established last time out, going a career-high five innings with seven strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: After notching a season-high 10 strikeouts in his last start -- a road win over the Yankees -- Matz will face Cleveland for only the third time in his career. In the previous two outings, he is 2-0 with a 0.68 ERA and 16 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: McKenzie was sent down to Triple-A over a week ago, but he has yet to make a start for Columbus. After Zach Plesac's thumb injury, the team needed McKenzie back in the Majors to start on Wednesday, and he'll serve as the 27th man against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Rodón hasn't truly struggled for any stretch this season, but he is 0-2 in his past three starts. Still, with a 2.55 ERA in that span -- and double-digit strikeouts in his past two outings -- the lefty has given the White Sox a chance to win every fifth day.

home_pitcher_note: Quantrill is set to make his first start of the year in Game 2 of the doubleheader against Chicago. Quantrill has worked out of the 'pen all year, so he's not stretched out to give the team too much length, but he has a 2.03 ERA in 17 games.
away_pitcher_note: Lambert, who debuted last season, was called up to make his 2021 season debut, as well as his first start in the Majors. In five starts with Triple-A Charlotte so far, Lambert has a 7.71 ERA, with 23 strikeouts in 11 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bieber finally looked like 2020 Bieber once again in his last outing Thursday. The righty carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning against Detroit and allowed just one run on one hit (solo homer) with 12 strikeouts in seven frames.
away_pitcher_note: Cease is coming off his second double-digit strikeout performance of the season, having fanned 10 Orioles over six innings in a win on Thursday. He has allowed three or fewer runs in nine of 10 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie pitcher will make his second start of the season, following four relief outings for the O's. On Sunday in his first start, he allowed just one run over 4 2/3 innings. He faces Cleveland in his first start at Oriole Park.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians are ready to give Mejía, who's made three scoreless appearances in relief, a chance to earn a spot in the rotation. Mejía was slated to take Eli Morgan's start on Wednesday, but a rainout pushed his first career start back to Friday.

home_pitcher_note: The Orioles' ace has posted a 2.70 ERA against Cleveland, having faced the Indians just twice in 2019. After taking his first loss of the season, Means will face the Tribe for his 12th start of the year. He has allowed two homers across his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians wanted to give Civale an extra day of rest and a rainout on Wednesday made it even easier. Last time out, Civale went six-plus frames in a seven-inning game, allowing four runs on 10 hits with a walk and a strikeout.

home_pitcher_note: López fanned seven batters and allowed just one run in his quality start against the Twins on Monday. Historically, Cleveland hasn't been kind to the righty. His 9.00 ERA against the club is his fourth highest against any team he's faced.
away_pitcher_note: Quantrill will continue to stretch himself out as a starter after getting his first start of the year in Monday's doubleheader against the White Sox. In that outing, he gave up just one run on four hits in 60 pitches across 3 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Martínez will look to put Wednesday’s disastrous start -- 10 runs in two-thirds of an inning -- in Los Angeles behind him. A sign of encouragement is that he'll be rested, coming off an off-day and having tossed just 39 pitches on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Since Bieber's rougher stretch in the middle of May, he has turned in back-to-back seven-inning starts and will look to continue that trend in St. Louis. He has made one career start against the Cardinals, allowing one run in six innings with five K's.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright was the epitome of resilience in his last outing, tossing 50 pitches in his first two frames but bearing down for just 55 across his last five. The veteran’s role gained importance with injuries ravaging the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians are hoping that Mejía will be able to reach up to 65 pitches in his quest to get stretched back out as a starter after spending some time in Cleveland's bullpen. In his first start, he tossed three scoreless frames against the Orioles.

home_pitcher_note: Civale returns to the hill looking to find the form that made him one of the AL's top wins leaders in May. In his previous two outings, Civale allowed a total of eight earned runs, after allowing three over the two starts before that. He carries an 0-1 record with a 6.75 ERA against the Mariners in one career start.
away_pitcher_note: Dunn (right shoulder inflammation) will be activated from the 10-day IL and start in Cleveland. The right-hander missed only one turn through the rotation after first experiencing the issue after his last outing on May 29 against Texas.

home_pitcher_note: McKenzie has already made two starts in the Majors since his demotion to Triple-A, but this time, he'll look to stay with the big league team for good. Two starts ago, he tossed five scoreless innings before fanning 10 batters in his next outing.
away_pitcher_note: Kikuchi avoided a scare against the Angels on Saturday, when he had to exit early after taking a hard-hit grounder to his right knee. But he recovered nicely this week and won’t have to miss his scheduled start.

home_pitcher_note: Bieber takes the mound after tossing six innings of one-run ball on Tuesday against the Cardinals. He is 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA, 24 strikeouts and five runs allowed (four earned) in 20 innings in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gilbert is coming off two strong starts over the division-rival A’s and Angels, in which he gave up a combined three runs on seven hits to the 47 batters he faced in 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Mejía will look to rebound from his first hiccup in the big leagues. Last time out, he allowed four runs on three hits through just two-thirds of an inning with two walks and a strikeout against the Cardinals in his second career start.
away_pitcher_note: Kremer was recalled from Triple-A Norfolk to make his 10th start of the season. He last pitched in the bigs on May 25, tossing four innings and allowing five runs in a loss to the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Although Quantrill worked two innings in relief in St. Louis he'll be right back in the rotation against the Orioles. He didn't allow a run and permitted just one hit working out of the 'pen, but hasn't had the same luck as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Harvey won three of his first six starts but owns an 11.79 ERA in his seven since, six of them losses. The veteran righty was highly critical of his performance after his last start, a blowout loss against the Mets on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Civale will look to build on the momentum he established last time out. After a leadoff single, a hit batter and a walk in the first inning, he was nearly perfect, retiring 22 consecutive batters to end his night after eight scoreless frames.
away_pitcher_note: Akin is making the most of his return to the rotation, pitching to a 2.63 ERA in three starts this season. The rookie southpaw is still looking to improve on his efficiency and pitching deeper into games.

home_pitcher_note: With warm temperatures and no rain in the forecast on Thursday, Morgan will get a chance at a redo after his debut in which he struggled through horrible conditions last time. Against Toronto on May 28, he gave up six runs in 2 2/3 frames.
away_pitcher_note: The Orioles have been encouraged by López, who has struck out 20 and allowed just two homers in his past 21 2/3 innings. The right-hander whiffed eight but allowed five runs in four-plus innings against the Rays last time out on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl earned his fourth loss this year in his previous start, tossing 3 1/3 innings and allowing five earned runs on Saturday. The right-hander will face the Indians for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Mejía will work on short rest after being pulled from his last outing after four innings to preserve his pitch count. The Indians are trying to be creative to get through their lack of starters, and Mejía will likely remain around the 50-60 pitch count.

home_pitcher_note: Crowe fanned a career-high eight batters and allowed two runs on two hits over five innings of work in his last start in Milwaukee on Sunday. He cruised through the Brewers lineup, retiring 15 consecutive batters.
away_pitcher_note: Like J.C. Mejía, Quantrill will work on short rest and will likely stay in the 60-pitch range once again to continue the Indians' plan of piecing together their rotation. Last time out on Tuesday, Quantrill gave up one run in four frames against the Orioles, striking out four.

home_pitcher_note: In two career starts against the Indians, Brubaker owns a 9.00 ERA, both outings coming during the 2020 season. In his last start Brubaker and his slider kept the Nationals at bay, netting nine ground balls and allowing just two runs on Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Hentges will work his way back into a starting role to help fill holes in the rotation. He last worked in relief on Thursday against the Orioles, allowing one hit and striking out three in one inning.

home_pitcher_note: Alzolay is expected to be activated from the 10-day IL after dealing with a blister on his right middle finger. In the seven starts prior to the blister-impacted game on June 7, the righty had 41 strikeouts vs. six walks with a 2.95 ERA in 39 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: With Shane Bieber and Zach Plesac on the IL, Civale is the front man of the Indians' rotation. He will take the mound against the Cubs for the second time in his career. Civale's previous start vs. Chicago saw him allow just two runs over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks tossed six shutout innings in a road win over the Mets on Thursday. The righty has gone 7-0 with a 2.54 ERA in his last seven turns, striking out 35 and walking seven in 46 innings. He has a 4.60 ERA in eight home starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed rookie will make his third career start for the Indians -- his second since his June 15 callup from Triple-A Columbus. In his last start, Morgan fanned five batters and allowed three runs to score over 3 2/3 innings of work.
